commits.pr_title: [Quantization] Online weight-only NVFP4 for dense linear layers
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Add `nvfp4_weight_only`, online NVFP4 weight-only quantization for dense linear layers: FP16/BF16 weights are quantized at load time and run on the existing W4A16 kernel selector, with no NVFP4 checkpoint needed. MoE layers are unchanged. It is selected like the other online methods: the whole model (`--quantization nvfp4_weight_only`), chosen layers (`quantization_config.targets`), or only the drafter (`"quantization": "nvfp4_weight_only"` in `--speculative-config`).

The main use is a BF16 spec-decode drafter on bandwidth-bound GPUs: **+13.1% decode on DGX Spark and +14.1% on RTX PRO 6000 at c=1** for Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 + DFlash2, with acceptance length unchanged.

Also in this PR:
- W4A16 kernel selection takes the activation dtype. The CuTe-DSL and b12x kernels are BF16 only, so FP16 goes to Marlin (before, FP16 could select a BF16-only kernel on SM100/103).
- Quantization uses `scaled_fp4_quant` when available and the torch packer otherwise. Both give identical scales; codes differ only on exact E2M1 ties, with the same error.
- The global scale is reduced over TP, as online FP8 does since #49764, so the quantized weights don't depend on TP size. **This changes `draft_lm_head_quantization: "nvfp4"` numerics at TP > 1.**

Not a duplicate of #49060, which builds Marlin directly instead of using the W4A16 selector and predates the `OnlineLinearBase` requantization contract.

## Results

Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 + DFlash2 (k=7), BF16 drafter vs `nvfp4_weight_only` drafter, SPEED-Bench coding, OSL 8K, nightly f5d93296c8, decode tok/s:

| GPU | c=1 | c=4 | c=8 | GSM8K-256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DGX Spark (GB10) | +13.1% | +22.7%* | +4.9% | 0.965 -> 0.961 |
| RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q | +14.1% | +16.2% | +1.4% | 0.961 -> 0.969 |
| GB300 | +0.1% | -2.4% | +2.9% | 0.969 -> 0.961 |

\*The c=4 arms produced different output lengths; read it as about +15 to 20%. AL is within noise in every row (GB10 c=1: 3.838 -> 3.934). Against an FP8 per-channel drafter, GB10 c=1 is +7.6%.

Whole model, Qwen3-8B: 15.27 -> 5.99 GiB, GSM8K-256 within noise of BF16 on all three GPUs, in BF16 and FP16.

TP=2 on 2x GB200: each rank's global scale equals the TP=1 scale for column- and row-parallel layers, and fails as expected when forced per rank.

Numbers are from b291bae1e0. Later commits are main merges and a docstring fix.

## Testing

On GB10, RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q and GB300, all pass:

```
pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py
pytest tests/model_executor/kernels/test_b12x_linear.py
pytest tests/quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py
pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py -k draft_lm_head_quantization
```

New tests: native vs reference quantization (BF16/FP16, zeros, E2M1 ties), TP shard invariance of the global scale, dtype-aware W4A16 selection.

Not covered: B200, and AL at TP > 1.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the code, tests and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and benchmarks above.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Widen the bound of test_quark_online_rotation_wikitext
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`test_quark_online_rotation_wikitext` fails now and then on MI355 in AMD CI because its bound, 45.9 ± 0.1, sits right at the edge of what the checkpoint actually measures. This moves it to 45.8 ± 0.5, as suggested by the test's author (@mjkvaak-amd), who added it in [#62750](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62750)

Failure: https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15835#01a1e3ce-3341-4b71-be91-e516ceeefbd9 (`assert 45.73561017602654 == 45.9 ± 0.1`). The previous nightly passed and none of the commits between the two touch Quark, MXFP4, the Hadamard rotation or Qwen3.

## Claims

- The test no longer fails depending on the node. Every value measured so far, 45.55 to 46.14, is inside 45.8 ± 0.5.
- It still catches what it is for. A loader that skips the activation rotation produces garbage, far outside this bound.

## Validation

On one MI355X, CI image `rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1e416-bbdc-4da8-98a8-fe70c9c01459` (main @ `9986df412`), GPU 0.

The test's own `lm_eval` call, run 10 times, gives the same value every time:

```text
WIKITEXT_PPL 45.80846984500968   (x10)
```

Changing only `max_num_batched_tokens` to 4096 reproduces the CI value, which fails on main and passes with this change:

```text
PPL_4096 45.74090295802434
```

The test itself with this change:

```text
$ pytest -q quantization/test_quark.py::test_quark_online_rotation_wikitext
1 passed, 17 warnings in 107.07s (0:01:47)
```

The test only runs where MX is supported, so on MI355 in AMD CI, `(MI355 DPX) Quantization`. It is skipped on MI300 and NVIDIA.

## Details

The MXFP4 perplexity of this checkpoint is deterministic on one machine but moves by a few tenths with the execution setup. Measured by the test's author on the Nov 16 nightly:

| Setup | wikitext word perplexity |
|---|---|
| AITER MXFP4 kernel (default) | 45.808 |
| MXFP4 emulation kernel | 45.811 |
| `max_num_batched_tokens=4096` | 45.74 (CI's value) |
| Triton attention backend | 45.55 |
| Eager mode | 46.14 |

The same changes move BF16 Qwen3-0.6B by about 0.002, so the spread comes from MXFP4 numerics and not from a correctness change. #62750 already measured 45.82 against the expected 45.9 when the test was added. The test started running in AMD CI on Nov 14, when `(MI355 DPX) Quantization` was added to the nightly, which is when the edge case showed up.

Not a duplicate: there is no open PR touching this test or its bound.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Add opt-in FlashInfer multimodal encoder autotuning
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
Add opt-in FlashInfer autotuning for multimodal encoders and projectors, which are skipped by the existing language-model warmup.

Enable with:
```
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_mm_encoder_autotune": true}'
```


## Claims
- Tunes encoder kernels using multimodal profiling inputs and FlashInfer’s per-operation token buckets.
- Improves offline image embedding throughput for Nemotron 3.5 Embed NVFP4 by 6.2–7.7% at 448×448 on RTX PRO 6000.
- Remains disabled by default because additional profiling increases startup time.


## Validation
Benchmarked `nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-NVFP4` with `flashinfer_cutlass`, compiled vision encoding, and identical LM tactics between configurations. Measurements used an off/on/on/off sequence on the same GPU, with two runs per configuration and unique images to avoid multimodal cache hits.

| Image size | Batch | Disabled, images/s | Enabled, images/s | Improvement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 448×448 | 1 | 43.59 | 46.97 | 7.7% |
| 448×448 | 4 | 153.74 | 163.35 | 6.3% |
| 448×448 | 8 | 262.12 | 278.48 | 6.2% |
| 1120×1120 | 1 | 32.89 | 33.04 | 0.5% |
| 1120×1120 | 4 | 34.26 | 34.50 | 0.7% |
| 1120×1120 | 8 | 34.05 | 34.69 | 1.9% |

Throughput variation between repeated runs was up to 2.1%; the smaller gains at 1120×1120 should be interpreted accordingly. Fresh encoder tuning increased startup from **16.1 s to 29.2 s** with compilation and LM caches warm. Embedding agreement checks passed.

For a ViDoRe finance_en image-only workload `enable_flashinfer_mm_encoder_autotune` gives about +2.6% throughput: 54.03 req/s against 52.67 for main:
| Config | Start 1 (req/s) | Start 2 (req/s) | Mean (req/s) | vs main |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main (upstream/main 831dd92674) | 52.73 | 52.61 | 52.67 | 1.000 |
| autotune | 54.07 | 53.99 | 54.03 | 1.026 |

- `tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py`: **78 passed**.
- All three cases in `tests/models/multimodal/test_nemotron_embed.py` collected successfully.
- Two-GPU startup validation passed for skipped profiling, fresh tuning, and cached tuning. Vision tactics agreed across ranks, embeddings agreed across runs, and cached startup left cache files unchanged.
- All pre-commit hooks passed.


## Details
Requires FlashInfer autotuning and Model Runner V2. Encoder profiling is skipped with `--skip-mm-profiling`. The pass runs after synchronized warmups, retaining the tuning process group in weights TP mode.

Legacy tuning uses one complete cache file per rank. When encoder tuning is enabled, its cache identity includes the multimodal profiling settings, preventing skipped profiling or different processor settings from falsely satisfying encoder coverage.

The Nemotron regression is wired into B200 CI and checks actual vision GEMM tactics and embedding agreement. This checkpoint does not exercise true encoder data parallelism.

Open-PR searches found no matching encoder-warmup implementation. Related [#63159](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63159) changes bucket handling in the existing LM sweep; it does not add encoder profiling.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Avoid false flushes for shared Full Attention prefixes
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Avoid forcing a pending offload store to complete early when a new Full Attention request shares its prefix blocks. Keep the flush fence for genuine block reuse.

## Claims

- A new request that shares Full Attention prefix blocks no longer adds the prior request's pending store to `jobs_to_flush`, avoiding an unnecessary wait.
- A genuinely reallocated physical block still flushes its prior pending store before reuse.
- The regression coverage uses the real core scheduler and CPU offloading manager, including synchronous and asynchronous scheduling and bounded replay.

## Validation

- Full scheduler suite: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -xq` — 537 passed, 16 warnings before the final group-iteration change.
- Focused scheduler and configuration cases: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py -k 'full_attention_pending_store or fence or cow or reset or preempt or offloading_skips_scratch_group or hisparse_offloads_only_indexer_group' -q` — 34 passed after the final change.
- `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` on the two changed Python files — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- The shared-prefix scenario was reproduced with the real core scheduler before the fix: the shared block was touched rather than allocated, but A's pending job appeared in `jobs_to_flush`. With the fix, the store completes and the CPU key is a hit. The different-content reuse control still flushes A's pending job.
- Applied the PR #66959 diff during compatibility validation before the review refactor; the relevant scheduler tests passed.
- GPU smoke: `LLM` with dummy OPT-125M weights, OffloadingConnector, TRITON_ATTN, and two requests with a shared 64-token prefix completed; the second request reported 64 cached tokens. This smoke test does not reproduce a pending store or measure accuracy.
- No model evaluation applies because this change does not alter model computation or outputs.

## Details

A search of open offloading and prefix-fence PRs found no other PR addressing this Full Attention shared-prefix case.

The scheduler output gives a new or resumed request its complete block table. For Full Attention, the table can include leading blocks found in the GPU prefix cache. Core touches those blocks and increments their reference counts; it does not allocate them again. The offloading scheduler previously treated every ID in that table as newly allocated and used the physical ID to find pending stores to flush.

The fix excludes the locally computed Full Attention prefix from the allocation candidates, using the existing block table and request state. For bounded replay, a retained local hit can extend past the replay execution boundary; when core discards a short hit, the computed-token boundary still limits the prefix excluded. Both allocation tracking paths examine all block groups. No public API or configuration is changed.

`jobs_to_flush` submits a deferred store if necessary and waits for its completion. A false fence therefore serializes an existing store with the new request; it does not itself create a duplicate store job or discard the pending one. Store deduplication is based on offload keys in the manager, independently of GPU block sharing.

HiSparse host and GPU block pools can reuse the same numeric ID. The existing allocation callback can therefore trigger an unnecessary fence on a host allocation; examining all groups in scheduler output extends that behavior to allocations for running requests. Pool-aware fence tracking is a follow-up.

This is separate from PR #66959, which fixes stale sliding-window tables. This PR does not depend on #66959; it targets Full Attention shared-prefix allocation tracking and was checked against that PR's diff for compatibility.

commits.pr_title: [KV Offload] Explain EFAULT from a full /dev/shm in _madvise_populate_write
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

When `/dev/shm` runs out while the CPU KV offload shared region is pre-faulted, `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` fails with `OSError: [Errno 14] Bad address`, which does not point at `/dev/shm`. With data parallelism this happens with offload sizes that fit one engine at a time but not all of them together. Each region's creator checks `/dev/shm` free space and then calls `ftruncate`, which reserves nothing on tmpfs, so engines starting together all pass the check. Pages are only claimed when `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` faults them in, and on a full tmpfs `madvise` reports that as `EFAULT`. On main (`642c18d6`), 8× RTX 4090, Qwen3-8B, `--data-parallel-size 8 --kv-offloading-size 32` and a 251.9 GiB `/dev/shm`: all 8 engines loaded the model, then 6 failed with `Bad address` and the server exited.

This PR makes the existing `_madvise_populate_write` helper turn that `EFAULT` into an error that names `/dev/shm`. Nothing else changes.

## Claims

- In `_madvise_populate_write`, an `OSError` with `errno.EFAULT` is re-raised as a new `OSError(errno.EFAULT, …)`, chained from the original. From the 64 MiB reproduction below:
  *"Pre-faulting the mapping failed with EFAULT, most likely because the memory backing it ran out. If it is in /dev/shm (now 0.00 GiB free of 0.06 GiB), note that /dev/shm is shared by every process that uses it, including other data-parallel engines; increase its capacity or reduce the host buffer size"*
- The free/total figures come from `shutil.disk_usage("/dev/shm")`; if that call fails, they are left out and the error is still raised.
- `EINVAL` (which selects the per-page fallback) and every other errno are re-raised unchanged.
- The probe and every native population path (per worker, whole region, sharded) go through this helper, so all of them get the message. HiSparse's pool uses the same region class, so it is covered too.

## Validation

Run on the nightly wheel of main `199c2e4b` with this PR's `shared_offload_region.py` applied, CPU only. `shared_offload_region.py`, its test file, `shm_broadcast.py`, `host_buffer.py` and `test_host_buffer.py` are identical between `199c2e4b` and `3ec1b24a`, the commit merged into this branch.

- `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py`: 70 passed. On unpatched main, 69 passed and the new test fails. The new test, `test_madvise_efault_raises_shm_diagnostic`, makes `madvise` raise `EFAULT` and checks the errno, that the message names `/dev/shm` and that `__cause__` is the original error; it then checks that `EINVAL` passes through as the same exception object.
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_host_buffer.py`: 8 passed, 1 skipped, with and without this PR.
- `host_buffer.py`'s handler, with `EFAULT` injected at `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` in `alloc_host_buffer`'s HugeTLB path (`MAP_HUGETLB` dropped because the test box reserves no HugeTLB pages; the code path is otherwise unchanged): it still fires and wraps the new text (`RuntimeError: Cannot populate … HugeTLB pages: [Errno 14] Pre-faulting the mapping failed with EFAULT, … The container's memory or hugetlb limit is too small.`). On main, the same handler wraps `[Errno 14] Bad address`.
- A real `EFAULT`: inside `unshare -m` with a 64 MiB tmpfs on `/dev/shm`, pre-faulting a 128 MiB file mapping through the helper. With this PR the error is the message above, with the original `OSError` (errno 14) as `__cause__`. On main it is a bare `OSError: [Errno 14] Bad address`.
- vLLM's pre-commit hook commands on both changed files: ruff check and format, typos, mypy through `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py` (Python 3.11 to 3.13), SPDX, lazy and forbidden imports, `check_torch_cuda`, `check_boolean_context_manager`, config validation, docstring style, trust-remote-code, test tethering: all pass.
- Not re-run end to end for this revision: the change only translates the error, and the real `EFAULT` above goes through the same helper that every population path calls.

## Details

**Why it stays an `OSError`.** `alloc_host_buffer` in `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/host_buffer.py` (#60130) also calls this helper, on anonymous (optionally HugeTLB) memory that is not in `/dev/shm`, and wraps its populate call in `except OSError` to explain a HugeTLB pool or container-limit shortfall. Raising a different type would skip that handler. That is also why the message hedges ("most likely", "if it is in /dev/shm") instead of asserting that `/dev/shm` is full.

**Limitations.**
- Under a memory-cgroup limit, the failure is `ENOMEM` or the OOM killer, not `EFAULT`, so this message does not appear.
- On kernels older than 5.14 there is no `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE`; the per-page fallback hits a `SIGBUS`, which this does not translate.
- `vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/cpu/ec_shared_region.py` has its own copy of the helper and still reports a bare `EFAULT`. It is left out to keep this PR to the KV offload region; I can send the same change there separately.

**AI assistance.** Claude Opus 5.5 assisted with the code, the test and this description. I reviewed every changed line and the results, and can answer for it; the non-merge commits carry an `Assisted-by:` trailer.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Gemma4/Gemma3n: allocate the PLE cache on the input device
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The per-layer-embedding (PLE) cache `per_layer_embeddings` in `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration`, `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` and `Gemma3nForConditionalGeneration` is a plain attribute, so it stays behind when the model is moved with `.to(device)` or built on the meta device. The first forward then fails with `Expected all tensors to be on the same device`.

This reallocates the cache on the inputs' device on first use. It stays a plain attribute, so the IPC weight cache never exports it.

## Details

- Each class gets a `_per_layer_embeddings_on(device)` helper, used by both the write in `embed_input_ids` and the read in `forward`. `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` inherits both, so it needs no change.
- On the default load path the devices already match, so nothing is reallocated and the address CUDA graphs rely on is unchanged.

## Validation

New `test_ple_cache_follows_inputs_device` (Gemma-4 and Gemma-3n) in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4.py`: a cache starting on `meta` reaches the backbone on the inputs' device, zeroed, and later steps reuse the same storage.

```
$ pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4.py -k ple_cache
# this PR
2 passed, 43 deselected
# main (827f2ccfaf)
FAILED ...::test_ple_cache_follows_inputs_device[Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration] - AssertionError: assert 'meta' == 'cpu'
FAILED ...::test_ple_cache_follows_inputs_device[Gemma3nForConditionalGeneration] - AssertionError: assert 'meta' == 'cpu'
```

commits.pr_title: [Model Loader] Direct reload of online-quantized modules
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

Direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336) now supports online quantization on a BF16 checkpoint. Part of #54477 (F4).

This revision replaces the earlier layerwise-staging approach: no module is staged on meta, buffered, or re-quantized at `finish`. Online quantization in direct mode is a pre-quantized checkpoint method whose loaders quantize on arrival. The diff against main is 10 files: about +200/-10 of source, plus tests and docs.

## Problem

`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct` refuses online quantization. Online methods create BF16 parameters on the meta device and quantize them in post-load processing. A direct reload writes in place into the kernel tensors, and those cannot hold BF16, so there is nothing to load the update into.

## Design

The only place a high-precision tensor can become a quantized one is the place it arrives: the weight loader.

- **Only in direct mode.** With `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct` (and not for requantization), `OnlineQuantizationConfig.get_quant_method` returns the method of the matching pre-quantized checkpoint for a convertible scheme. Every other mode keeps the online classes, so behavior there is unchanged from main.
- **Online scheme = checkpoint method + quantize-on-load.**
  - `quantize_on_load` wraps the weight loaders once and permanently. Each arriving tensor is quantized, then its values and scales are written through the original loaders.
  - Cold start and direct reload therefore load and post-process exactly like that checkpoint. There is no layerwise staging.
  - The full unsharded tensor is quantized before the original loader TP-splits it, as a checkpoint would be.
- **Scheme mapping** (linear / MoE):
  - `fp8_per_tensor` → `Fp8LinearMethod` / `Fp8MoEMethod`
  - `fp8_per_block` → the same, with 128×128 blocks
  - `fp8_per_channel` → `ModelOptLinearMethod` (PcPt) / `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoEMethod`
  - `mxfp8` → `ModelOptLinearMethod` / `CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod`
  - `mxfp4` MoE → `Mxfp4MoEMethod`
  - `nvfp4_per_token` MoE → `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE` with the per-token override
- **NVFP4 pairing (the only special case).** w1 and w3 of an expert share one global scale. One w13 loader holds the first of the pair until the other comes, then quantizes both with the shared amax.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `online/loading.py` (new) | `quantize_on_load`, the scheme → checkpoint-method mapping, NVFP4 w1/w3 pairing |
| `online/base.py` | In direct mode, return the checkpoint method, or raise for a scheme that has none |
| `base_config.py` | In direct mode, raise for requantization |
| `config/vllm.py` | Drop the blanket online-quantization refusal |
| `gpt_oss.py` | Refuse quantize-on-load layers: gpt-oss writes BF16 experts outside their loaders |
| `tests/quantization/test_online_loading.py` (new) | NVFP4 pairing (either order, a repeated half, other ranks' experts, a lone half), contiguous quantizer input |
| `test_direct_reload.py` | A quantize-on-load case in the reload-equals-cold-start suite |
| `docs/training/layerwise.md`, `docs/features/quantization/online.md` | Usage, supported schemes, refusals, NVFP4 delivery rule |

**NVFP4 pairing details.** The held half is a copy, because a weight-transfer receive buffer is reused. A packed NCCL transfer runs loads on alternating streams, so the pairing load waits on an event recorded after the copy and records its stream on the held tensor. A repeated half replaces the held one. Another rank's expert returns `False` before anything is held. If a half is still held at post-load processing, the update fails.

## Refused in direct mode

These raise at model construction, when the quant method is chosen:

- Online schemes without a quantize-on-load checkpoint method:
  - `mxfp4` linear, including `mxfp4_hadamard32`
  - any `hadamard_size`
  - `int8` / experts_int8
  - `lut_b`
  - lm_head targets
- An activation override that differs from the scheme default.
- Requantization of a pre-quantized checkpoint.
- gpt-oss with online quantization.
- `fp8_per_block` linear layers whose TP shards are not multiples of 128. `Fp8LinearMethod` validates the block shape, whereas main's online method pads.
- The NCCL load plan (`check_plannable`): tracing would quantize the traced tensors.
- The existing refusals in direct reload (`_check_supported_modules`, `VllmConfig._verify_direct_reload_compat`) are unchanged and stay as the backstop: Muse Spark FP8 MoE, fused shared experts, torchao, LoRA, weight offloading, Humming.

## Known differences and risks (direct mode only)

- **fp8_per_tensor numerics.** Each shard of a merged layer (q/k/v, w1/w3) gets its own scale. Post-load processing then requantizes to the max scale, exactly as for an FP8 checkpoint. Main's online path quantizes the merged BF16 weight once. The final scales are equal; values may differ by one extra FP8 rounding.
- **fp8_per_channel and nvfp4_per_token** quantize with the online path's own functions, so their values and scales match main.
- **Kernel selection follows the checkpoint method:**
  - fp8 MoE: `Fp8MoEMethod` disallows vLLM CUTLASS.
  - mxfp4 MoE: `select_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_moe_backend` prefers MXFP8, then BF16, activations (W4A8 / W4A16). Main's online method runs `kMxfp4Dynamic` (W4A4).
  - per-channel linear: ModelOpt's `select_linear_kernel`, without the online PTPC refusal of weight-only Marlin/Humming kernels.
- Experts loaded as one 3-D tensor (Llama 4 fused BF16 checkpoints) fail loudly in the 2-D quantizers. mxfp8 is the exception and loads.
- To be measured: GSM8K and decode tok/s against main's online cold start on flagship MoE models.

## Tests

In progress: unit tests (`test_direct_reload.py`, `test_online.py`), plus end-to-end L2 sleep → weight update → wake runs for every converted scheme on Qwen3-30B-A3B and flagship BF16 MoE models. Each run compares GSM8K and tensor digests with a fresh start, and decode throughput with main's online cold start. Results will be posted here.

commits.pr_title: [RL][Model Loader] Load FP8 indexer wk and MLA projections independently, as FP8 or BF16, in any scale layout
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Load the FP8 weights of layers that vLLM runs in BF16 (the sparse-attention indexer's `wk`, GLM5-next's MLA projections) from their own checkpoint parameters, so a weight and its scale can arrive in different `load_weights` calls, and accept the weight whole in BF16 as most RL trainers send it. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477). Supersedes #64717.

Builds on aoshen02's restructuring of every indexer (aoshen02/vllm#243): `wk` and `weights_proj` are ordinary layers loaded under their own names, and `wk_weights_proj` (the fused BF16 GEMM) is a derived weight refilled in place after each load. No pending dicts, no merged-name mappings. This PR adds the input formats real trainers and checkpoints use on top of that structure.

## Files

- `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/dequant_linear.py` (new): `DequantLinearMethod`, a layer with an FP8 checkpoint weight that runs in BF16. `wrap(layer)` converts a layer built by any quant config whose weight is FP8 (not online-quantized); `bf16_linear(build, quant_config)` builds a layer that way or, for another quantized format, unquantized. Also the loader that keeps a weight in the dtype it is sent in (FP8 or BF16) and the post-load dequantization.
- `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/quant_utils.py`: `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights` returns a `DequantLinearMethod` layer's weight as is (it is BF16 after loading).
- `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py`: `init_indexer_wk_weights_proj` builds `wk` (with `bf16_linear`) and `weights_proj` as checkpoint layers whose weights are views of the fused BF16 `wk_weights_proj`; `fuse_indexer_wk_weights_proj` refills it in place after each load.
- `vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/*`, `vllm/models/hy_v4/*`, `vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_mtp.py`: use those two functions; drop the FP8 `wk` pairing and dequantization in `load_weights`.
- `vllm/models/glm5next/common/attention.py`: the indexer as above; the MLA projections are built with the checkpoint's quant config through `bf16_linear`.
- `vllm/models/glm5next/common/model.py`, `mtp.py`: drop the pending-dict FP8 pairing; `_mla_proj_checkpoint_tensor` adapts each tensor on its own (Quark scale name, NoPE `kv_a` padding of weight and block scale); match `modules_to_not_convert` by suffix.
- `vllm/models/dots3_note/nvidia/model.py`: its FP8 indexer `weights_proj` is wrapped with `DequantLinearMethod.wrap` instead of being dequantized in `load_weights`.
- `tests/quantization/test_fp8_dequant.py` (new, replaces `test_deepseek_v32_weight_loading.py` and the GLM5-next part of `test_quark.py`); `.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml` runs it.
- `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py` is unchanged.

## Claims

- **BF16 `wk` (and BF16 MLA projections) from a trainer load correctly.** On #243 a BF16 tensor is cast into the FP8 parameter and dequantized with the previous update's scale: wrong values, no error. Here the weight is kept in the dtype it is sent in, and the scale is not needed for that update. FP8 ↔ BF16 can alternate between updates, in cold start, direct reload and layerwise reload, at the cold-start addresses.
- **Every `wk` scale layout found in published checkpoints dequantizes exactly:** 128×128 blocks (official DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x FP8), per-channel `[128]` (Quark, amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8), MX 1×32 E8M0 (ModelOpt MXFP8), and E8M0 block scales under `Fp8Config`. On #243 the Quark per-channel `wk` fails at cold start (`AssertionError` in `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights`' identity-GEMM fallback, `ReplicatedLinear` has no `input_size_per_partition`).
- Weight and scale load independently, in either order and in different calls.
- **The fused indexer weight is filled on every path:** under a KV-cache quant method on the MLA layer (ModelOpt, e.g. nvidia/GLM-5.3-NVFP4, where #243 leaves it uninitialized), and after an in-place reload of the runtime weights (`refresh_derived_weights`). `wk` stays exact BF16 under online quantization, as on main.
- MiMo-V2's split loading is out of scope (its fused qkv is a separate problem).

## Validation

All on GB200, nightly wheel e336407a3d (= this branch's merge-base) with each arm's Python files overlaid. "Main" = e336407a3d, "#243" = cc96c04bea (aoshen02's head), "this PR" = c7b8cd58ce for the GPU runs below; 5d69c2f057 (review fixes) and 1bbe0fd507 (no extra memory) were checked with the unit tests, the memory table, the GLM-5.3-Flash reload and the DeepSeek-V3.2-NVFP4 check below.

**Cold-start A/B** (same node(s), arms back to back; GSM8K 5-shot greedy, 1319 questions; throughput `vllm bench serve` random 1024/256, concurrency 64; a worker-extension probe counts quant-method classes per rank).

| Model (GB200, TP) | GSM8K main → this PR | Other | Output tok/s | KV cache | Path check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 + MTP (TP4) | 0.9166 → 0.9219 | acceptance length 1.952 → 1.952 | 3217 → 3279 | 2.106M → 2.090M | `DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER`; 44 `Fp8DequantLinearMethod` (MLA) per rank on this PR, 0 on main |
| GLM-5.3 FP8 + MTP (2 nodes, TP8; block-FP8 `wk`) | 0.9022 → 0.9030 | acceptance length 1.944 → 1.943 | 1995 → 1952 | 1.129M → 1.129M | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`; 21 `Fp8DequantLinearMethod` (`wk`) per rank on this PR, 0 on main |

At c7b8cd58ce / 5d69c2f057 GLM-5.3-Flash loaded 0.05 GiB more weights per rank (79.12 → 79.17 GiB: separate `wk` / `weights_proj` next to the fused copy, as in #243, and the retired scales), hence 0.75% less KV cache. Since 1bbe0fd507 the weights take exactly main's memory (see **Memory** below). Jobs 46205, 46210.

"fp8": the checkpoint as is. "bf16": the FP8 MLA projections (`q_a_proj`, `kv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `q_b_proj`, `o_proj`) sent dequantized to BF16 by the trainer, without scales. "Differing" = device tensors (registered and reachable from module attributes, incl. the fused `wk_weights_proj.weight`) whose digest differs from the fresh start.

Cold-start GSM8K of this PR on the same model is 0.9219 (A/B above; #64717 measured 0.9212 after direct and layerwise reloads). 48 MLA weights per update went as BF16 in the bf16 rows. Jobs 46330 (c7b8cd58ce), 46448 (5d69c2f057) and 46585 (1bbe0fd507) and 46688 (ebf9a34202) and 46736 (ac6483411c), the last four with the cold-start GSM8K in the same run; no tensor moved in any of them. At 1bbe0fd507 the GLM-5.3 slice (block-FP8 `wk`, FP8 then BF16 updates) again differs from fresh only in the 2 runtime buffers (jobs 46587, 46690 at ebf9a34202) (earlier TP2 attempts with the trainer on GPU 2, jobs 46206/46272/46301/46305/46313, could not start the server: 155.5 GiB of weights per rank leaves too little memory for CUDA graphs and the KV cache on this wheel).

**Direct reload, reduced slices** (first 2 decoder layers + embeddings/head, TP1; 3 updates per variant; "bf16" sends `wk` dequantized to BF16 without its scale). The two tensors that differ in every row are `index_group.physical_topk_indices`, runtime state written by the generations between snapshots.

| | this PR | ok | 2 / same | 2 / same |

On this PR the BF16 rows match the fresh start bit for bit, so the cold-start dequantization equals the trainer's reference dequantization. Jobs 46209, 46208, 46300.

**Fused weight under ModelOpt NVFP4** (nvidia/DeepSeek-V3.2-NVFP4, TP4, job 46436): ModelOpt puts a KV-cache quant method on every MLA layer, so `finalize_model_weights` skips the indexer under it. (Prompts shorter than `index_topk` = 2048 hide it, since top-k then keeps every token.)

**Unit tests** (`tests/quantization/test_fp8_dequant.py`, GPU): 42 passed at a94cae6ce (verda GB300, job 31857, nightly 60bd6dd2ed with this branch's Python files overlaid; it adds per-tensor MLA scales and `test_wrap_skips_online_quantized_layer`), and 41 passed in `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_direct_reload.py` and `test_reload_lifecycle.py` (same job). The model runs above predate a94cae6ce, which moves the method out of `fp8.py` without changing what the block-FP8 checkpoints load (class names in the tables are the old `Fp8DequantLinearMethod`). 37 passed at ac6483411c (job 46734) and at ebf9a34202 after the re-review folded the aliasing checks into the cold-start and reload tests (job 46687). 47 passed at 1bbe0fd507 (job 46580; adds `test_indexer_parts_live_in_fused_weight[mode × layout]`: `wk` / `weights_proj` are views of the fused weight after cold start and FP8 / BF16 reloads, and filling it copies nothing; `test_mla_dequantizes_in_loaded_storage[mode]`). 35 passed at 5d69c2f057 (job 46416); the 3 tests added with it fail at c7b8cd58ce (same job). 32 passed at c7b8cd58ce (job 46175); with that test file on #243's head, 20 fail: every BF16 update (direct and layerwise, block / block E8M0 / per-channel / MXFP8 `wk`, cold start in FP8 or BF16), the MLA BF16 update, and the per-channel cold start.
- `test_indexer_fused_weight[layout × scales_first]`: BF16, block, block E8M0 (`Fp8Config` with `is_scale_e8m0`), Quark per-channel and ModelOpt MXFP8 `wk`, scale before or after the weight in separate calls; the fused weight equals the exact dequantization.
- `test_indexer_reload_fp8_or_bf16[mode × cold × layout]`: direct and layerwise reload, updates alternating FP8 (scale before or after the weight) and BF16; fused weight exact, all addresses kept.
- `test_mla_cold_start_separate_calls[scheme × scales_first]`, `test_mla_reload_equals_cold_start[scheme × mode]`: GLM5-next-like fused (unequal shards, partial last block) and row-parallel projections built with `Fp8Config` and wrapped, block or per-tensor (one scale per shard) scales, FP8 → BF16 → FP8 updates.
- `test_wrap_skips_online_quantized_layer`: a layer with `quantizes_on_load` (#65802) is not wrapped.
- `test_indexer_wk_stays_bf16_under_online_quantization`, `test_layerwise_metadata_does_not_keep_layers_alive`, `test_indexer_fuse_allocates_weight_left_on_meta`.

MXFP8 `wk` (ModelOpt) is covered by unit tests only; see Details for why no in-scope MXFP8 checkpoint was run.

## Details

**What RL trainers send for `wk`** (from reading each repo's weight-sync code):

| Framework | `wk` sent as | `weights_proj` |
|---|---|---|
| SkyRL (GLM-5 spec, `weight_sync/fp8/models/glm5.py`) | BF16 | BF16 |
| NeMo-RL default (quantizes in the vLLM worker per what vLLM built) | BF16 | BF16 |
| ROLL (`roll/third_party/vllm/fp8.py`), prime-rl (online FP8), vLLM `examples/rl/rlhf_http_nccl.py` | BF16 | BF16 |
| slime (`quantizer_fp8.py`, SGLang rollout) | FP8 + block `weight_scale_inv` | BF16 |
| verl native FP8 | FP8 + scale | — |

No trainer mixes FP8 and BF16 rows inside one tensor, so a tensor is accepted whole in one format.

**How published checkpoints store `wk`** (safetensors headers of 465 repos):

| Layout | Examples |
|---|---|
| Block FP8 128×128, F32 `weight_scale_inv` | deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 (+Exp, Speciale), zai-org/GLM-5.x-FP8, zai-org/GLM-5.3 |
| BF16 | zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash (even the FP8 repo), most NVFP4/MXFP4 quantizations |
| MXFP8 1×32, U8 E8M0 `weight_scale` | local-inference-lab/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4-*, nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local (MTP layer), zianglih/DeepSeek-V3.2-MXFP8 |
| Per-channel `weight_scale` `[128]` | amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 (F32), amd/DeepSeek-V3.2-mtp-ptpc (BF16) |
| Per-tensor | none |

**Design.**
- `DequantLinearMethod` (`quantization/dequant_linear.py`, not tied to `Fp8Config`) wraps the checkpoint's own linear method instead of subclassing `Fp8LinearMethod`. That method's `create_weights` makes the checkpoint parameters (names, shapes, loaders), so each loads on its own. `wrap(layer)` is the only entry point: the indexer's `wk`, GLM5-next's MLA projections and dots3's `weights_proj` are built with the checkpoint's quant config (so its ignored layers apply as for any layer) and wrapped when their weight is FP8, whatever the config: `Fp8Config`, Quark, ModelOpt MXFP8. `bf16_linear` rebuilds a layer of another quantized format unquantized (e.g. online quantization), as these layers are BF16 on main.
- `wrap` skips a layer that quantizes the BF16 tensors it loads (`quantizes_on_load`, online quantization in direct reload, #65802): viewing its FP8 weight in the sent dtype would store unscaled values.
- The weight's loader views the parameter in the dtype the tensor is sent in (FP8, or the model dtype) before the normal loader runs. After a cold start the parameter's storage is BF16-sized, so the view fits and direct reload keeps the address; at a cold start from an FP8 checkpoint the first BF16 load allocates.
- No extra memory. `wk` and `weights_proj` have no storage of their own: `weights_proj.weight` is a view of the fused weight's rows after `wk`'s, and `wk.weight` is a view of the start of the fused storage in the dtype it loads (FP8 or BF16). An FP8 weight (indexer `wk` or a GLM5-next MLA projection) is allocated BF16-sized and dequantized through a temporary back into that storage, so `wk` lands in its fused rows in every load mode; filling the fused weight then copies nothing. A part in its own storage (dots3's separately built `weights_proj`, or parameters handed over by the weight cache IPC loader, for which the fill also allocates the fused weight) is copied into the fused rows. Direct reload views `wk` back to FP8 on the same storage at begin.
- The BF16-accepting loader is a method bound to the layer, so layerwise reload's metadata (`sanitize_layer_refs`) does not keep layers alive. `wk` is built plain BF16 when the checkpoint does not store it in FP8.
- GLM5-next matches `Fp8Config`'s `modules_to_not_convert` by suffix (as `bailing_moe_v3`): GLM-5.3-Flash lists its BF16 modules under text-model names (`model.layers.N…`), which sit under `language_model.` in the multimodal model, so the exact match never applied and the BF16 indexer `wk` was built as an FP8 layer with a scale the checkpoint lacks. It is now built BF16: the probe counts 33 `Fp8DequantLinearMethod` (now `DequantLinearMethod`) per rank instead of 44 and 11 more `UnquantizedLinearMethod` (cold-start A/B against ebf9a34202, job 46735: GSM8K 0.9189 → 0.9196, KV cache 2.106M both).
- `DeepseekV32Attention` runs its indexer's post-load hook itself: `finalize_model_weights` does not descend into a layer that has a quant method, and ModelOpt gives every MLA layer a KV-cache method. Indexers also expose that hook as `refresh_derived_weights`.
- Post-load processing dequantizes an FP8 weight with whatever scale was loaded (`weight_scale_inv` or `weight_scale`; U8 read as E8M0; 1-D per channel, or per tensor with one scale per merged shard (`logical_widths`); group shape from `weight_block_size` or from the scale's shape) in one fp32 pass, and retires every scale. A BF16 weight is left as is. This replaces the block-only loop of #243 and the generic identity-GEMM fallback for these layers. `scaled_dequantize` is not used: GLM5-next's `fused_qkv_a_proj` ends in a partial block (e.g. 2048 + 576 rows), which its divisibility asserts reject. The temporaries (an fp32 copy and the expanded scale, about 8 bytes per weight element) live only while one layer is processed.

**Trade-offs and limits.**
- **Deferred to a follow-up (AMD Quark):** `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` stores the GLM5-next MLA projections as block FP8 with Quark's `weight_scale`. Main dequantized them in `load_weights` (#56176). Here they are now built with the checkpoint's config (Quark per-block FP8) and wrapped, as `wk` is, but `_mla_proj_checkpoint_tensor` pads the NoPE `kv_a` block scale only under the `weight_scale_inv` name, so the `kv_a` scale shard still fails its shape check at load. Not run end to end; the follow-up pads `weight_scale` too and validates that checkpoint.
- A fused parameter (GLM5-next `fused_qkv_a_proj`) must receive all its shards in one format within an update.
- When `wk` or an MLA projection arrives in BF16 its scale keeps the previous value; it is retired and unused, but still counts toward the layer's size. Layerwise reload therefore buffers that layer until finish, and the sharded RDT engine refuses it. Direct reload over NCCL/IPC is unaffected. This only concerns a trainer sending BF16 for a layer the checkpoint stores in FP8 (no longer GLM-5.3-Flash's `wk`, which is BF16 in the checkpoint and now built BF16). Deferred with the item above.
- No in-scope checkpoint with an MXFP8 `wk` runs end to end: the ModelOpt `MIXED_PRECISION` GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoints (local-inference-lab/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4-Spark, nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local MTP layer) also store `weights_proj`, `wq_b` and the MLA projections in MXFP8 / FP8 blocks, while GLM5-next builds those layers unquantized (main and #243 alike) and keeps building `wk` from `Fp8Config` only. Supporting them is a separate change; the MXFP8 dequantization itself is unit-tested here.
- `zianglih/DeepSeek-V3.2-MXFP8` names its MX scale `weight_scale_inv`, which ModelOpt MXFP8's parameter (`weight_scale`) does not match; untested, 23 downloads.
- MiMo-V2: out of scope.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Always use the unfolded layer-0 mHC entry on gfx942
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On gfx942 the DeepSeek-V4.1 layer-0 attention entry seam projects the 2-D embedding with the folded `hc_attn_fn_broadcast` unless layer 0 runs as a whole mono layer. No AITER kernel takes that form and TileLang mHC is off on gfx942, so the seam runs `MHCPreDelayedOp.forward_native`, a chain of small eager kernels on every step. #60731 already switches this seam to the unfolded form (the expanded residual projected with `hc_attn_fn`, served by `mhc_pre_delayed_aiter`) for a whole mono layer 0. This PR uses the unfolded form whenever the seam runs on gfx942: without `--monokernel`, and for a layer 0 that takes only the mono FFN launch, whose attention runs this stock seam the same way. `MonoDecodeLayer.unfolded_entry` has no other user and is removed.

## Claims

- gfx942: the layer-0 entry seam drops from 336.8 µs to 13.8 µs at 24 tokens (single GPU, HIP graph replay, real layer-0 weights).
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4× MI300X, TP4, InferenceX AgentX, no `--monokernel`: E2E-normalized interactivity P50 +3.5% at concurrency 8 (mean of three same-node pairs, +2.7% to +4.1%); no regression at concurrency 32 (one pair). GSM8K is unchanged and the real-acceptance gate passes in all runs (acceptance length 3.495 mean over 3 runs vs 3.519 over 2 without it, within run-to-run spread).
- No change on gfx950, for a whole mono layer 0 (it already took the unfolded form), or for the DSpark draft (its first layer takes a 3-D stream). With `--monokernel`, a layer 0 that takes only the mono FFN launch now also takes the unfolded form; that case was not run end to end, because `--monokernel` does not start on MI300X here (`Available KV cache memory: -5.33 GiB`).

## Why this is not a duplicate

No open or merged PR makes the gfx942 entry seam unfolded outside a whole mono layer.

- #61311 (open, changes requested) rewrites the same line as `self.unfolded_entry`, which only the specialized decode sets, so it keeps the folded seam here. With this change the entry seam no longer needs that attribute; whichever PR merges second drops it or sets it to `on_gfx942()`.
- #65992 (merged) runs the fused gfx950 seams as Mega-MHC and does not touch this gate; the new test's hand-built decoder sets `hc_attn_fn_packed = hc_ffn_fn_packed = None`, as `test_deepseek_v41_rocm_decoder_overlap_matches_serial` does.
- #60153 (open) keeps layer 0 (`x`) on `pre_delayed` in its gfx942 seam dispatch. Its `forward` reads `self.mhc_seam`, so whichever PR merges second sets `decoder.mhc_seam = None` in the new test. #65461 (merged) changes only the mono path.

## Validation

**Unit test** (`tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py::test_deepseek_v41_rocm_first_layer_unfolded_entry`) runs a layer-0 decoder and records its entry seam: gfx942 must project with `hc_attn_fn` and other platforms with `hc_attn_fn_broadcast`, the layer input must be bitwise equal across the two forms, and the three mixes must agree within `atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-3`. That is the tolerance this file uses for AITER and for TileLang against the reference; on gfx950 the folded form runs TileLang, so the test compares two backends there. `on_gfx942` is patched so both forms run on any ROCm GPU with AITER mHC. Like `test_deepseek_v41_rocm_decoder_overlap_matches_serial`, it builds the decoder by hand with stand-in attention and FFN, since only the entry seam is under test and a real layer needs checkpoint weights and a TP group. In CI this file runs in `:nvidia: (B200) mHC Kernels`, where the test is skipped, and in its AMD mirror `:amd: (MI355) mHC Kernels`; no gfx942 job runs it, so the MI300X results below are from a local run of this branch on main b99384c62:

```
$ HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 pytest -v tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py::test_deepseek_v41_rocm_first_layer_unfolded_entry
tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py::test_deepseek_v41_rocm_first_layer_unfolded_entry PASSED
1 passed in 7.13s
```

With only the gate line reverted (the import kept), it fails at the routing assertion:

```
>       assert unfolded_fn is decoder.hc_attn_fn
E       AssertionError
1 failed in 6.75s
```

On main as is, it fails earlier because `amd_model` has no `on_gfx942` to patch:

```
E       AttributeError: <module 'vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.model' ...> has no attribute 'on_gfx942'
1 failed in 3.54s
```

Other tests on MI300X with this change: `pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` 98 passed, 5 skipped. `pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py -k rocm` 21 passed, 3 failed; the three failures (`test_mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rocm_aiter[True-2/7/128]`, 3 to 303 bf16 elements off by up to 0.25 against a 0.02 tolerance) are identical, element for element, on main without this change.

**Entry seam microbenchmark** (single MI300X, HIP graph replay, real layer-0 weights, hc=4, hidden=5120, 20 Sinkhorn iterations; script below):

| Tokens | Folded, main (µs) | Unfolded, this PR (µs) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 24 | 336.8 | 13.8 |
| 48 | 322.0 | 12.4 |
| 288 | 392.6 | 24.1 |
| 8192 | 626.4 | 291.0 |

Max abs error vs the reference op on fp32 inputs is the same order for both forms (layer input 0, post mix 6e-8 to 2.4e-7, comb mix 6e-8 to 6.3e-7).

<details>
<summary>Microbenchmark script</summary>

```python
"""Layer-0 entry mHC seam on gfx942: folded (x=embedding) vs unfolded (x=None).

Uses the checkpoint's layer-0 hc_attn_* weights, times both forms under HIP graph
replay and compares each with the reference op run on fp32 inputs.

Usage: python bench_mhc_entry.py --model <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash dir> [--tokens 24 48 ...]
"""

import argparse
import json

import torch
from safetensors import safe_open
from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
from vllm.model_executor.layers.mhc import MHCPreDelayedOp


def load_layer0(model):
    with open(f"{model}/model.safetensors.index.json") as f:
        wmap = json.load(f)["weight_map"]
    weights = {}
    for name in ("hc_attn_fn", "hc_attn_scale", "hc_attn_base"):
        key = f"layers.0.{name}"
        with safe_open(f"{model}/{wmap[key]}", "pt") as f:
            weights[name] = f.get_tensor(key).float().cuda()
    with open(f"{model}/config.json") as f:
        cfg = json.load(f)["text_config"]
    return weights, cfg


def seam(op, residual, fn, w, cfg, x, native=False):
    args = (
        residual,
        fn,
        w["hc_attn_scale"],
        w["hc_attn_base"],
        cfg["rms_norm_eps"],
        cfg["hc_eps"],
        cfg["hc_eps"],
        2.0,
        cfg["hc_sinkhorn_iters"],
    )
    forward = op.forward_native if native else op.forward_hip
    return forward(*args, x=x)


def graph_us(call, iters=200):
    for _ in range(3):
        call()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
        call()
    for _ in range(20):
        graph.replay()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    start, end = torch.cuda.Event(True), torch.cuda.Event(True)
    start.record()
    for _ in range(iters):
        graph.replay()
    end.record()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / iters


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--tokens", type=int, nargs="+", default=[24, 48, 288, 8192])
    args = parser.parse_args()

    torch.manual_seed(0)
    w, cfg = load_layer0(args.model)
    hc, hidden = cfg["hc_mult"], cfg["hidden_size"]
    fn_unfolded = w["hc_attn_fn"]
    fn_folded = fn_unfolded.view(-1, hc, hidden).sum(dim=1)
    with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()):
        op = MHCPreDelayedOp()
    print(f"hc={hc} hidden={hidden} sinkhorn={cfg['hc_sinkhorn_iters']}")
    print(
        "| Tokens | Folded (us) | Unfolded (us) | Max abs err vs fp32 reference, "
        "folded / unfolded: layer input, post mix, comb mix |"
    )
    print("|---:|---:|---:|---|")
    for t in args.tokens:
        emb = torch.randn(t, hidden, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        residual = emb.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, hc, -1).contiguous()

        def folded(residual=residual, emb=emb):
            return seam(op, residual, fn_folded, w, cfg, emb)

        def unfolded(residual=residual):
            return seam(op, residual, fn_unfolded, w, cfg, None)

        t_f, t_u = graph_us(folded), graph_us(unfolded)
        ref = seam(op, residual.float(), fn_unfolded, w, cfg, None, native=True)
        errs = [
            [(out[i].double() - ref[i].double()).abs().max().item() for i in (3, 1, 2)]
            for out in (folded(), unfolded())
        ]
        err = " / ".join(" ".join(f"{e:.1e}" for e in form) for form in errs)
        print(f"| {t} | {t_f:.1f} | {t_u:.1f} | {err} |", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python bench_mhc_entry.py --model <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash dir> --tokens 24 48 288 8192`

</details>

**End to end**: 4× MI300X (gfx942), TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DSpark with 5 draft tokens and golden acceptance length 3.51 for throughput, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, SWA bounded replay on, no `--monokernel`, InferenceX AgentX trace replay, 1 h per arm, baseline and patched arm on the same node. The baseline is the image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-f5d93296c8ec` (main as of 2026-11-11); the patched arm overlays an earlier revision of this change on it, whose gate (`self.mono.unfolded_entry if self.mono is not None else on_gfx942()`) takes the same path as this branch without `--monokernel`. These runs predate the rebase onto b99384c62, which brings nine further `deepseek_v41/amd` commits; the unit tests above were rerun on the rebased branch.

| Concurrency | Run pair | E2E interactivity P50, f5d93296 → this PR | E2E interactivity P90 | Output tok/s per GPU | Failed requests, f5d93296 / this PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | node 1, first | 137.82 → 142.75 (+3.58%) | -1.19% | +0.59% | 1 / 0 |
| 8 | node 1, second | 139.17 → 142.95 (+2.72%) | +2.10% | +0.53% | 0 / 0 |
| 8 | node 2 (patched arm first) | 136.80 → 142.40 (+4.09%) | +1.67% | +0.53% | 1 / 0 |
| 32 | node 2 | 58.46 → 59.47 (+1.73%) | +6.15% | +1.16% | 1 / 2 |

The concurrency 32 baseline is the lowest of the unpatched runs on that node (two earlier ones, with the same vLLM packages in an older container, measured 58.98 and 58.49), so concurrency 32 is reported as no regression rather than a gain. Failed requests are client-side (`InvalidInferenceResultError` for an empty response, `ClientOSError`) out of about 1,150 requests per arm at concurrency 8 and 3,450 at concurrency 32; the server logs show no GPU memory fault or engine error in any run.

Reproduce with the image above and:

```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --moe-backend aiter --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","enable_adaptive_verification":false,"synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51}'
```

The load is the InferenceX AgentX trace replay (`dsv41flash` TP4 concurrency 8 and 32, 3,600 s). Accuracy runs use `"rejection_sample_method":"block"` without the synthetic length.

**Accuracy** (TP4, concurrency 32, real block verification, same image; stderr ±0.0044 for GSM8K):

| Build | Runs | Acceptance length (golden 3.51) | GSM8K strict-match |
|---|---:|---|---|
| this PR | 3 | 3.482, 3.489, 3.514 (mean 3.495) | 0.9735, 0.9757, 0.9735 |
| f5d93296 | 2 | 3.523, 3.516 (mean 3.519) | 0.9742, 0.9712 |

All runs pass the acceptance gate. The patched mean is 0.7% lower; earlier unpatched runs in this setup measured 3.486 to 3.523, so the difference is within run-to-run spread at this sample size. Throughput runs use the fixed synthetic length and are not affected by it.

## Details

- **Numerics**: the hc copies of the expanded embedding are equal, so the projection computes the same products and only their order of addition changes; `pre_mix=None` still selects copy 0 as the layer input. Outputs are not bitwise identical to main.
- **Scope**: the gate is now `on_gfx942()` alone, so the stock layer-0 entry seam no longer depends on the mono switch. It applies to decode, prefill and mixed steps of the stock path, which RFC #60904 keeps as the default and as the path for prefill, mixed and large batches. gfx950 keeps its current path (TileLang for the folded seam).
- **Graph capture**: `mhc_pre_delayed_aiter` already runs inside FULL graphs at the other gfx942 seams; the end-to-end runs above exercise this seam in FULL_DECODE_ONLY decode graphs.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][KDA] Export Triton KDA prefill checkpoints via a per-sequence buffer
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Let the Triton KDA prefill of GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K3 (NVIDIA) export align-mode prefill checkpoints, with the same contract FlashKDA already uses: the chunk recurrence writes each checkpoint's state into a per-sequence `[N, H, V, K]` buffer, and the shared `FlashKDAPrefillCheckpointExporter` moves it into the checkpoint block together with the conv window. A prompt is then no longer split at its last Mamba block boundary on the Triton backend.

The kernel change is ZJY0516's from ZJY0516/vllm#30 (the GDN version of the same idea), applied unchanged to `chunk_delta_h.py`; thanks to ZJY0516 for it. Related: #59755 (difference from #61951's host split explained there). #65186 stores checkpoints from a paged-state recurrence instead; this PR keeps the existing gather/scatter and only adds the two checkpoint arguments.

## Claims

- `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` gains `checkpoint_state` / `checkpoint_offsets`; launches without them compile to the same kernel as before (`STORE_CHECKPOINT` is a constexpr).
- `--kda-prefill-backend triton` declares checkpoint alignment 64, so in `--mamba-cache-mode align` the scheduler runs a prompt that crosses a block boundary in one step.
- The KDA wrappers only pass the two arguments through; the layers reuse the FlashKDA buffer + exporter path.

## Validation

GB300:

```bash
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py \
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_checkpoint_exporter.py tests/kernels/fla
# 1924 passed, 7 skipped
```

- `test_triton_kda_checkpoint_correctness` (new): with checkpoints, output and final state match the run without them, a row with offset 0 is untouched, and each checkpoint matches a naive fp32 recurrence over its prefix.
- `test_prefill_checkpoint_resumes_suffix` gains Triton cases (offsets 64 and 256): restoring both cached states reproduces an uninterrupted prefill through the real layer forward, with and without spec decode.
- Forcing `STORE_CHECKPOINT` off makes 10 of these tests fail.

- GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 on GB300: TTFT -15% / -20% / -17% at concurrency 1 / 4 / 16; gsm8k with prefix-cache hits unchanged.
- GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 on MI355X (same Triton path): TTFT -35% / -11% at concurrency 1 / 16 (concurrency 4 within noise); Kimi-K3 on MI355X (separate AMD path) unchanged.

GLM-5.3-Flash FP8, 4x GB300, TP4, `--kda-prefill-backend triton --enable-prefix-caching` (align mode, block size 2176), 8192-token step budget. Baseline is main at `9448aba2c8`; two fresh servers per arm, interleaved base/PR/base/PR, mean of both.

| ISL 8000 / OSL 32, concurrency | TTFT ms, main → PR | total tok/s, main → PR | TPOT ms, main → PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 218 → 185 (-15%) | 26,176 → 29,727 | 2.84 → 2.74 |
| 4 | 526 → 419 (-20%) | 37,583 → 41,329 | 10.59 → 11.54 |
| 16 | 980 → 812 (-17%) | 46,883 → 48,397 | 56.7 → 59.4 |

Prefix-cache counters: 0 hits at concurrency 1 and 4, 6,528 of 2,048,000 tokens at 16 (both arms). Without a checkpoint the scheduler ends an 8000-token prompt's first step at 6528 (3 × 2176) to save the state and needs a second step; with it the prompt runs in one step. The unsplit prefill delays other requests' decode steps, so TPOT rises 9% / 5% at concurrency 4 / 16.

| `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-shots 20` (fixed few-shot prefix, 61% of prompt tokens hit), 4 runs per arm | main | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| accuracy | 0.9227 / 0.9174 / 0.9219 / 0.9257 | 0.9174 / 0.9242 / 0.9181 / 0.9249 |

Same workload on ROCm, this branch against main `9448aba2c8`, two fresh servers per arm, mean of both:

| ISL 8000 / OSL 32, concurrency | GLM-5.3-Flash, 4x MI355X, TP4: TTFT ms | TPOT ms | total tok/s | Kimi-K3, 8x MI355X, TP8: TTFT ms | TPOT ms | total tok/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 486.6 → 318.9 (-34.5%) | 6.27 → 6.14 | 12,411 → 15,988 | 448.2 → 452.9 | 13.44 → 13.45 | 9,285 → 9,230 |
| 4 | 527.3 → 559.4 (+6.1%) | 16.30 → 14.28 | 31,212 → 32,406 | 834.2 → 833.7 | 28.24 → 28.27 | 18,648 → 18,646 |
| 16 | 1,417.1 → 1,267.5 (-10.6%) | 64.54 → 61.43 | 37,305 → 39,956 | 2,223.7 → 2,224.0 | 116.16 → 116.06 | 21,749 → 21,773 |

GLM concurrency 4 TTFT is noisy on MI355X: a third pair of servers gave 824.7 → 543.5 ms. Kimi-K3 on ROCm runs its own `kimi_k3/amd` path, which this PR does not change; all its differences are below 0.6%.

`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` server on this branch: checkpointed 8000-token prefills and prefix-hit resumes from the stored checkpoints (2176 / 4352 / 6528 cached tokens), no sync errors.

## Details

- Buffer: `max_num_seqs × local heads × 128 × 128` in the state cache dtype, reserved at init from the shared grow-only workspace (GLM-5.3-Flash TP4: 1 MiB per sequence with an fp32 state). FlashKDA already reserves two buffers of this size.
- The Kimi exporter now gets `state_len=conv_size - 1`, as GLM's does, so checkpoints keep the right conv window under speculative decoding; #67784 makes the same change for FlashKDA.
- An unsplit prefill can delay other requests' decode steps in that step, as with FlashKDA.
- GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm uses the same Triton kernel and layer code, so it gets checkpoints too (serving numbers above; the unit tests were run on GB300 only). FlashKDA and FlashInfer KDA prefill are unchanged.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the implementation and the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][KV Connector][MooncakeConnector] Submit Mooncake transfer descriptors with array API
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Mooncake TE [v0.3.14](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/releases/tag/v0.3.14) introduced `batch_transfer_sync_write_arrays` through [Mooncake #4763](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4763). vLLM's integration should use this released API to avoid list conversion overhead. This PR switches from `batch_transfer_sync_write` to the arrays API, keeping descriptors as contiguous `uint64` arrays through submission, with capability-based list fallback for older engines.

This follows the descriptor-overhead investigation in [vLLM #63006](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63006) and [Mooncake #5169](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/5169). Instead of reducing descriptor preparation time inside vllm and handling time inside Mooncake, this PR targets reducing Python/C++ descriptor conversion time between vllm and Mooncake (pre-transfer time). Such pre-transfer time consumes about 14–18% of a batched API call time in these runs.

## Claims

- Avoid Python address boxing, element-by-element list conversion in pybind11, and the additional by-value vector copies at the synchronous list entry. The existing arrays API still performs a bulk buffer-to-vector copy.
- Preserve compatibility with engines that do not expose a callable arrays API.
- In Qwen3-32B vLLM PD disagg runs, KV transfer BW improves **10.4–17.7%** and mean pre-transfer overhead falls **95.0–97.3%**. Normal public-API 1K calibration pairs show **+12.4% / +7.1%** bandwidth changes.

## Details

- **`batch_transfer_sync_write` repeats O(N) conversion and copying.** The connector boxes values with `.tolist()`; pybind11 rebuilds three vectors, which the WRITE wrapper copies again. These passes hold the GIL and scale with descriptor count.

- **`batch_transfer_sync_write_arrays` removes intermediate conversions.** This arrays API bulk-copies contiguous numpy `uint64` buffers into vectors and moves them into the shared transfer function. One buffer-to-vector copy remains; descriptor counts and downstream TE/TENT execution stay the same.

- **Capability detection keeps older Mooncake engines compatible.** Initialization selects the callable arrays API or falls back to the legacy list path for older engines, including ROCm builds.

Production code modification is small: uses `batch_transfer_sync_write_arrays` API and directly uses `np.NDArray` as ptr inputs without `.to_list()` conversion. Test logic is not modified but uses `np.testing.assert_array_equal` to match type change.

## Validation

### Unit Tests

Six new parametrized cases cover array arguments, missing/non-callable API fallback, low/high addresses and Python integer statistics. They fail on the base and pass with the change. The connector, hybrid/Mamba and statistics suites pass **213 tests with three existing xfails**. pre-commit, mypy and CI test-selection checks pass.

Unit command, from a vLLM checkout with its test environment active:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_stats.py
```

### Qwen3-32B E2E Results

Source bases: vLLM main `43c1db8c9f30` (checked out 11-13-2026) and Mooncake main `6ca711276690` (checked out 11-13-2026). 
Both performance variants use the following configuration:

| Parameter | Configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware | One node with 8 × NVIDIA H20 GPUs and four RoCE HCAs |
| Model | Qwen3-32B, BF16; 64 GQA layers, 8 KV heads |
| Deployment | Prefill TP4, decode TP2; PP1, DP1; separate GPU, CPU, NUMA and HCA placement |
| KV cache | Block size 16; APC disabled; static KV cache; maximum model length 40,960 |
| Execution | Normal compilation and CUDA Graph enabled |
| Workload | Fixed synthetic prompts: 1K/2K/4K/8K/16K/32K; one output token; 300-second dispatch window |
| Arrival rate | 0.5 requests/s at 1K–8K; 0.25 requests/s at 16K/32K |
| Samples | 150 requests per variant at 1K–8K; 75 at 16K/32K; fresh services for each run |
| Transport | Classic TE RDMA; 10 sender threads; 2 workers per context |
| RDMA settings | Signal interval 32; WR limit 4,096; CQ depth 8,192; 2 QPs per endpoint; slice size 65,536 bytes |

**Results**: values are means. 

| Prompt | RPS | Connector | TTFT (ms) | KV BW (MiB/s) | KV BW delta vs. MC before | Xfer time (ms) | Pre-transfer overhead (ms) |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1K | 0.5 | MC before (list) | 202.44 | 13088.28 | — | 4.903 | 0.685 |
| 1K | 0.5 | MC after (arrays) | 203.35 | 14815.56 | +13.2% | 4.338 | 0.034 |
| 2K | 0.5 | MC before (list) | 352.72 | 14003.46 | — | 9.188 | 1.409 |
| 2K | 0.5 | MC after (arrays) | 349.18 | 15466.38 | +10.4% | 8.313 | 0.050 |

**Updated on 11-16-2026**

Mooncake transfer backend refactor #64363 has landed on main 20b15bbf5bf550e390d322ce49b6a9d8b3ae3cbf. To use `batch_transfer_sync_write_arrays` API, this PR adds a `transfer_sync_array` abstract method in `backend.py` alongside the general `transfer` method. New benchmark results show that, with new `transfer` method folding each `(src_ptr, dst_ptr, length)` into a `RequestRange`, KV transfer BW can be significantly degraded under numerous descriptors per batched call, due to `RequestRange` construction overheads:

| Prompt | RPS | Connector | TTFT (ms) | KV BW (MiB/s) | KV BW delta vs. MC before | Xfer time (ms) |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1K | 0.5 | MC before (transfer method) | 209.15 | 7461.49 | — | 8.656 |
| 1K | 0.5 | MC after (transfer_sync_array method) | 195.04 | 13099.90 | +75.6% | 4.891 |
| 2K | 0.5 | MC before (transfer method) | 367.88 | 7578.66 | — | 17.032 |
| 2K | 0.5 | MC after (transfer_sync_array method) | 346.14 | 13505.68 | +78.2% | 9.487 |
| 4K | 0.5 | MC before (transfer method) | 686.05 | 9169.94 | — | 27.999 |
| 4K | 0.5 | MC after (transfer_sync_array method) | 653.14 | 16077.53 | +75.3% | 15.925 |
| 8K | 0.5 | MC before (transfer method) | 1381.14 | 8635.29 | — | 60.140 |
| 8K | 0.5 | MC after (transfer_sync_array method) | 1283.16 | 17356.62 | +101.0% | 29.515 |
| 16K | 0.25 | MC before (transfer method) | 2849.70 | 9939.02 | — | 103.183 |
| 16K | 0.25 | MC after (transfer_sync_array method) | 2754.60 | 18149.70 | +82.6% | 56.428 |
| 32K | 0.25 | MC before (transfer method) | 82406.13 | 9497.09 | — | 216.533 |
| 32K | 0.25 | MC after (transfer_sync_array method) | 82182.29 | 18122.50 | +90.8% | 113.026 |

Using `batch_transfer_sync_write_arrays` with `transfer_sync_array` method avoids per-`RequestRange` and list-vector conversion overheads. KV transfer BW has returned to the better performance of MC after (arrays) in the previous table.

Since neither `batch_transfer_sync_write` nor `batch_transfer_sync_write_arrays` in Mooncake TE API returns per request-range status, `transfer() -> list[TransferEvent]` seems unnecessary currently but hurts performance. I suggest using `transfer_sync_arrays() -> BatchTransferResult` as the prefered fast path, treating `transfer` as a canonical and general fallback.

## Related

- [Mooncake #4763 — Buffer-protocol and page-gathered batch transfer APIs](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4763): provides the existing arrays API used here; this PR connects it to vLLM without adding a production Mooncake API.
- [vLLM #62478 — Vectorize transfer descriptor build](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62478): vectorizes descriptor construction; this follow-up retains its array results through the binding instead of converting them back into Python lists.
- [vLLM #63006 — Descriptor and WR overhead RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63006) and [#63142 — Descending-block coalescing](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63142): motivate reducing descriptor costs; this change preserves their grouping/coalescing behavior and reduces submission overhead for the remaining descriptors.
- [Mooncake #5039 — Classic TE preparation/posting pipeline](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/5039): overlaps downstream preparation and posting; array submission addresses overhead before that shared transfer body.
- [Mooncake #5169 — TENT metadata preparation roadmap](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/5169): broader investigation; this change reuses the shared facade and does not implement worker-sharded preparation or claim measured TENT gains.
- [vLLM #60605 — Contiguous block grouping optimization](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60605): open, adjacent work on grouping allocations rather than arrays API selection.
- [vLLM #65501 — High-address overflow on Intel XPU](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65501): open work on unsigned address arithmetic in the list path. This PR needs the same unsigned arithmetic for its buffer contract and additionally changes descriptor representation, API selection and legacy fallback.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Enable CUDA IPC weight-cache restarts for serialized compressed-tensors tensor/channel FP8 linear weights. Part of #56049.

This is now independent, directly based on main `34d5de18cd8b`. [Review only this feature](https://github.com/liusy58/vllm/compare/34d5de18cd8baf9f5958e45720858939863a7264...4d954d5d1289d3940116fdafca757a12aa363873); head `4d954d5d1289`. Rebuilt in response to Zifeng’s request to decouple the stacked PRs.

## Claims

- Reuse processed weights/scales across engine restarts with the validated CUTLASS backend.
- Preserve exact outputs, shared storage and required Python metadata; unsupported configurations remain rejected.
- Include only this feature and its necessary common plumbing beyond merged main.

## Validation

B300, November 4, exact source hashes verified against this head:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Layer/configuration regressions | 10 passed, 59 deselected in 22.66s |
| Real model: ordinary → fallback → IPC → second IPC | 1 passed in 141.02s |
| All changed-file pre-commit hooks | Passed, including mypy, ruff and CI test tethering |

Both IPC loads forbid fallback. Exact greedy outputs use `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`; layer tests also verify shared pointers and unchanged tensors. The Llama8B test used the existing local RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-FP8 snapshot `881d74b74ad8ebe8775fb178b1fd0c935477f1bc`, substituted for its HF alias, with GPU memory utilization 0.12. Assertions and all four loading paths are unchanged.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k compressed_fp8_preprocessed -q -rs
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_ipc_cache_compressed_fp8 -q -rs
pre-commit run --files $(git diff 34d5de18cd8baf9f5958e45720858939863a7264 HEAD --name-only)
```

The isolated runtime used Python 3.12, Torch 2.14/cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, process-local CUDAcompat13.4, and reused stable extensions from `5d55ef159`. Relevant CUTLASS FP8 C++ is unchanged; unrelated HiSparse binding and removed Qutlass-wrapper changes are outside these tests. This is targeted smoke/output equivalence, not a pristine full-source rebuild, full accuracy evaluation, performance benchmark, or upstream GPU CI result. No new skips, retries or weakened assertions were added. GPU occupancy guards prevented launches onto busy GPUs; other workloads were untouched.

<details>
<summary>Original feature baseline evidence (previous revisions)</summary>

On original base `084cab1bc7`, the ten new layer/attention cases failed; the real model failed with `UnsupportedQuantForIPCError: CompressedTensorsLinearMethod does not support loading from pre-processed weights`. The attention restore also reproduced `Tensor.item() cannot be called on meta tensors`. These are historical baseline runs, not a rerun on today’s main.

</details>

## Details

Only an actual CUTLASS FP8 linear kernel opts in. IPC restores the transposed layout metadata, dynamic input-scale state, and attention-scale host metadata without transforming shared tensors again.

The common compressed-tensors scheme capability bridge and attention-buffer restoration are also necessary in independent #63976. Neither PR requires the other. If both merge, retain both narrow capability cases; the shared hook may need a textual conflict resolution.

Duplicate-work check: this updates the existing draft; #63672/#63754 have merged and are preserved. No duplicate PR or broader quantization expansion is introduced. Dedicated B200 CI selects the relevant new tests. The format guide links the preload commands and limitations; fresh local documentation checks passed. GitHub/rendered checks for the new head are tracked separately until observed.

AI assistance was used. Human review and human-executed validation are not asserted by these agent results.

commits.pr_title: [XPU][UT] Enable v1/attention tests on XPU
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Make `tests/v1/attention` collect and run on XPU, and enable XPU for tests whose code paths are platform-neutral or have an XPU implementation. It changes 11 test files and adds one Intel CI job, with no `vllm/` changes. Apart from `test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py`, which is now ROCm-only, it does not change which tests run on CUDA or ROCm.

Related: #64255 (XPU `FLASH_ATTN_MLA` class in `test_mla_backends`), #65600 (`test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90` on non-CUDA builds), #48761 (Intel CI job for `v1/attention`).

## Claims

- XPU collection errors go from 5 to 2. The three GLM-5.3-Flash test files (`glm5next` raises `NotImplementedError` on XPU at import) now skip at module level. The remaining two, `test_cuda_backend_probe_errors.py` and `test_deepseek_v4_rocm_adaptive.py`, are CUDA/ROCm-only and are left unchanged; XPU runs should `--ignore` them.
- **223 tests go from skipped to passed on XPU**, including 54 sparse MLA decode-correctness cases on `XPUMLASparseBackend` and 78 mamba block-table kernel tests.
- `test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py` now runs only on ROCm, because AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill is ROCm-only. Its 12 failures on XPU become skips. Its mocked selection tests no longer run on CUDA CI.
- No test that passed before is skipped or failing now.
- New Intel CI step `:intel: (BMG) V1 Attention` (`.buildkite/intel_jobs/attention_intel.yaml`) runs the changed tests on XPU, so these XPU paths are covered in CI.

## Validation

Intel Arc Pro B60, torch 2.14.0+xpu, vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.17, base `157e42a762`. Same selection with and without this PR:

| | Collection (`v1/attention`) | Changed tests: passed / skipped / failed |
|---|---|---|
| main | 2448 collected, **5 errors** (whole run aborts) | 108 / 182 / 12 |
| this PR | 2807 collected, **2 errors** (0 with the two `--ignore`s) | **331 / 329 / 0** |

<details><summary>Skipped → passed per file</summary>

| File | Skipped → passed |
|---|---|
| `test_mamba_align_block_table.py` | 78 |
| `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` (was module-skipped) | 76 |
| `test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py` | 32 |
| `test_indexer_dcp_localize.py` | 21 |
| `test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py` | 14 |
| `test_mla_backends.py` | 1 |
| `test_vit_attn_wrappers.py` | 1 |

</details>

```bash
cd tests
pytest --collect-only -q v1/attention
pytest -v v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py \
  v1/attention/test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py \
  v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py \
  v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
  v1/attention/test_mamba_align_block_table.py \
  v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py::test_mock_mla_dcp_fp8_decode_gathers_quantized_query \
  v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py \
  v1/attention/test_vit_attn_wrappers.py::test_sdpa_output_layout_without_cu_seqlens
```

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes.

## Details

- **Collection errors, now module-level skips placed before the failing import:** `test_kpool_indexer_block_sizes.py`, `test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py`, `test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py` (`glm5next` refuses XPU at import).
- **Guards widened to XPU, with hardcoded `"cuda"` devices replaced by `current_platform.device_type`:**
  - `test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py`. The `is_rocm=True` params of `test_prefix_cache_replays_the_swa_window` still skip off CUDA/ROCm.
  - `test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py`.
  - `test_indexer_dcp_localize.py`. These tests now run on CUDA, ROCm and XPU; #62298 enabled ROCm for the same tests, and this PR merges the two.
  - `test_mla_backends.py::test_mock_mla_dcp_fp8_decode_gathers_quantized_query`.
  - `test_mamba_align_block_table.py`, which covers the shared Triton block-table kernel used by GDN/mamba/linear attention.
  - `test_vit_attn_wrappers.py::test_sdpa_output_layout_without_cu_seqlens`.
- **`test_sparse_mla_backends.py`:**
  - The module now runs on XPU. `XPUMLASparseBackend` is parametrized into the decode-correctness test, mirroring the existing ROCm setup.
  - The ROCm-only autouse fixture is generalized to per-platform allowlists. The XPU allowlist is limited to the tests that exercise code XPU's sparse path uses: decode correctness, the `sparse_utils` Triton index conversion, and indexer prefill chunking.
  - The `torch.cuda.get_device_capability() < (9, 0)` skip decorators now check `is_cuda()` first, so they no longer crash at collection on XPU.
- **Still CUDA-only, deliberately:**
  - CUDA-graph capture tests.

  - HiSparse CUDA-op tests.

- **CUDA/ROCm:** every widened guard evaluates the same as before on CUDA/ROCm GPU runners (`torch.cuda.is_available()` is replaced by `is_cuda_alike()`, which matches on those runners).
