commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Return 400 for media the request got wrong
commits.pr_body:
## Overview With the Rust frontend, a chat request whose media is wrong (data that is not base64, bytes that do not decode as audio or an image, a URL the media connector refuses) gets a 500 `InternalServerError`. For bad data and bytes that do not decode, the Python frontend answers with a 400. ## Claims - Media errors that `llm_multimodal::MediaConnectorError::fault()` classifies as `MediaFault::Client` now return a 400 `BadRequestError`. This covers chat completions and `/tokenize`, and a gRPC request whose media is at fault now gets `INVALID_ARGUMENT` instead of `INTERNAL`. - `Transient` errors (a fetch timeout, a 5xx from the media host) and `Internal` ones (a decode task or decoder I/O failing on the server) stay 500, as in Python. - An `input_audio` part whose `format` is neither `wav` nor `mp3` gets a 400, as Python's request validation gives it, instead of a 500. Rust still accepts `WAV`/`MP3` and a missing `format`, which Python also rejects with a 400. ## Validation Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B on one RTX 6000 Ada. The same `/v1/chat/completions` requests against the Python frontend, and against `vllm-rs` built from 75fc05a53 (the commit of the installed wheel, which pins an older llm-multimodal with the same `fault()`) without and with this change, selected with `VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH`: | Audio input | Python | Rust, main | Rust, this PR | |---|---|---|---| | `input_audio` data that is not base64 | 400 | 500 | 400 | | `input_audio` data that is base64 text, not audio | 400 | 500 | 400 | | `input_audio` with empty data | 400 | 500 | 400 | | `audio_url` data URL whose payload is not audio | 400 | 500 | 400 | | `audio_url` `ftp://example.invalid/a.wav` | 400 | 500 | 400 | | `audio_url` `http://127.0.0.1:9/nope.wav` | 500 | 500 | 400 (see below) | | valid WAV, labelled `wav` and `mp3` | 200 | 200 | 200, same transcript | An `input_audio` part labelled `flac` gets a 400 from Python's request validation and a 500 from Rust on main (checked on 50a184f43). The second commit makes it a 400; that is covered by the unit test below, not by the GPU run above. Tests: - `non_stream_chat_rejects_invalid_media_as_bad_request` (`vllm-server` route test): image data URLs that are not base64 or not an image, and a `file://` URL. All three return 500 on main. - `input_audio_uses_connector_data_urls` (`vllm-chat`): an unsupported `input_audio` format is a validation error. It fails on the first commit. - `media_error_is_request_validation_error_only_when_the_request_is_at_fault` (`vllm-chat`): a client error is a validation error; a timeout and a decoder I/O error are not. It fails if every media error is treated as a validation error. - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings` pass. `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` on Linux passes except `roundtrip_step5`, `roundtrip_mimo_v26` and `roundtrip_kimi_k25`, which load live Hugging Face checkpoints (for example, `stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview` fails with "the model config does not define `vocab_size`") and do not touch this code. `audio_pipeline_attributes_stage_timings_to_request` also fails, on main too, when it shares a process with the other `vllm-chat` tests; it passes on its own, and CI's nextest runs each test in its own process. ## Details `vllm-chat` turned every `MediaConnectorError`, directly and through `MultiModalError::Media`, into `Error::Multimodal(String)`. `is_request_validation_error()` counts `Multimodal` as a server error, which fits its other uses (a missing processor config, a placeholder that does not tokenize). The connector already reports whose fault each error is, so this keeps the typed error in a new `Error::Media` variant and asks `fault()`. `Error::Media` displays the connector error's whole chain. The 400 body uses `Display`, and reqwest keeps the reason for a failed fetch (a refused connection, a TLS error) in its source, so without that the 400 would only say "error sending request for url (…)". Where Python answers differently, this follows the connector's classification: | Case | Python | This PR | |---|---|---| | Media host answers 4xx (other than 408 and 429), or the download is over the size limit | 422 | 400 | | Media host answers 408 or 429 | 500 | 400 | | Host cannot be resolved or refuses the connection | 500 | 400 | | Private or loopback address | fetched like any other host | 400 (the connector never fetches these here; it was a 500 before) | | Data URL that is not base64-encoded | 501 | 400 | The Rust frontend has no 422 error class; adding one for the first row can be a follow-up. In the first table, nothing listens on `127.0.0.1:9`, so Python's request fails to connect, while the Rust connector refuses the address before connecting. No open or closed PR or issue covers this; I searched for Rust frontend media error codes. #63580 adds a different variant to `is_request_validation_error()`. ---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Slice WRITE heads by each layer's head count
commits.pr_body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"tjtanaa"} -->
_Requested by **Tun Jian** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Y89rdnx6bykh6PmfBBmcrG?thread=cmsg_01Y89rdnx6bykh6PmfBBmcrGMxmekkMytHSZontLWbLbMo)_


## Overview

Heterogeneous-TP MoRIIO WRITE (#61726) sizes every layer's KV-head slices from the model-wide KV-head count, which is the maximum over layers. Models whose layers have different KV-head counts (Gemma4) then write slices a layer does not have. This PR slices each layer by its own head count.

## Claims

- **Per-layer head counts.** WRITE between different prefill and decode TP sizes builds each attention layer's targets from that layer's own KV-head count, read from its KV cache spec (`num_kv_heads` per rank times the TP size). This covers drafter layers with their own KV cache (e.g. EAGLE3), which the target's per-layer config does not list. When a layer holds one head per rank, the spec cannot tell the total, so the count comes from the config of the model the layer belongs to: the target's per-layer config, or the drafter's (`speculative_config.draft_model_config`) for draft layers, indexed from the drafter's first layer. Models whose layers all share one count are unchanged.
- **Failures fixed.** With the Gemma4 shape in vLLM's model-config test (4 KV heads in the sliding layers, 8 in full attention, model-wide 8):
  - prefill TP1 → decode TP2 used to fail with `Head slice ... is outside 4 / 2 heads` on the sliding layers;
  - prefill TP4 → decode TP8 used to write from a producer head that does not exist.
- **Drafters fixed.** With an EAGLE3 drafter (RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-speculator.eagle3), prefill TP1 → decode TP2 used to raise `IndexError: list index out of range` in `_layer_total_num_kv_heads`, because the draft layer's index is past the target's per-layer config.

## Validation

- **New fixtures** in the WRITE byte-exact matrix (`test_moriio_hetero_tp_write.py`), across the existing TP pairs plus TP4 ↔ TP8, HMA on and off, and 3 cache-layout pairs:
  - `mixed_heads`: before this change, 44 of its 48 cases fail; after, all pass.
  - `mixed_heads_draft` (draft layer numbered after the target's) and `draft_from_zero` (drafter numbered from 0). At TP4 ↔ TP8 their draft layers hold one head per rank; without the drafter-config lookup, 12 of those cases fail.
- **EAGLE3 E2E:** RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-speculator.eagle3, prefill TP1 → decode TP2: gsm8k 0.446 strict / 0.460 flexible.
- **Full MoRIIO unit suite** (CPU): 1113 passed; the 4 failures need a ROCm attention backend and fail the same way on main. Ruff is clean, and mypy reports no new errors.

## Details

- `_execute_write_task` recomputes an attention layer's target for the same decode rank from the layer's mapping. It skips the layer when another producer writes that copy, which happens when a layer with fewer heads is replicated.
- The request's `write_done` writers (`num_writers`) are unchanged. A layer with fewer heads only ever needs a subset of the model-wide writers, so every writer still writes something and sends `write_done`.
- Mamba state slicing does not depend on KV heads and keeps the request's mapping.
- The same bug in heterogeneous-TP READ is fixed in the READ PR stacked on the READ fan-in fix.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Report transferred bytes in tiering metrics
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow up on #63524 by using the secondary tier's reported transfer bytes in tiering metrics. This fixes inflated FS write metrics when blocks are already on disk.

## Claims

- Avoid counting FS blocks skipped because they already exist as bytes written.
- Preserve the existing fallback and partial-failure accounting.

## Validation

- Tests cover reported byte counts, including zero, and preserve fallback and partial-failure accounting.
- The existing FS cascade test checks metrics for fully new, partially existing, and fully existing batches.
- Before: FS metrics reported `[32, 32, 32]` instead of `[32, 16, 0]`. After: all 17 targeted tests passed.
- `pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_metrics.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py`: 95 passed.

## Details

The FS tier skips blocks already on disk, but the metrics currently count every block in a successful job as transferred. As a result, repeated stores can overstate the bytes written.

For successful jobs, use `JobResult.transfer_bytes` when provided, including zero. Jobs without a reported count and partially failed promotions retain the existing chunk-based accounting. #63524 corrected the FS tier's reported byte count but left the Prometheus counters unchanged.

This differs from #67535, which changes lookup metrics, and #67052, which adds promotion outcome metrics; neither fixes transfer-byte accounting.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Apply EVS-recomputed M-RoPE positions on every PP stage
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With video pruning (EVS, `--video-pruning-rate > 0`), Model Runner V2 recomputes each request's M-RoPE positions from the pruned encoder outputs. Only the first pipeline stage runs the encoder, so later stages keep the positions computed for the unpruned video and run their layers with wrong positions for the video tokens, the text after them and every decode step. When positions depend on encoder outputs, the first stage now sends them to the later stages with the intermediate tensors.

## Claims

- **Fix EVS with pipeline parallelism.** Qwen2.5-VL with `video_pruning_rate=0.75` at PP=2 now matches PP=1; on main it silently returns an empty answer for a video request.
- **No change elsewhere.** Positions are sent only for models whose model state reports that they depend on encoder outputs (M-RoPE with multimodal pruning) and only when PP > 1. PP=1 output in eager mode is bitwise identical to main.

## Validation

`Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct` on 2×B300, one video request (the `baby_reading` asset, 16 frames, prompt from `test_qwen2_5_vl.py`), prompt logprobs and 16 greedy tokens. Each row compares PP=2 with PP=1 in the same mode.

| Mode | Video pruning | Code | Prompt logprob \|Δ\| mean / max | Generated tokens equal | PP=2 answer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| eager | 0.75 | main | 0.202 / 4.67 | 0/15 | empty |
| eager | 0.75 | this PR | 0 / 0 (bitwise) | 15/15 | same as PP=1 |
| eager | off | main | 0 / 0 (bitwise) | 15/15 | same as PP=1 |
| CUDA graph | 0.75 | main | 0.217 / 4.67 | 0/15 | empty |
| CUDA graph | 0.75 | this PR | 0.040 / 0.38 | 15/15 | same as PP=1 |
| CUDA graph | off | main | 0.040 / 0.50 | 15/15 | same as PP=1 |

With this PR, the remaining CUDA graph difference is the same size as the PP=2 vs PP=1 difference without pruning.

The new test fails on main (`mean_diff=0.2017`) and passes with this PR with both `VLLM_PP_TRANSPORT=nccl` and `VLLM_PP_TRANSPORT=copy_engine`:

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_qwen2_5_vl.py::test_qwen2_5_vl_evs_pipeline_parallel
```

It carries the 2-GPU distributed mark, so the L4 Distributed Models step and its MI300 mirror run it; this PR adds `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pp_utils.py` to that step's source dependencies. It was not run on ROCm. pre-commit passes.

## Details

- `ModelState.positions_depend_on_encoder` marks model states whose positions need the first stage. `DefaultModelState` sets it for M-RoPE models with multimodal pruning, evaluated from the config on every stage, since later stages have no encoder cache.
- `PPHandler.send_positions` adds the positions to the outgoing `IntermediateTensors` as a token-major `[num_tokens, 3]` int64 tensor, since intermediate tensors are sliced along the first dimension. `PPHandler.receive_positions` copies them into the persistent positions buffer before the forward, so CUDA graphs read them too. Middle stages forward what they received. Only the batch's real tokens are copied, so the copy does not depend on how each stage pads the batch.
- Later stages add a `pp_positions` buffer to their persistent intermediate tensors, since every PP transport requires the received tensors to match them in keys, dtypes and per-token shapes (#67093).
- No host synchronization is added. The extra transfer is `3 × num_tokens` int64 per step, only with EVS and PP.
- Only Qwen2.5-VL was run. The other models that prune with M-RoPE and support PP take the same runner path: Qwen3-VL and its subclasses (Qwen3-VL-MoE, Qwen3.5, Cosmos3) and Cohere Compass. PP > 2 was not run.
- No open issue or PR covers this. #62732 transfers the pruning-adjusted M-RoPE state between disaggregated prefill and decode instances; this PR covers the stages within one instance.

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix LLaVA-OneVision generation when one request contains videos with different frame counts. Return a two-dimensional embedding sequence for each video and add a real-model regression in `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_llava_onevision.py`.

Fixes #67743. Related historical report: #15078, closed by #15082.

## Claims

- A request containing 2-frame and 3-frame videos completes instead of failing the multimodal encoder's 2D-output assertion.
- The regression checks all 982 video placeholder tokens, a nonempty completion, and finite generated-token logprobs.
- The existing optional Nightly / Extended Generation 1 Buildkite step selects this regression with `-m 'not core_model'`; no pipeline change is needed.

## Validation

Reran the dedicated test file in Kaggle version 7 on a Tesla T4 using the model source and test from PR commit `981c75257c7c9211f476ca5cc38ae001b1b44b58`. Downloaded test bytes and source/test SHA-256 values match that commit. The subsequent review edit removes only the `core_model` marker and unused `pytest` import; the test function body and model source remain unchanged.

Configuration: `llava-hf/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov-hf`, FP16, TP=1, eager execution, automatic attention backend selection (TRITON_ATTN decoder and TORCH_SDPA vision encoder selected on T4), greedy sampling, `max_tokens=2`, prefix/processor caches disabled. Environment: PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, Transformers 5.23.0, vLLM 0.34.0rc1.dev535+g919d45fc3.

Both runs use the official wheel and repository test fixtures from merged-main baseline `919d45fc3a54c07034bf637fe649dfa86eed48c2`. The fixed run replaces only the OneVision model module with the PR version. Both runs execute the identical current regression file with no attention backend overrides in the test or environment.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Collection at the GPU-tested commit (before marker removal) | 1 test collected |
| Baseline model source | Expected embedding assertion; 1 failed in 108.87s |
| Current PR model source | 1 passed in 86.38s |

Both JUnit reports contain exactly one test, zero skips, and zero setup/teardown errors. The baseline fails during `LLM.generate`, after model loading; it is not a collection or setup failure. Timings describe individual runs, not a performance comparison.

Run from the repository root, retaining the new test for both model-source variants:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \
  .venv/bin/python -B -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_llava_onevision.py::test_llava_onevision_mixed_frame_count_videos
```

<details>
<summary>Kaggle v7 commands and raw result excerpts</summary>

The harness ran the following commands from `/tmp/vllm-video-wwoh5pnp/repo/tests`, with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` and `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn`. The first used the baseline model module; the second used the PR module.

```bash
/tmp/vllm-video-wwoh5pnp/.venv/bin/python -B -m pytest -v -s \
  models/multimodal/generation/test_llava_onevision.py::test_llava_onevision_mixed_frame_count_videos \
  --junitxml=/kaggle/working/base.xml

/tmp/vllm-video-wwoh5pnp/.venv/bin/python -B -m pytest -v -s \
  models/multimodal/generation/test_llava_onevision.py::test_llava_onevision_mixed_frame_count_videos \
  --junitxml=/kaggle/working/fixed.xml
```

Both runs automatically selected these backends; neither attention setting appears in the logged non-default arguments:

```text
Using AttentionBackendEnum.TORCH_SDPA for MMEncoderAttention.
Using TRITON_ATTN attention backend out of potential backends: ['TRITON_ATTN', 'FLEX_ATTENTION'].
```

Baseline:

```text
AssertionError: Expected multimodal embeddings to be a sequence of 2D tensors, but got tensors with shapes [torch.Size([1, 393, 896]), torch.Size([1, 589, 896])] instead. This is most likely due to incorrect implementation of the model's `embed_multimodal` method.
======================== 1 failed in 108.87s (0:01:48) =========================
EXIT base.log 1
```

Fixed:

```text
========================= 1 passed in 86.38s (0:01:26) =========================
EXIT fixed.log 0
```

</details>

CI configuration inspection confirms that the optional Nightly step `multi-modal-models-extended-generation-1` selects the unmarked file through `models/multimodal/generation -m 'not core_model'`; its ignore list only excludes `test_common.py`, and its source dependencies cover the model and test changes. The AMD mirror uses the same selection. This test is no longer selected by the Standard 4 `core_model` step. The GPU run above predates marker removal; the Nightly routing was checked statically, and the whole Nightly suite was not run.

`git diff --check` and applicable commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, test tethering and DCO.

Earlier T4 runs on baseline `c07d58dc82d75f7d1a947b3264b460384ec3e18d` also verified the standalone reproducer and control requests `[2]`, `[3]`, `[2,2]`: all three controls retained identical generated token IDs and recorded top-5 logprobs before/after. Those controls used `max_tokens=8`. These are targeted regression/control checks, not a general accuracy evaluation; HF comparison, larger checkpoints, ROCm and XPU execution have not been run.

## Details

Unequal frame counts take the list branch of `_process_video_pixels`. Each list element previously had shape `(1, frames * tokens_per_frame + 1, hidden_size)`. Converting the list to a tuple preserves those three-dimensional elements, violating the per-video 2D embedding contract.

Flatten each video's features to `(frames * tokens_per_frame, hidden_size)`, append a `(1, hidden_size)` newline along dimension 0, and return the resulting 2D entries. The batched-tensor and image paths are unchanged. No new arithmetic, transfers, synchronization, dependencies, or shared model-runner changes are introduced.

The model-specific regression reuses `vllm_runner` in its own generation test file. It does not use the common suite's parameterized HF comparisons; `test_common.py` has no changes relative to merged main.

Duplicate checks on 2026-11-15 UTC found no open PR for this packing fix. #57379 adds encoder CUDA graph support without changing the existing list packing; merged #67505 changes input normalization and is included in the model source used in the v7 rerun.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for implementation review, the regression test, GPU validation, and this description.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Pass pulled object storage model dir to the Rust frontend
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

When using the rust frontend, if model tag points to object storage (eg S3), vllm serve fails at startup. This is bc the Rust frontend tries to resolve the path as a HF repo id, which returns 404.

`ModelConfig.maybe_pull_model_tokenizer_for_runai` already pulls the config and
tokenizer files into a local directory and sets `model_config.model` to it. The
weights keep streaming from `model_config.model_weights`. But
`RustFrontendProcessManager` builds `model_tag` from the raw CLI args, so the
Rust frontend never sees the local directory.

So we pass `vllm_config.model_config` to `RustFrontendProcessManager`. For
object storage models, it forwards the pulled directory as `model_tag`. Unless
`--served-model-name` was given, it also sets `served_model_name` to the
original URI, so the served model name matches the Python frontend's.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/test_api_server_process_manager.py
```

New test: `test_rust_frontend_uses_pulled_object_storage_model`. It covers the
default served name and an explicit `--served-model-name`.

## Test Result

All 14 tests in the file pass locally.

---

AI assistance was used to investigate the issue and draft this
change. I have reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Order packed NCCL loads after the caller stream
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`packed_nccl_broadcast_consumer` receives and loads on its own slot streams, which never wait on the caller's stream. Work the caller queued just before the receive can therefore run after the loads and overwrite them. In direct reload, that work is the zero-fill of padded MoE params that `begin_direct_reload` queues at `start_weight_update` (#64352): if it lands late, the loaded weights end up zero.

The fix makes each slot stream `wait_stream(caller_stream)` once, before the first receive. This adds no host sync and covers anything queued before the call. The unpacked NCCL path and IPC already load on the caller's stream.

This PR used to also copy misaligned packed entries on unpack (#64936). That fix is the same `unpack_tensor` change as #65009 and #57665, so it was dropped here to keep one fix per PR.

## Timeline (main)

```
caller stream:  --[ zero-fill W ]------------------------->   (queued first, runs late)
slot stream:    ----------[ broadcast ]--[ load W ]-------->   (no wait on caller)
GPU order:      load W -> zero-fill W -> W == 0
```

With the fix the slot stream waits on the caller's stream first, so the order is always zero-fill, then load.

## Validation

- `TestPackedBroadcastRoundtrip` now loads like a direct reload: every roundtrip copies the received tensors into destinations that the caller zero-fills on its own stream behind a GPU sleep right before the receive, and checks them byte for byte (shape and dtype are asserted before each `copy_`, which would otherwise convert silently). Each case runs once to warm up, then once with the sleep, and asserts the fill was still pending at the first load, so the race window was really open. This replaces four copies of the produce/consume/verify code with one helper. GB200 job 50811: without the fix all 7 roundtrip cases fail in 3/3 runs; with the fix 7/7 pass in 3/3 runs. Whole `tests/distributed/test_packed_tensor.py` with the fix: 33 passed. Ruff 0.17.2 check and format pass.
- End to end (earlier revision with the same stream change, job 46524): gpt-oss-20b, MXFP4, TP1, direct reload over packed NCCL, with a ~10 s GPU delay injected before begin's padding fill. On main, all 144 padding-fill params (w13/w2 weights, scales and biases of 24 layers) end all zero and greedy output is garbage. With the fix, all 459 params are bit-identical to a fresh start. Without the injected delay both pass: the window normally depends on host latency.

---

commits.pr_title: [Kernel][XPU] Mamba2 SSD: tensor-descriptor path for _chunk_scan_fwd_kernel and _chunk_state_fwd_kernel
commits.pr_body:
### Purpose

Mamba2 SSD prefill spends most of its SSD time in `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel` and `_chunk_state_fwd_kernel`. Both load and store 2D tiles with masked pointer arithmetic. This PR adds a tensor-descriptor (TD) path to both behind a `USE_TD` constexpr: on Intel XPU the descriptors lower to 2D block IO, and the path is on by default there. Elsewhere it is opt-in with `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=1` (TMA on sm90+). With TD off the generated code is unchanged.

Co-author: @mfylcek; work initiated by Marceli.

No open PR adds a tensor-descriptor path to these kernels (searched open and merged PRs for SSD and tensor descriptor); earlier single-kernel attempts #47084 and #45816 were closed.

### Changes

- **Kernels:** tiles go through `tl.make_tensor_descriptor` (zero padding replaces the load masks, outputs are stored through descriptors). When a sequence has no initial state, the TD branch skips the `prev_states` dot. `USE_TD` is part of both autotune keys.
- **Guard:** `vllm.triton_utils.tensor_descriptor_compatible` sends a launch down the pointer path when an operand cannot back a descriptor: non-unit inner stride, base not 16 B aligned, last-dim width under 64 B or not a 16 B multiple, outer pitch under max(64 B, width) or not a 16 B multiple. The 64 B rule is the Intel 2D block IO minimum; narrower operands (for example `head_dim=8`) abort under `TRITON_INTEL_2DBLOCK_ASSERT=1`.
- **Tests / CI:** TD tests are added to `tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` (`-k ssd_td`, 37 tests): TD vs pointer path with identical pinned tiles, guard fallbacks, TD vs the torch reference, and a launch spy that asserts which path ran. An Intel step runs them; the CUDA mamba step also depends on the TD helper files.

### Results

> **Reproducing these results requires #60800** (SSD autotune warmup on up to 32 chunks instead of one). The kernels are autotuned on the first call and the tile picked there is reused for every later prefill; with the one-chunk warmup a start can lock in a slow tile, so numbers vary from start to start (main's most of all). That PR has the evidence.

**Kernel level**, time per call with the best tile of each side (all tiles timed, median of 3 reps), Arc Pro B60 and B70:

| kernel | Nano-4B 4x2048, B60 | Nano-4B cases, B70 | geomean over 20 realistic cases, B60 | geomean over 20 realistic cases, B70 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel` | 7186 -> 3467 us (**2.07x**) | **2.26x** | **2.10x** | **1.78x** |
| `_chunk_state_fwd_kernel` | 1993 -> 1092 us (**1.82x**) | **1.57x** | 1.25x | 1.15x |

The 20 cases are 4 model shapes (Nemotron-3-Nano-4B, Falcon-H1-0.5B, Nemotron-3-Ultra TP=8 per-card shape, a synthetic dstate=256 shape) x 5 batch shapes.

Nemotron-3-Nano-4B-BF16, TP=1, seed 42, prefix caching off, Triton 3.8.0, `vllm bench latency --output-len 1` (prefill). Every sample is a separate process (B70: one container per sample) with its own autotune results, which are cached on disk; main and PR interleaved, warm-up discarded. On B70 compiled Triton binaries were reused between samples, autotune results never.

| platform | input x batch | main | PR | delta | samples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Arc Pro B60 | 2048 x 4 | 905 ms (902-910) | 828 ms (821-832) | -8.5% (-7.9 ... -9.6%) | 9, all faster |
| Arc Pro B60 | 8192 x 1 | 935 ms | 862 ms | -7.8% (-7.6 ... -8.1%) | 3, all faster |
| Arc Pro B60 | 128 x 1 | 38.2 ms | 36.2 ms | -5.3% | 2, all faster |
| Arc Pro B70 | 2048 x 4 | 658-835 ms | 587-590 ms | -18.7% (-10.4 ... -29.6%) | 7, all faster |
| Arc Pro B70 | 8192 x 1 | 708-738 ms | 607-611 ms | -15.7% (-13.7 ... -17.7%) | 2, all faster |
| Arc Pro B70 | 128 x 1 | 32-34 ms | 33-34 ms | -1.5%, +4.8% | 2, mixed |

On B70 main's own time varies between samples (658-835 ms at 4x2048) because of the first-call tile choice (see Notes). Against main with the same warmup change the gain of this PR is -8.3 ... -9.4% at 4x2048 (7 samples) and -8.4 ... -8.9% at 1x8192 (2 samples). At 128 tokens the PR is not a win on B70: 3-8% (1-3 ms) slower than main with that change.

`vllm bench serve` (random 2048/128, 200 prompts, concurrency 16), main vs PR with the warmup change:

| platform | mean TTFT | p99 TTFT | TPOT | output tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Arc Pro B60 | -12.1% | -11.9% | -4.9% | +6.0% |
| Arc Pro B70 (3 reps) | -23.6% | -22.8% | -11.0% | +14.6% |

On B70 main's throughput varies by 8% between server starts (331-359 tok/s) because of the first-call tile choice (see Notes), the PR's by 1%; the per-rep gain is +9.8% to +18.7%. In the B70 serve runs the warmup sequence is 8 chunks (`max_num_batched_tokens` 2048).

gsm8k 5-shot (full set, 1319), `lm_eval --model vllm`, Nemotron-3-Nano-4B, main vs PR:

| platform | flexible-extract | strict-match |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Arc Pro B60 | 0.8476 vs 0.8476 (stderr 0.0099) | 0.8453 vs 0.8461 |
| Arc Pro B70 | 0.8484 vs 0.8476 (stderr 0.0099) | 0.8461 vs 0.8431 |

The kernel speedups above are larger than the end-to-end ones because the SSD kernels are only part of the prefill. Most of the scan gain is the skipped `prev_states` dot (TD without the skip: 1.18x). State is shape dependent: on Falcon-H1-0.5B the best state tile with TD is 1.04-1.13x slower than main's best, so the end-to-end numbers are the claim.

A launch spy confirmed `USE_TD=True` for every launch of both kernels on the PR and `False` on main. With TD off (CUDA default), TTGIR and PTX of every autotune config of both kernels (69 scan / 28 state variants) are identical to main on H200 NVL and B200, and the autotune config lists are unchanged.

### Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py -k ssd_td                # the Intel CI step
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py                          # TD on (XPU default) / off (CUDA default)
VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=1 pytest -v -s tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py     # CUDA, TD forced
vllm bench latency --model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-4B-BF16 --input-len 2048 --output-len 1 --batch-size 4 \
  --num-iters-warmup 3 --num-iters 15 --max-model-len 2304 --no-enable-prefix-caching --seed 42
lm_eval --model vllm --model_args pretrained=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-4B-BF16,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=4096,seed=42,enable_prefix_caching=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto --seed 42
```

### Test Result

| | Arc Pro B60 | B200 | H200 NVL / H200 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-k ssd_td` (37 tests) | 37/37 (263 s cold) | not re-run (34/34 before the sm90 pin fix) | 34 passed, 3 skipped (45 s / 41 s, TD forced) |
| full file, TD on | 128/128 | 128/128 (forced) | 128/128 (forced) |
| full file, TD off | 128/128 | 128/128 | 128/128 |

The 3 sm90 skips are tile cases whose pinned chunk-scan config sm90 drops (#61718); their `-sm90` variants run. The full-file rows (128 tests) predate the sm90 pin fix, which only changes `-k ssd_td` tests.

### Notes

- Part of the tensor-descriptor work under RFC #42545, gated by the shared `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` (auto on for XPU, opt-in elsewhere).
- Earlier single-kernel SSD TD attempts were closed for flat end-to-end results: #47084 (`_bmm_chunk_fwd`) and #45816 (`_chunk_cumsum_fwd`).
- Depends on #60800 for stable, reproducible autotune picks (see the note at the top of Results). Without it a start can pick a slow tile, with or without TD.
- On CUDA and ROCm the opt-in path is validated by unit tests only (CUDA sm90/sm100); there is no accuracy or end-to-end measurement there, and ROCm is untested.
- Overlaps #58592, which splits the CUDA mamba kernel CI step and moves `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py`; whichever lands second rebases.
- AI assistance (Claude) was used for parts of this change, the tests and the measurements. All results come from runs on the hardware listed above.

commits.pr_title: [Fast Start] Add weights mirror support for daemon2daemon
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add daemon-to-daemon weight seeding to the preload stack: a second replica's daemons fill their shards from an already-loaded replica instead of reading the checkpoint again. Builds on the D2D transport from #63088 and adopts the storage-manifest + mover data plane proposed in #60086, reworked so a mirror is an ordinary daemon using a new internal `peer_cache` load format rather than a special tensor-bag daemon.

## Claims

- One new flag: `vllm preload --weight-cache-seed <source>`. Same-host copies go over CUDA IPC (`peer_ipc`), cross-host pulls go over Mooncake RDMA (`rdma`); the backend and the mirror's GPU placement are inferred, no other flags needed.
- A mirror is a normal daemon: it builds its model (meta device), finalizes its config, adopts the FlashInfer autotune table through the ordinary warmup-cache seeding, and serves engines identically — so chained seeding (a mirror seeding another replica, e.g. for failure recovery) needs no special code.
- Fingerprints (`WeightCacheKey`) are compared before any bytes move; a mismatched source/rank pairing is refused, not silently mirrored.
- 502 GiB of DSv4.1-Flash weights move between two nodes in ~9.3s (~54 GiB/s aggregate over 4 RoCE NICs).
- The remote control plane is JSON-only and authenticates before decoding (no pickle from untrusted peers); node-local movers are never served remotely.

## Validation

Startup performance on GB200 (SM100) nodes, `batch` partition; reproduction: `.slurm-logs/d2d_dsv41.sh` / `d2d_qwen30b.sh` / `d2d_xhost2.sh`.

| Startup path | Model / config | Time to READY | Transfer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cold preload (disk) | Qwen3-30B-A3B, tp=4 | 230s | — |
| **D2D seed** | Qwen3-30B-A3B, tp=4 | **100s** (2.3x faster) | 18.75 GiB/rank in 2.19s (~34 GiB/s aggregate, rdma) |
| Cold preload (first ever) | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, tp=4 | 1152s (651s with warm kernel caches) | — |
| **D2D seed** | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, tp=4 | transfer done at +9.3s* | 125.53 GiB/rank (~13.5 GiB/s/rank, ~54 GiB/s aggregate, rdma) |
| Cold preload | tiny kimi-k3, tp=1 | 58s | — |
| **D2D seed (same host)** | tiny kimi-k3, tp=1 | 60s | 0.12 GiB in 0.25s (peer_ipc) |

\* DSv4.1's mirror cannot reach READY yet: `DeepGemmMxfp8BmmLinearKernel` does not declare pre-processed-weight support (`modelopt.py`), the same gap the ModelOpt weight-cache series (#63754, #63976, #63672) addresses. The DSv4.1 numbers validate the data plane; Qwen3-30B validates the full loop.

Warm engine restarts against a daemon (`--load-format ipc_cache`) are unchanged by this PR and not separately instrumented here; the E2E tests assert correctness of the whole path instead (see below).

Tests: `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py`

- New E2E, run on GB200 (Slurm jobs 40933/40975): `test_d2d_weight_seeding_same_host` and `test_d2d_weight_seeding_cross_host` — a mirror daemon seeds over peer_ipc / rdma with `fallback=False` and serves outputs byte-identical to the disk baseline. Cross-host needs `WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM=0` (dmabuf) on hosts without a working nvidia-peermem module.
- Full file + `pre-commit run` (incl. mypy): green. The two GPU failures in the file (`kimi-k3` autotune-table assertion, `tp2_ep` nvcc ICE) reproduce identically on upstream/main.
- Correctness of served weights: Qwen3-30B-A3B served from the source replica and from the mirror replica produce byte-identical greedy outputs (2 nodes, tp=4).

AI assistance was used (Kimi Code); the subsections above list the exact validation commands and measured evidence.

## Details

Design, and how it differs from #60086:

- **Mirror lifecycle**: #60086's mirror holds a bare `MirrorState` (no model, no world group, no warmup, autotune table carried in the seed payload). Here the mirror is a normal daemon whose `load_format` is `peer_cache`: `PeerModelLoader` pulls the post-processed tensors and installs them through `build_model_from_processed_weights`, the same meta-device install pipeline engines use for `ipc_cache`. Config finalization, warmup, and serving need zero mirror-specific code, and future warmup-cache kinds work on mirrors without changes. The price: a mirror forms its own world group and needs the model's config files locally (not its safetensors).
- **Control plane**: one kind-keyed `SeedTransport` serves both `weights` and `flashinfer_autotune`. Same-host peers are served over the daemon's owner-verified Unix socket (pickle, which CUDA IPC handles require); remote peers over the token-authenticated TCP JSON listener. The peer loader fetches through the daemon's own D2D endpoint (injected at load), so there is exactly one configured channel per daemon.
- **Data plane** (as in #60086): storages move, not tensors — the manifest describes each tensor as a view over its storage so shared allocations (e.g. MLA's `W_UV`/`W_UK_T`) are copied once and keep their aliasing and footprint. `peer_ipc` verifies the source GPU by UUID before opening a handle; `rdma` registers each storage once and serves any number of mirrors.
- **Placement**: a same-host mirror must see the source's GPUs at their indices (CUDA IPC physics); the launcher learns the source's GPU UUIDs from its sockets and places the mirror's ranks on the remaining GPUs — no `--device-offset`-style flag.
- **Limitations / follow-ups**: single source per replica (multi-source fan-in is a natural next step); no bandwidth throttling; Mooncake required cross-host; mirror bring-up still pays world-group setup and meta-model construction (pipelining the copy with the meta build is a planned optimization); DSv4.1-class models additionally need per-rank host tables shipped out-of-band (they exceed `MAX_MSG_SIZE`).

Relationship to #60086: this is not a duplicate — it adopts that PR's data plane but reworks the mirror lifecycle and control-plane integration onto the current daemon framework (see Details). Happy to rebase/split if maintainers prefer landing the data plane first.

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The Python multimodal preprocessing path for GLM-5.3-Flash was adapted from GLM-4.6V and diverges from the model’s official preprocessing pipeline.

The Rust frontend already implements preprocessing aligned with the official pipeline. This PR removes the non-aligned Python path and requires Rust for image and video preprocessing, giving GLM-5.3-Flash a single supported implementation.

## Claims

- Remove the Python media processor and video timestamp sampler, and require the Rust frontend for multimodal initialization.
- Retain synthetic encoder profiling inputs and support Python text-only inference with image and video limits set to zero.

## Validation

Verified commit `b32bbd885d`, after merging main at `865cf8c1f2`, on two NVIDIA B200 GPUs with the GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint, TP=2, 16K context, and at most four concurrent sequences. Rust startup completed with normal profiling and kernel warmup. Greedy functional requests passed before and after the merge:

| Request | Result | HTTP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text: 2 + 2 | `4` | 200 |
| 512×256 red image | `Red` | 200 |
| 4032×3024 red image | `Red`, 7957 prompt tokens | 200 |
| Four-second red → blue video | Correct chronological order | 200 |

These four cases are functional smoke checks; full-context capacity and benchmark accuracy were not evaluated.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_glm5next.py \
  tests/models/glm5next/test_epd_metadata.py -v
# 13 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  'tests/models/test_initialization.py::test_can_initialize_large_subset[Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration]' -v
# 1 passed
```

The 100-token synthetic video profiling case failed before the fix with `max_pixels=156800 is too small. At least 158368 pixels are required for one aligned patch.`, then passed afterward. Ruff, mypy, documentation lint, CI test tethering, and all other applicable pre-commit checks passed. Initialization was run in a separate process, as in CI; a combined invocation stalled in the existing OpenMP cleanup after a fork.

## Details

The Python engine still needs encoder budgets and profiling inputs during startup. Those inputs are now synthetic patch tensors; real image and video preprocessing is performed by Rust. Serve multimodal requests with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`; selecting `--tokenizer-mode glm5_next` alone does not enable Rust. Python text-only deployments must set image and video limits to zero.

Duplicate-work checks found related PRs [#55727](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55727), which bounds video sampling parameters, and [#65757](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65757), which tests tokenizer parity. No other open PR implements this processor removal and Rust requirement.

AI assistance was used to prepare the code, validation, and description.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Support sequence parallelism with pipeline parallelism for Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5 and DeepSeek-V2/V3
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enable sequence-parallel MoE (SP) with pipeline parallelism (PP) for Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, and models using `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer`: DeepSeek-V3/R1, Kimi-K2, DeepSeek-V2, Mistral Large 3, and the DeepSeek MTP drafter.

With DP > 1, TP > 1, and EP, these models keep token shards on each TP rank between layers. They currently disable this optimization under PP because the next stage expects full-token tensors replicated across TP ranks. This PR restores that layout with an all-gather at each non-last stage's exit, then re-shards where needed in the next stage, following DeepSeek-V4 (#65766) and MiniMax-M3 (#65537).

Credit to @AceCoder0 for first enabling this combination in #53191 (last updated 2026-08-21). This PR also covers `vllm/models/qwen3_5/nvidia/model.py` and keeps SP enabled for small batches. #53191 added a small-batch all-reduce fallback for Qwen3-Next after observing NaNs on Ascend; on CUDA, Qwen3-Next and Qwen3.5 match the SP-off baseline in concurrency-1 GSM8K without that fallback.

## Claims

- Enable SP under PP for Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, and DeepSeek-V2/V3 with DP > 1, TP > 1, and EP.
- GSM8K scores are within run-to-run noise of PP1 with SP. Prompt-logprob differences from PP1 are no larger than those of PP2 on main.
- Qwen3.5 throughput is comparable to main. DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Qwen3-Next decode throughput is about 4% lower than main; DeepSeek-V2-Lite shows a similar SP decode cost at PP1, so PP now has the same trade-off as PP1.
- Qwen3.5 MTP under PP with SP achieves comparable GSM8K accuracy and acceptance length to PP1 with SP.
- PP1 behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

B300, TP2 × DP2 + EP with `allgather_reducescatter`, which enables SP wherever the model allows it. PP1 uses 4 GPUs; PP2 uses 8. Models: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1`, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` (`--language-model-only`), `Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat`.

**GSM8K.** Each cell reports concurrency 64 / concurrency 1: all 1319 questions at concurrency 64, and the first 100 at concurrency 1.

| Model | PP1, SP on | PP2, main (SP off) | PP2, this PR (SP on) |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-R1 | 0.951 / – | 0.955 / – | 0.953 / – |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | 0.860 / 0.900 | 0.845 / 0.890 | 0.851 / 0.890 |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B | 0.859 / 0.870 | 0.856 / 0.880 | 0.860 / 0.880 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | 0.635 / 0.630 | 0.649 / 0.690 | 0.635 / 0.630 |

DeepSeek-R1 was tested only at concurrency 64. A DeepSeek-V2-Lite rerun on the first 200 questions at concurrency 1 scored 0.645 at PP1 with SP and 0.660 at PP2 on main, a difference of less than one standard error (about 0.034).

**Prompt logprobs.** Six fixed prompts, scored twice per server through `/v1/completions` with `prompt_logprobs: 0`. Values are mean |Δ logprob| relative to the first PP1 run:

| Model (positions) | PP1, SP on, second run | PP2, main (SP off) | PP2, this PR (SP on) |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-R1 (412) | 0.0349 | 0.0894, 0.0743 | 0.0643, 0.0541 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (438) | 0.0098 | 0.0233, 0.0184 | 0.0035, 0.0233 |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B (432) | 0.0436 | 0.0503, 0.0513 | 0.0388, 0.0499 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite (460) | 0.0011 | 0.0405, 0.0419 | 0.0287, 0.0262 |

For Qwen3.5, the second PP2 run with this PR is byte-identical to the first PP2 run on main.

**Throughput.** Output tok/s at PP2 × TP2 × DP2, with runs interleaved as main → this PR → main → this PR:

| Model | Workload (in/out, concurrency) | main (SP off) | This PR (SP on) |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | decode 512/512, c64 | 6979, 7381 | 6728, 7088 |
| | mixed 2048/256, c64 | 6906, 7100 | 7141, 6407 |
| | prefill 8192/16, c8 | 347.3, 340.2 | 339.3, 340.1 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | decode 512/512, c64 | 5517 | 5650, 5608 |
| | mixed 2048/256, c64 | 6129 | 6335, 6132 |
| | prefill 8192/16, c8 | 271.4 | 277.6, 286.1 |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B | decode 512/512, c64 | 5081, 5051 | 4830, 4870 |
| | mixed 2048/256, c64 | 5519, 5382 | 5319, 5424 |
| | prefill 8192/16, c8 | 190.7, 194.9 | 199.2, 210.4 |

The second Qwen3.5 main run failed to start because the DP coordinator timed out; it was not repeated.

**SP at PP1.** DeepSeek-V2-Lite output tok/s at PP1 × TP2 × DP2, with SP-off and SP-on runs interleaved. SP was disabled through a local edit to the decoder-layer gate:

| Workload | SP off | SP on |
|---|---|---|
| decode 512/512, c64 | 10520, 10612 | 10131, 10087 |
| mixed 2048/256, c64 | 8355, 8217 | 8015, 7952 |

**MTP speculative decoding.** `{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 2}`, tested on all 1319 GSM8K questions at concurrency 64. Acceptance metrics come from the spec-decode counters over each GSM8K run:

| Model | Config | GSM8K | Acceptance rate | Mean acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | PP1, SP on | 0.851 | 0.888 | 2.777 |
| | PP2, this PR (SP on) | 0.853 | 0.890 | 2.779 |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B | PP1, SP on | 0.859 | 0.877 | 2.755 |

Qwen3-Next MTP fails to start under PP on both main and this PR: the drafter branches on PP rank and fails `assert intermediate_tensors is not None` on the last stage. #66063 fixes this.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 2
# The other models use the same flags; Qwen3.5 adds --language-model-only.
# PP1 rows drop --pipeline-parallel-size.
# MTP rows add --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 2}'.

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 1 --num-questions 100

vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 512 \
  --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos --seed 1

curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "...", "prompt": "...", "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0, "prompt_logprobs": 0}'
```
</details>

## Details

PP transport sends a 1/TP slice of each `IntermediateTensors` entry from each TP rank and reconstructs it with an all-gather on the receiving stage. Stage outputs therefore need to cover all tokens and be identical across TP ranks.

- Remove `pipeline_parallel_size == 1` from the SP gates in Qwen3-Next's `_should_use_sequence_parallel`, both Qwen3.5 decoder implementations, and `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer`.
- At each non-last stage's exit, concatenate `hidden_states` and `residual`, all-gather once, trim token padding, and split them back.
- On non-first stages, Qwen3-Next and Qwen3.5 shard the received `residual` alongside `hidden_states`. DeepSeek-V2's first SP layer already shards a full `residual`.
- DeepSeek-V2 uses the last local layer's SP flag to decide whether to gather at the stage exit. Row counts are ambiguous for a one-token batch, whose shard also has one row. #50691 replaces the existing intra-stage shape checks with explicit layout tracking.
- Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next MTP reuse these decoder layers and inherit SP enablement under PP.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, implement and validate this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3.1] MiniMax-M3.1-Flash Specialized Decode: CuTe DSL Optimized GB300 (up to 1.45x)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This PR adds an NVIDIA-developed specialized decode for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash on GB300, for the small decode batches that agentic and interactive serving run. It supports:
- one GB300 tray at TP4 (GB200 / B200 also run it);
- no speculation, or DSpark speculative decoding with up to 7 draft tokens;
- FULL-graph decode steps of up to 64 rows (8 requests × (K + 1) tokens). Prefill, mixed batches and larger batches fall back to the stock forward.

It is opt-in via `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'`, the same switch as #61867 and #61868. With the default (`auto`), the model runs exactly as on upstream `main`. Every kernel is CuTe DSL (`nvidia-cutlass-dsl`, already a vLLM dependency), compiled for the live device at warm-up; nothing is added to `setup.py` or CMake.

All changes are under `vllm/models/` (`minimax_m3/nvidia/` and the DSpark draft model in `minimax_m3/common/dspark.py`); the model runner, the CUDA graph manager, the attention backends and the DSpark speculator are unchanged.

The integration follows #61867 and #61868: the model owns a decode executor that takes over FULL-graph decode steps. The model itself was added in #64111.

## Claims

MiniMax-M3.1-Flash on one GB300 tray (TP4) with DSpark K = 7, the same build with the switch on and off:
- Decode step on this head: **32–33% faster at c = 1** (6.99 → 4.76 ms at 8K context, 6.90 → 4.61 ms at 128K), 7–18% faster at c = 2–8 (1.08x–1.22x).
- InferenceX AgentX traces, measured on an earlier revision of this branch (see Performance): **p90 interactivity 1.45x at c = 1** (550 → 799 tok/s/user), 1.23x at c = 4 and 1.28x at c = 8. That is above the InferenceX GB300 references at each of these concurrencies.
- GSM8K, GPQA-Diamond, AIME26 and RULER NIAH (32K–256K) match the switch-off model within one standard error, and the DSpark acceptance length does not change.

## Validation

### Correctness

The reference is the same build with the switch off. Both arms run TP4 with fp8 KV and fp8 index caches, DSpark K = 7 with probabilistic drafting and lossless block verification (real acceptance), `--max-num-seqs 8` and `--max-model-len 1048576`. The bar for each row is |on − off| ≤ max(1 SE of the switch-off score, 1 point).

All 15 score rows and all 7 acceptance-length rows pass.

</details>

This PR is based on `main` at `308a3253c` (2026-11-07). These evals ran on earlier bases (`2b009fc6d`) and are being re-run on this head, switch on and off; see "Since these measurements". Since they ran, this PR's own code changed only in license headers, type-checking fixes, the removal of test-only and debug code, and the rebase.

Kernel-level tests (each kernel against a float64 reference or the stock op it replaces, the TP4 boundary exchange under graph replay, each kernel stage against its stock stage on real weights, and a five-layer model served with the switch on and off) were run on 4× GB300, but they are kept out of this PR to keep it reviewable and can follow in a separate PR with a CI step. Those runs were on a revision that also carried the test harness and debug code this PR leaves out; GPU re-validation of this head is pending (see "Since these measurements").

### Performance

All runs use MiniMax-M3.1-Flash on one GB300 tray (TP4) with fp8 KV and fp8 index-K caches, the checkpoint's MXFP8 / NVFP4 weights, Model Runner V2 with async scheduling, FULL CUDA graphs for decode and DSpark K = 7. Both arms force the acceptance length to 4.04 (synthetic rejection), so they verify the same number of tokens per step. The switch-off arm is the same build with `decode_backend=auto`.

**AgentX** (InferenceX's agentic coding traces, closed loop at fixed concurrency, 20 minutes per cell; the switch-off c = 1 cell ran 60 minutes). Interactivity is 1 / per-request ITL. AgentX was measured on an earlier revision of this branch on `main` at `2b009fc6d` (see "Since these measurements"); the decode-step table below is on this head.

**Decode step** on an earlier revision of this PR (`main` at `463e23b1d`, real weights; being re-run on `308a3253c`). Steady-state step p50 over 256 decode tokens; every server was booted twice in mirrored order, and each cell is the mean of the two runs. The switch-off column carries about ±5% run-to-run noise.

| 8K | 1 | 8 | 6.99 | **4.76** | −32% (1.47x) |
| 8K | 2 | 16 | 8.00 | **6.54** | −18% (1.22x) |
| 8K | 4 | 32 | 9.79 | **8.22** | −16% (1.19x) |
| 8K | 8 | 64 | 12.31 | **10.80** | −12% (1.14x) |
| 128K | 1 | 8 | 6.90 | **4.61** | −33% (1.50x) |
| 128K | 2 | 16 | 7.64 | **6.41** | −16% (1.19x) |
| 128K | 4 | 32 | 9.99 | **8.57** | −14% (1.17x) |
| 128K | 8 | 64 | 12.70 | **11.80** | −7% (1.08x) |

**Long-context multi-request steps** next to a 524K-token request (step p50, ms), without and with the split-row page top-k and the pre-wait sparse decode:

| Batch | Without | With | Saving |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 524K + 16K (16 rows) | 8.36 | 8.04 | 0.32 ms |
| 524K + 3 × 16K (32 rows) | 10.65 | 9.97 | 0.68 ms |
| 524K + 7 × 64K (64 rows) | 12.46 | 12.04 | 0.42 ms |

<details><summary>Since these measurements</summary>

The AgentX numbers, the long-context steps and the evals ran on `main` at `2b009fc6d`. The AgentX numbers come from an earlier revision of this branch with the same executor and fused kernels, before they were ported to CuTe DSL; each CuTe DSL kernel is bit-identical to its predecessor on the same inputs. Decode-step comparison on real weights on that base:
- CuTe DSL build vs the earlier build: mean ratio 0.985. At 128K c = 1 the CuTe DSL build is 4.0% slower (4.836 vs 4.652 ms); under nsys both take the same GPU time per step (5.05 vs 5.06 ms) with identical launches and PDL overlap.
- This PR's kernel and runtime code vs the first CuTe DSL build: 1.002 / 0.982 / 0.992 / 1.035 at 8K and 0.994 / 0.951 / 1.006 / 0.953 at 128K (c = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8), mean 0.989, acceptance length 4.03–4.06 in both.

After the rebase onto `main` at `463e23b1d`, the rebased build (before the debug code was left out) against the pre-rebase build (in one job, mirrored boot order): mean step ratio 1.003, from 0.96 (128K c = 1) to 1.04 (8K c = 1, 128K c = 8). The rebased runs used vLLM's precompiled binaries for `463e23b1d` on a CUDA 13.4 aarch64 image whose PyTorch (2.16 nightly) is newer than the wheel's pin; every compiled extension imported and ran.

GPU re-validation of this head is pending. Leaving out the test harness and debug code changed the `o_proj` and front kernel signatures (debug pointer arguments and their compile-time-off or null-pointer branches are gone), so the numbers above are from the earlier build until the decode-step comparison, the correctness evals' smoke subset and the kernel tests are re-run on it.

The measured builds also carried three Model Runner V2 opt-ins that this PR leaves to a follow-up (a fused upload of the per-step inputs, the FLASHINFER_TS draft metadata refreshed inside the drafter's FULL graph, and the aux hidden states written straight into the drafter's staging). They save about 30–40 µs per step, about 0.7% of the step at c = 1, so this PR alone is expected to be that much slower than the decode-step and AgentX numbers above until the follow-up lands.

This PR is now based on `main` at `308a3253c`. Every number in this PR (evals, AgentX, decode step, long-context steps) was measured on the older bases above and is being re-run on this head, both arms. Upstream changes in between that touch the measured paths: MiniMax-M3.1 now reads the upstream Transformers `MiniMaxM3VLConfig` (#61813), and DSpark's stock Markov sampling fuses the Markov bias and the block combine into the Gumbel kernel (#64476), which changes the switch-off arm's drafter kernels. The ROCm-only DSpark drafter monokernel (#65386) does not run on NVIDIA.

</details>

<details><summary>Server command</summary>

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash -tp 4 --block-size 128 \
  --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager --async-scheduling \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "fp8"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "attention_backend": "FLASHINFER_TS", "kv_cache_dtype": "fp8", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic"}' \
  --additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'   # switch on only
```

- Performance runs add `"rejection_sample_method": "synthetic", "synthetic_acceptance_length": 4.04` to the speculative config; accuracy runs use `"rejection_sample_method": "block"`.
- The log shows `MiniMax-M3.1 specialized decode on, for FULL-graph decode steps of up to 64 rows`.

</details>

## Details

### What runs

In FULL-graph decode steps of up to 64 rows, the executor replaces the per-layer op chain of the sparse MoE layers (3–59) with fused kernels chained with programmatic dependent launch (PDL):

```text
qkv_front -> index_score -> page_topk -> sparse_decode -> o_proj (+ router CTAs)
  -> post (all-reduce + norm + NVFP4 + top-4 routes) -> fused NVFP4 MoE
  -> (push) next layer's qkv_front
```

- **QKV front**: lands the previous sublayer's TP all-reduce from a peer exchange, adds the residual, Gemma RMSNorm, MXFP8, the QKV / index-QK GEMV (tcgen05), per-head QK norm + RoPE, and the fp8 KV and index-K inserts, in one launch.
- **Index score** (upstream's CuTe DSL scorer with a different split), an **exact page top-k** that writes physical page ids, and an **fp8 sparse decode** on clusters that writes the `o_proj` input as MXFP8.
- **`o_proj` with router CTAs**, then the **post**: all-reduce + residual + norm + NVFP4 quantize of the FC1 input + top-4 routing in one kernel.
- A **fused NVFP4 MoE engine** (routed + shared experts) that reads vLLM's TRT-LLM-gen expert buffers in place and pushes its output into the next layer's front.
- The DSpark drafter keeps its stock model. With the switch on it samples its Markov chain in one kernel per position, fuses its norms with the next MXFP8 quantize, and reads both LM heads' logits through peer memory.

Which steps reach which kernels (rows = c × (K + 1)):

| Rows | front | index / top-k / sparse decode | `o_proj` | post + MoE |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1, 2, 4, 8 | kernel | kernel | kernel | kernel (fused engine) |
| 3, 5, 6, 7 | kernel | kernel | stock | stock |
| 9..16 | kernel | kernel | wide GEMV | stock |
| 17..64 | wide GEMV | kernel | wide GEMV | stock |

So at K = 7, c = 1 runs every kernel. At c = 2..8 the attention kernels and the wide GEMVs run, with the stock post-attention boundary and MoE: at 32–64 rows × top-4 most experts are hit, and the stock grouped GEMMs are near the HBM roofline there.

### vLLM integration

As in #61867 and #61868, the model owns a decode executor. With the switch on, the model returns its own model state, which builds the executor once the weights are loaded and compiles and warms up the kernels before memory profiling and CUDA graph capture. For each forward the model asks the executor for a step (`plan()`); it returns one only for a FULL CUDA graph capture of a pure decode step within the row cap, and the forward otherwise runs the stock layers. Within a step, each stage runs its kernel inside its envelope and its stock implementation otherwise, and paired stages fall back together. Every decision reads host state that all TP ranks share.

| Package (`vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/specialized_decode/`) | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `__init__.py` | The switch, `DecodeConfig`, row caps and `unsupported()` |
| `stages.py`, `stock.py` | One interface per stage slot, and every stage on the ops the stock layers run |
| `kernel_stages.py`, `kernels/` | The kernels behind the stage interfaces, their registry, and the collective fail-closed build |
| `drafter.py`, `draft_norm.py`, `peer_logits.py` | The DSpark drafter kernels |
| `runtime/` | The executor, its per-step plan, the model state and warm-up |
| `AGENTS.md` | Structure, dispatch and fallback, adding a kernel stage, serving |

**Rank lockstep.** The kernels exchange partials with their TP peers, so a rank that diverged would hang rather than fall back. `unsupported()` runs on every rank and the results are combined with a MIN all-reduce, so if any rank misses a requirement, every rank raises with the full list. The kernel build is collective and fails closed: the ranks agree after each build phase, and a stage that failed on any rank runs stock on every rank.

**With the switch off.** Nothing in the package runs. Outside the package:
- `nvidia/model.py`: the model defines its model state and builds the executor only with the switch on; `forward()` calls `plan()` only when an executor exists;
- `common/dspark.py`: the drafter kernels attach only with the switch on.

With the switch on, the executor hands the model runner and the DSpark speculator the same outputs as the stock forward (the final hidden states and one cloned `[rows, hidden]` aux hidden state per aux layer), and the drafter's FLASHINFER_TS metadata is built eagerly before each draft step, as for any model.

**Scope and requirements.** SM100 or SM103; Model Runner V2 with async scheduling; TP = 4 over the whole world, with no PP, DP, EP or CP and no micro-batching; no speculation or DSpark with at most 7 draft tokens and without adaptive verification; fp8 KV and fp8 index-K caches (NVFP4 and BF16 caches are refused); the checkpoint's MXFP8 / NVFP4 weights on the default TRT-LLM-gen MoE backend (not MegaMoE); block size 128 and at most 8,192 pages per request; FULL graphs for decode only; no `torch.compile` of the model, sleep mode, LoRA, KV transfer or batch invariance. Any other deployment raises at start-up on every rank and lists every missing requirement.

### Known limitations and follow-ups

- **fp8 KV and index-K caches only.** The kernels read and write fp8 (E4M3) caches and refuse NVFP4, the KV format the checkpoint was trained for (QAT) and the one the InferenceX recipes use. On GB200 TP4 that is a 3.66M-token KV pool against 6.55M with NVFP4. In InferenceX AgentX on GB200 (aggregated TP4), the pool keeps up through concurrency 12 (96–98% prefix-cache hits; p90 660, 437 and 375 tok/s/user at c = 1, 8 and 12). At concurrency 16 it evicts the cached prefixes of waiting sessions: 32.1M prompt tokens are recomputed against 11.3M with stock NVFP4, so the median leads stock (448 vs 413 tok/s/user) but p90 trails it (264 vs 292). CPU KV offload (`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`) is the stopgap; NVFP4 KV and index-K in the sparse decode and the index scorer are the follow-up, which would also halve the bytes those kernels read.
- **TP8** is a follow-up; `unsupported()` accepts TP4 only.
- **The fused post + MoE engine stops at 8 rows**, so the full kernel chain runs at c = 1 with K = 7 (see the table above).
- **Attention metadata** builds still run eagerly each step.
- **Capture sizes.** The executor derives its step rows from `cudagraph_capture_sizes`. It should move to the decode capture-shape helpers from #63406, as DeepSeek-V4.1's specialized decode did.
- **Co-residency check.** The post kernel's shared memory is dynamic, and `post/host.py` reports it as 0, so the co-residency check under-counts the post by at most 304 B. The current kernels still pass the check and run co-resident, but it should read the launch's shared memory, as the MoE host does.
- **Tests** are not part of this PR; they follow separately.
- **Model Runner V2 opt-ins** (fused input upload, in-graph FLASHINFER_TS draft metadata, aux hidden states into the drafter's staging): about 30–40 µs per step; separate PR.
- **Not run yet:** compute-sanitizer (memcheck / synccheck / racecheck).

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write, port and review this change, and the commit carries a `Co-Authored-By` trailer. The change is large (about 25.4k added lines, most of it kernel code), so careful human review of the kernels is requested.

commits.pr_title: [DeepSeek-V3.2] Support sequence parallelism with pipeline parallelism
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enable sequence parallelism (SP) with pipeline parallelism (PP) for DeepSeek-V3.2 on NVIDIA GPUs, fixing incorrect results on `main` when PP > 1, DP > 1, TP > 1, and expert parallelism (EP) are enabled.

Related: #62947 addresses a separate path in the same file: naive all2all with MoE SP disabled. That path also incorrectly scales the MoE output by the TP size.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V3.2 with PP > 1, DP > 1, TP > 1, and EP now uses the same SP path as PP = 1.
- GSM8K accuracy matches PP1 at 0.955, and mean NLL is comparable: 0.928 versus 0.932 at PP1. On `main`, this configuration yields GSM8K accuracy of 0.858 and mean NLL of 1.511.
- With one token per decode step (requests sent one at a time), PP2 produces the same tokens and logprobs as PP1. GSM8K at concurrency 1 is 0.970, versus 0.975 at PP1 (200 questions).
- MTP works at PP2 with this change.
- Behavior is unchanged for PP = 1 and for PP > 1 without DP-triggered SP.

## Validation

Validation used `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2` (FP8) on B300 GPUs with EP + TP2 + DP2 and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` CUDA graphs, except for the TP4 + DP1 control noted below. All configurations include #65554, which is required to start DeepSeek-V3.2 with PP in this setup.

**Prompt logprobs and GSM8K.** Prompt logprobs were compared against PP1 using six fixed prompts and 412 scored positions. GSM8K evaluation used 1319 questions with 5-shot prompting.

| Config | Mean \|Δ logprob\| vs PP1 | Max | Mean NLL | GSM8K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PP1 (SP on), reference | – | – | 0.9318 | 0.955 |
| PP2, main | 0.7551 | 8.04 | 1.5114 | 0.858 |
| PP2, this PR | 0.0178 | 0.58 | 0.9280 | 0.955 |

**Control.** With TP4 + DP1 (SP disabled throughout), the PP2-versus-PP1 comparison yields a mean \|Δ logprob\| of 0.0129 and identical mean NLL of 0.9262. This control indicates that the incorrect results on `main` depend on DP > 1.

**Single-request decode.** Requests were sent one at a time, so each decode step shards a single token across the TP ranks, with padding on the other rank. Six prompts generated 128 greedy tokens each; their decode logprobs were compared with the same sequences re-scored via `prompt_logprobs`. GSM8K used the first 200 questions at concurrency 1.

| Config | Decode vs re-scored mean / max \|Δ logprob\| | Output vs PP1 | GSM8K (200, concurrency 1) |
|---|---|---|---|
| PP1 (SP on), reference | 0.0344 / 0.67 | – | 0.975 |
| PP2, this PR | 0.0344 / 0.67 | Identical tokens and logprobs (6/6 prompts) | 0.970 |

**MTP** (k = 1):

| Config | GSM8K | Acceptance rate |
|---|---|---|
| PP1, main | 0.955 | 0.950 |
| PP2, this PR | 0.951 | 0.947 |

**Throughput at PP2**, measured in output tokens/s. Because `main` produces incorrect results in this configuration, these measurements are not a like-for-like baseline comparison.

| Workload (in/out, concurrency) | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| decode 512/512, c64 | 1874 | 1797 |
| mixed 2048/256, c64 | 1510 | 1447 |
| prefill 8192/16, c8 | 26.7 | 27.0 |

Pre-commit passed on the changed files. CI does not currently include a job that runs DeepSeek-V3.2 with both PP and DP; this configuration requires 8 GPUs and the full checkpoint. Validation of this path is therefore limited to the runs reported above.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2
# MTP arms add: --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}'

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 1 --num-questions 200

curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "...", "prompt": "...", "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0, "prompt_logprobs": 0}'

# Single-request decode: generate, then re-score prompt_token_ids + token_ids
# with "max_tokens": 1 and "prompt_logprobs": 0.
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "...", "prompt": "...", "max_tokens": 128, "temperature": 0,
       "logprobs": 0, "ignore_eos": true, "return_token_ids": true}'

vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 512 --num-prompts 256 \
  --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos --seed 1
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** DP > 1, together with TP > 1 and EP, enables MoE SP through `use_sequence_parallel_moe`. On `main`, `DeepseekV2MoE` reads this flag directly and continues to use SP under PP, while the decoder restricts SP to PP = 1 with `use_sequence_parallel = use_sequence_parallel_moe and pp == 1`.

The decoder constructs the MoE with `reduce_results=False` and normally performs the TP all-reduce in the next layer's `fused_allreduce_rms_norm`. With SP enabled, however, `DeepseekV2MoE.forward` partitions tokens across TP ranks, computes complete outputs for each rank's partition, and all-gathers them (`deepseek_v2.py`, `is_sequence_parallel`). Every rank therefore already holds the full, reduced output. Under PP, the decoder treats this output as an unreduced partial sum and all-reduces it again, causing the MoE contribution to be added to the residual stream TP times. Because the first three layers are dense, model quality degrades rather than the output becoming entirely nonsensical.

**Implementation.** Decoder SP now follows `use_sequence_parallel_moe` regardless of PP, keeping the decoder and MoE on the same SP path. The attention layer's SP flag, which all-gathers the A-projection outputs before the TP-split projections, follows the same setting; its row-count fallback cannot detect a one-token batch, which shards to one row per TP rank. PP communication requires full-token, TP-replicated tensors, so each non-last stage all-gathers the token shards in `hidden_states + residual` before returning. Subsequent stages already re-shard their input on entry. This follows the PP + SP handling in MiniMax-M3 and DeepSeek-V4.1.

**Alternative considered.** Disabling MoE SP under PP would also restore correct results, but would remove SP support for PP > 1.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, implement, and validate this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results. Codex was used to polish the PR description.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Align CPU offload latency-test prefixes with cache blocks
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Align the CPU-offload latency test's reusable prefix to the offload block size, leaving one token to recompute. Retain the original latency regression check and add exact cache-hit assertions.

Refs #67307 (CPU-offload item).

## Claims

- Preserve the original requirement that CPU hits beat cold recomputation in at least 8/10 trials.
- Require zero cached tokens on cold requests and complete prefix reuse on both GPU and CPU hits.
- Retain the existing async-store synchronization, stored-event checks, accuracy checks, and 4096-token engine context limit. No new skips or tolerance changes.

## Validation

Real-weight validation used base `730194d2362716c47648d06e172c91bcdace3b32`, its matching precompiled nightly, RTX 4090, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, and default compiled execution/CUDA Graphs. The FlashInfer sampler was disabled.

Falcon-H1 resolves its GPU/offload blocks to **832 tokens**. The old 4095-token input reused 3328 tokens and still recomputed a 767-token tail. The aligned 3329-token input reuses the **same 3328 tokens**, leaving one token to recompute.

A controlled comparison in one 4096-context engine (one warmup + ten measured trials per case) gave:

| Input / reused / recomputed tokens | CPU-hit wins | Median cold / CPU-hit latency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4095 / 3328 / 767 | 0/10 | 52.13 / 64.86 ms |
| 3329 / 3328 / 1 | 10/10 | 70.55 / 18.47 ms |

Increasing the context limit and testing 8191-, 10001-, and 16383-token inputs also gave 10/10 wins, but alignment resolves the reproduced failure without raising the existing context limit. These are end-to-end request timings, not isolated DMA measurements.

The actual updated tests passed:

| Case | Result | Average cold / CPU-hit latency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Falcon-H1, independent engine lifetime 1 | Pass; 3328-token GPU/CPU hits | 53.22 / 16.40 ms |
| Falcon-H1, independent engine lifetime 2 | Pass; 3328-token GPU/CPU hits | 63.00 / 16.48 ms |
| Mamba-130M | Pass; 4032-token GPU/CPU hits | 38.21 / 13.86 ms |
| Negative control: reset CPU cache as well | Expected failure: `0 == 3328` at the full CPU-hit assertion | — |

Both native model tests include the unchanged accuracy check.

Supplemental real Qwen3-1.7B checks of the shared helper also passed with CPUOffloadingSpec and TieringOffloadingSpec's example/fs secondary-tier configurations (1 GiB CPU cache, 192-token chunks). All three reused the complete 4032-token prefix and retained the same 8/10 latency requirement. Another GPU job started during this supplemental run, so these cases are used only as cache-hit compatibility coverage, not as isolated latency evidence. These helper checks do not replace native Llama/Gemma coverage.

Ruff check/format and `git diff --check` pass. The full pre-commit suite was not run in the GPU environment because Git is unavailable there.

<details>
<summary>Commands and relevant raw output</summary>

From the source checkout, with real model weights in a task-local Hugging Face cache:

```bash
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
export HF_HUB_CACHE=/home/xd/inference-perf-lab/cpu-offload-67307-20261115/hf-cache
export TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0
PYTHON=../.venv/bin/python

# Run in two independent processes.
"$PYTHON" -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py \
  -k 'test_cpu_offloading and Falcon' -v -s --junitxml=../runs/review-r1/falcon-1.xml
"$PYTHON" -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py \
  -k 'test_cpu_offloading and Falcon' -v -s --junitxml=../runs/review-r1/falcon-2.xml

"$PYTHON" -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py \
  -k 'test_cpu_offloading and mamba-130m' -v -s --junitxml=../runs/review-r1/mamba.xml

"$PYTHON" -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_review_negative.py \
  -k 'test_cpu_offloading and Falcon' -v -s --junitxml=../runs/review-r1/negative.xml

"$PYTHON" -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_plain_attention_probe.py \
  -v -s --junitxml=../runs/review-r1/plain-attention.xml
```

The negative-control and plain-attention probe files are validation-only files, not PR additions. The negative control differs from the updated native test only by passing `reset_connector=True` to the GPU-cache reset inside `_latency_test`. The Qwen probe creates real LLM/connector instances for the three configurations above and invokes the actual shared `_latency_test`; it does not substitute a checkpoint into the existing Llama parametrizations.

```text
# Falcon-H1, lifetime 1
Reusable prefix length: 3328
Average times:
    Cold: 53.22ms
    GPU hit: 8.00ms
    CPU hit: 16.40ms
================= 1 passed, 14 deselected in 99.92s (0:01:39) ==================

# Falcon-H1, lifetime 2
Reusable prefix length: 3328
    Cold: 63.00ms
    CPU hit: 16.48ms
====================== 1 passed, 14 deselected in 28.62s =======================

# Mamba-130M
Reusable prefix length: 4032
    Cold: 38.21ms
    CPU hit: 13.86ms

# CPU-cache-clear control
>           assert cpu_hit.num_cached_tokens == prefix_len
E           AssertionError: assert 0 == 3328

# Additional Qwen helper checks: CPU / example / fs
======================== 3 passed in 132.19s (0:02:12) =========================
```

The controlled length/alignment probes use the same real engine and request path, record each request's latency and cached-token count, and preserve all warmup and measured rows. Worker metadata was read outside the timing windows through a process-local collective RPC; pickle serialization was enabled only for those diagnostic probes, not for the updated test runs.

</details>

## Details

With an unaligned prefix, the cache-hit measurement includes a large uncached tail as well as offload transport. Its compute/dispatch path can leave too little advantage over cold prefill for the original timing assertion to be reliable.

The test now derives the reusable prefix length from the resolved GPU block size and offload chunk configuration, then appends one token for logits. Both hit paths must report exactly `prefix_len` cached tokens, so partial reuse fails. The relative-latency assertion remains unchanged. Timings use the monotonic `perf_counter`.

The diff changes only this test helper. H200 MIG and native Llama/Gemma cases still need CI validation; the 4090 results do not establish behavior on the failing MIG slice. The existing V1 KV Connectors CI step selects this directory and tracks it as a source dependency.
