commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Today, the SharedOffloadRegion opens the files in a hardcoded path. This PR makes it configurable.

## Claims

Add an optional, keyword-only mmap_path that sets where the region's files live, so processes outside one engine (e.g. pods sharing a host directory) can open the same region. The default path is unchanged. The creator's free-space check now uses the region's own directory.

This is required by llm-d's CPU Sharing mechanism, described in this RFC: https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/issues/3047

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Hy4] Enable sink-aware ShardQ prefill
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Enable HY4 sparse-MLA ShardQ prefill by gathering checkpoint-loaded attention sinks in TP head order. Reuse the existing token split, attention kernels and eligibility checks.

## Claims

- Enable token-sharded prefill for the target backbone with MTP3 enabled.
- On 8×H200, prefill-only throughput improves **59.10% at ISL8192** and **62.53% at ISL32768**, with OSL1 and saturated requests.
- Preserve sink values across CPU-staged loading, checkpoint reload and CUDA graph replay.

## Validation

PR source `25227c86327a0acf3e9d502286028df5db57000c` on frozen main `329f93e1909efdd4548524b1500fa2c54ef2cbb0`, rebuilt CUDA extensions, `tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8`, TP8/DP1/EP8, ModelOpt MXFP8, default Humming MoE, `fp8_ds_mla` KV and natural MTP3. Default graph mode, memory utilization and sequence limits, with `max_model_len=262144`.

Tested packages include `torch 2.14.0`, `triton 3.8.0`, `flashinfer-python 0.7.3`, `humming-kernels 0.1.19`.

Same-GPU serial A/B/A, three seeds per arm, warmups excluded and profiling in separate runs. Each run uses 128/32/16 requests at ISL2048/8192/32768, respectively, OSL1 and RPS∞. Means below pool the six main runs and three PR runs. Every request succeeded with the expected input/output token counts.

```bash
  --port 8254 --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 20 --max-concurrency 32 \
```


A separate greedy single-request check with 3596 input tokens produced the same next token and top-five token set, passing `check_logprobs_close(always_check_logprobs=True)`. Maximum absolute logprob difference among those five tokens was 0.5782.


### Regression tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/hy_v4/test_shardq_sinks.py -v -s
```

On main, the TP2 case fails at `assert layer.mla_attn.use_shardq == (world > 1)`. With this change, all three TP1/TP2/TP8 cases pass in 72.49 s. The TP2 case uses 32 total heads to exercise ShardQ on two-GPU CI and includes CPU-staged finalization, exact local/full sink values, padding, weight reload and graph replay. The TP8 case uses 64 total heads.

Pre-commit passed on all changed files. The existing two-H100 ShardQ Buildkite step selects TP1/TP2. TP8 was run manually on eight H200s.

### Profile

Matched three-second profiles at ISL8192/32768, OSL1, collected separately from throughput runs. The profile clients use N8/C4 at 8K and N4/C2 at 32K. All eight ranks show FlashMLA query rows decreasing from 8192 to 1024, with 64 kernel heads. The table gives rank 0 median GPU execution time per native FlashMLA invocation, summing its associated metadata/attention/combine kernels by profiler external ID. The E2E throughput results include the ShardQ exchanges.

| ISL | Main query shape | PR query shape | Main FlashMLA GPU time | PR FlashMLA GPU time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8192 | `[1,8192,64,576]` | `[1,1024,64,576]` | 6.706 ms | 0.858 ms |
| 32768 | `[1,8192,64,576]` | `[1,1024,64,576]` | 6.734 ms | 0.879 ms |

#### Main
[main-isl32768-rank0.pt.trace.json.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34846186/main-isl32768-rank0.pt.trace.json.gz)
#### Shardq
[shardq-isl32768-rank0.pt.trace.json.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34846188/shardq-isl32768-rank0.pt.trace.json.gz)


## Details

ShardQ computes all query heads for each rank's token slice, so HY4's learnable sink must follow the full-head layout during prefill. Gather it once during weight finalization on the TP execution device, and update the cache in place on reload to preserve graph references. Decode uses the local sink layout.

Throughput was measured before the loading-only CPU-staging fix and comment/log cleanup. The final production files were then revalidated with the real checkpoint, 20-shot GSM8K, matching profiles and the sink regression suite.

This extends the shared ShardQ machinery to HY4's model-local sink backend. The earlier norms/A-projection extension covers the DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.3 model package. [#66549](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66549)

Open-PR searches for HY4/Hy4 ShardQ found zero matching implementations. The open DSv4.1 sink/token-sharding extension and shared route-selection refactor cover separate changes.

commits.pr_title: [KV Offload] Rename the filtered group index to config_group_idx
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Rename the filtered group-config index in the KV offloading connector from `config_idx` to `config_group_idx`.

## Claims

- `config_group_idx` now names the position in `OffloadingConfig.groups` (the filtered `kv_group_configs`).
- `group_idx` keeps its current meaning: the `KVCacheConfig` group id. This covers `GroupOffloadConfig.group_idx`, the offload key, and the KV events.
- Behavior does not change. The diff renames variables only.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` passes on the commit.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector` gives 747 passed, 2 skipped, 12 failed.
- The same 12 tests fail on a clean `upstream/main` 5039f736e6: 6 `test_cache_reset_*` tests, 4 `test_lookahead_partial_lookup_uses_available_hashes` tests, and 2 `test_lookahead_partial_store_uses_checkpoint_hash` tests. They fail on this macOS host and are not related to the rename.

## Details

The offloading scheduler uses two group indices:

1. `group_idx`: the id in `KVCacheConfig.kv_cache_groups`.
2. `config_group_idx`: the position in the filtered offloading groups.

Some locals named `config_idx`, `grp_idx`, `idx`, or `group_idx` hold the second index. The names hide the difference between the two indices. This change gives the second index one name, `config_group_idx`, at every site in `scheduler.py`, `state.py`, and `store_triggers/`. The handoff loop in `on_handoff.py` keeps `group_idx` for the `KVCacheConfig` group id and maps it to `config_group_idx`.

The change is internal. It does not change user-visible behavior, so it needs no docs.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change. The human submitter must review every line and run the tests.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][GDN] Drop the prefill copies of the fused spec-decode path
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Remove redundant prefill buffer initialization and copies from the fused GDN spec-decode (MTP) path used by Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.

Merged [#64419](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64419) covered the non-MTP GDN path; this addresses the fused path it left behind. No open PR touches these copies.

## Claims

- Remove the output-buffer zero fill, gate reshape copy, and per-head norm-weight materialization.
- Eliminate 9.79 ms of copy/initialization work per step across 36 GDN layers at 16,384 padded tokens on B300.
- Preserve bit-identical gated RMSNorm output and warmup coverage for the fused layout.

## Validation

Validated on this branch with NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/fla/test_fla_layernorm_guard.py \
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_fused_mtp.py \
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py \
  tests/kernels/fla/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py -q
```

Result: **1755 passed in 12m18s**. All pre-commit hooks pass.

Direct measurements of the removed zero fill and gate reshape copy, multiplied by the 36 GDN layers in Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. Device time via `flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time_with_cupti` (CUPTI, cold L2), median of the timed calls:

| Padded tokens | Zero fill per layer | Gate copy per layer | Removed work per step |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1,024 | 4.4 µs | 16.8 µs | 0.76 ms |
| 4,096 | 14.0 µs | 58.0 µs | 2.59 ms |
| 8,192 | 26.6 µs | 112.0 µs | 4.99 ms |
| 16,384 | 51.9 µs | 219.9 µs | 9.79 ms |

These are isolated removed-operation costs, not an end-to-end serving speedup measurement; they exclude the additional weight and `a`/`b` copy savings.

<details>
<summary>Copy-cost reproducer</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import statistics

import torch
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti

HEADS = 48
DIM = 128
LAYERS = 36


def measure_us(op):
    op()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return statistics.median(
        bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(op, cold_l2_cache=True)
    ) * 1e3


print(torch.cuda.get_device_name())
print("tokens,zero_us,gate_copy_us,removed_ms_per_step")
with torch.inference_mode():
    for tokens in [1024, 4096, 8192, 16384]:
        # Packed Q/K/V/Z: 16 Q/K heads and 48 V/Z heads.
        qkv_width = (2 * 16 + HEADS) * DIM
        packed = torch.randn(
            tokens, qkv_width + HEADS * DIM,
            device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        )
        gate = packed[:, qkv_width:].view(tokens, HEADS, DIM)
        copied = gate.reshape(-1, DIM)
        assert copied.data_ptr() != gate.data_ptr()
        del copied

        zero_us = measure_us(
            lambda: torch.zeros(
                (tokens, HEADS, DIM),
                device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16,
            )
        )
        gate_us = measure_us(lambda: gate.reshape(-1, DIM))
        removed_ms = (zero_us + gate_us) * LAYERS / 1000
        print(f"{tokens},{zero_us:.1f},{gate_us:.1f},{removed_ms:.2f}")
        del gate, packed
PY
```

</details>

## Details

With MTP enabled, every Qwen GDN forward uses the fused spec-decode path, including prefill batches. That path incurred three per-layer costs absent from the non-MTP path:

- **Output initialization:** `forward_cuda` now allocates `core_attn_out` with `torch.empty`. The kernels write every actual row; padding rows feed only row-wise operations and cannot affect sampled outputs, following the uninitialized-output contract established by #64419. The no-metadata branch of `_forward_core_fused_norm_packed` explicitly zero-fills the buffer for profiling/dummy runs.
- **Gate copy:** the gate is a strided view of packed `in_proj_qkvz` output, so flattening tokens and heads with `reshape(-1, V)` copied it. Gated RMSNorm now uses one row per token and one group per head, reading the gate in place. Output is bit-identical because the fp32 math and operation order within each group are unchanged.
- **Weight materialization:** a stride-0 `expand` shares `norm.weight` across heads. FLA `layer_norm_fwd` accepts `stride_w_group=0` for shared weights and derives `ROWS_PER_BLOCK` from rows × groups, preserving the tiling behavior of the row-per-head layout.

The fallback `_forward_core` call also accepts the strided `a`/`b` views directly, removing their `.contiguous()` copies. Warmup registers the fused row-per-token/group-per-head call pattern to avoid runtime compilation.

Tests add stride-0 shared-weight coverage and warmup-key coverage for the fused layout. The packed-entrypoint test now NaN-poisons its output buffer, detecting any actual row left unwritten.

AI assistance was used (Kimi Code).

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Fuse the MTP drafter's pre-FC Gemma RMSNorms into one Triton launch
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fuse the two pre-FC Gemma RMSNorms of the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4Exp) MTP drafter into one Triton launch, via a new `fused_pre_fc_norms_split` next to Qwen3.5's `fused_pre_fc_norms` in `vllm/kernels/triton/fused_pre_fc_norms.py`.

## Claims

- The drafter's two pre-FC norms (embedding, width `H`; hidden, width `hc_count*H`) run as one launch instead of eager `pow/mean/rsqrt/mul` chains plus a per-call `weight.float() + 1.0`, repeated on every draft iteration.
- Kernel microbenchmark on B300: **12-77x** faster than the eager pair (CUPTI device time, cold L2); the eager chain's cost is dominated by its many small kernels, the fused launch sits near the kernel floor.
- Decode median ITL improves **0.07-0.17 ms/step (~0.2-0.45%)**; MTP acceptance and GSM8K are unchanged.
- Not a duplicate: this extends the existing kernel module without modifying Qwen3.5's same-width `fused_pre_fc_norms` — its `[N, 2H]` concat feeds a single FC and cannot serve Qwen4Exp's different-width norms feeding `fc_embedding`/`fc_hidden` separately. [#55329](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55329) (FlashInfer Gemma RMSNorm on CUDA) is a general norm kernel, not the MTP pre-FC pair; [#65497](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65497) is RMSNorm+FP8 quant fusion.

## Validation

B300, this branch:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `python -m pytest tests/kernels/core/test_fused_pre_fc_norms.py -v` | 24 passed in 29.32s: 12 pre-existing concat-kernel tests + 12 new split tests (bf16/fp16/fp32 x {1,129} tokens x contiguous/strided hidden, against an eager GemmaRMSNorm reference) |
| `python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py::test_qwen4_exp_mtp_returns_sample_and_multi_streams -v` | 4 passed: CPU plumbing test; its nvidia arm stubs the drafter norms (kernel weights only) and bypasses the CUDA-only fused kernel, which the kernel tests above cover |
| pre-commit | all hooks pass (ruff, mypy, docstring style, test-tethering, sign-off) |

`tests/kernels/core` is already selected in `.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`; no CI change needed.

Kernel microbenchmark on this branch, B300 SXM6 AC (`sm_103`), bf16, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next drafter shapes (embeds `[T, 2560]`, hidden `[T, 10240]`). Device time via `flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time_with_cupti` (CUPTI, cold L2); arms interleaved with alternating order over 3 rounds; medians with min-max ranges (all within ±2%). Eager arm: the two production `GemmaRMSNorm` modules, which delegate to `forward_native`.

| Tokens | Eager pair | Fused launch | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 260.9 µs | 3.4 µs | 76.9x |
| 128 | 258.0 µs | 3.9 µs | 65.5x |
| 512 | 264.3 µs | 8.3 µs | 31.8x |
| 2,048 | 424.5 µs | 27.0 µs | 15.7x |
| 8,192 | 1212.5 µs | 98.1 µs | 12.3x |
| 16,384 | 2336.2 µs | 190.9 µs | 12.2x |

The eager pair decomposes into ~15 small kernels per call (pow/mean/rsqrt/mul chains plus a per-call `weight.float() + 1.0`), so its device time is dominated by launch-bound tiny kernels; the fused launch is one kernel. Accuracy: the fused kernel is tested against the eager `GemmaRMSNorm` reference (bf16/fp16/fp32, contiguous and strided inputs) and preserves `forward_native` operation order (fp32 accumulation, `1 + weight`, cast on store); it is not bit-exact with the eager chain.

## Details

- **Root cause:** `GemmaRMSNorm.forward_cuda` delegates to `forward_native`: its fp32 weight fails the fused implementation's `weight.dtype == x.dtype` predicate, silently selecting eager decomposition. CUDA has no dedicated Gemma norm kernel.
- **Implementation:** the split variant keeps `forward_native`'s math (fp32 accumulation, `1 + weight` scale, cast on store) but takes two widths and writes two contiguous outputs, because `fc_embedding` and `fc_hidden` consume separate tensors. In `mtp.py` both norms run before `fc_embedding`; the hidden norm has no dependency on that projection. The GemmaRMSNorm modules remain for weight loading.
- **Numerics:** same op order as `forward_native`, but not bit-exact with the eager chain (single fused pass); accuracy results above.
- **PDL:** `gdc_wait()` after the offset math, before the first load of producer data; `gdc_launch_dependents()` after the stores. Placement is scheduling-only — consumer safety comes from its own `gdc_wait()` — and after-stores minimizes how long prelaunched dependent blocks spin on SMs.
- **Limitations:** measured on B300 only. The gain is dominated by the eager path's kernel count and shrinks where the drafter's steps are otherwise GPU-saturated.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Llama 4: honor per-request max_patches
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Llama 4 computes `aspect_ratios` / `patches_per_image` (and from them the image placeholders) with the image processor's default `max_patches`, while the HF processor that produces `pixel_values` uses the merged request kwargs. So `mm_processor_kwargs={"max_patches": N}` per request, or `{"images_kwargs": {"max_patches": N}}` at init or per request, gives fewer tiles in `pixel_values` than vLLM accounts for. This reads `max_patches` and `resize_to_max_canvas` from the merged image kwargs, the same way Mistral3 resolves `size`.

## Claims

- With a per-request or scoped `max_patches`, Llama 4 requests now run, and the prompt token ids are identical to the HF processor's.
- Default kwargs and an init-time flat `max_patches` (which already worked) give the same placeholders as before.

## Validation

End to end on one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (Colab), with the vLLM nightly wheel `0.34.0rc1.dev509+g0431c0f73` as main and the same install with this PR's diff applied. `LLM.chat(..., mm_processor_kwargs=kw)`, the `stop_sign` image asset resized to 1024x768, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=32`, a fresh process per kwargs set. HF: `AutoProcessor` on the same chat-template text (`add_special_tokens=False`, since the template already has BOS) and image, transformers 5.22.2.

| Model | `mm_processor_kwargs` | HF tiles / prompt len | main | this PR: prompt len | this PR: output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-quantized.w4a16` | `{}` | 13 / 1904 | 1904 | 1904 | `The image shows a stop sign in front of a Chinese-style gate.` (same as main) |
| | `{"max_patches": 8}` | 7 / 1034 | `EngineDeadError` | 1034 | same sentence |
| | `{"images_kwargs": {"max_patches": 4}}` | 5 / 744 | `EngineDeadError` | 744 | same sentence |
| `RedHatAI/Llama-Guard-4-12B` (bf16) | `{}` | 13 / 2092 | 2092 | 2092 | `safe` (same as main) |
| | `{"max_patches": 8}` | 7 / 1222 | `EngineDeadError` | 1222 | `safe` |
| | `{"images_kwargs": {"max_patches": 4}}` | 5 / 932 | `EngineDeadError` | 932 | `safe` |

Root error on main (`max_patches=8`), from the vision embedding split in `Llama4ForConditionalGeneration`:

```
RuntimeError: split_with_sizes expects split_sizes to sum exactly to 7 (input tensor's size at dimension 0), but got split_sizes=[13]
```

New test, `test_processor_override` in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mllama4.py`. It compares vLLM's prompt token ids with the HF processor's `input_ids` and checks that `patches_per_image` adds up to the number of tiles in `pixel_values`, for `{}`, a flat `max_patches` and a scoped `images_kwargs.max_patches`, with kwargs at init and per request (one 1024x768 image):

```
$ pytest -q tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mllama4.py -k processor_override

# main (e22287df5)
FAILED ...test_processor_override[True-mm_processor_kwargs2-meta-llama/Llama-Guard-4-12B]
FAILED ...test_processor_override[False-mm_processor_kwargs1-meta-llama/Llama-Guard-4-12B]
FAILED ...test_processor_override[False-mm_processor_kwargs2-meta-llama/Llama-Guard-4-12B]
E         At index 291 diff: 200084 != 200085
E         Left contains 1160 more items, first extra item: 200092
3 failed, 3 passed

# this PR
6 passed
```

The test uses the same model as the existing `test_profiling`. I don't have access to the gated `meta-llama` repos, so I ran it locally against `RedHatAI/Llama-Guard-4-12B` (an ungated copy with the same `preprocessor_config.json`), swapping the id in the test and in `tests/models/registry.py`. With this PR, `test_mllama4.py` passes (10 passed) and so does `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k "Llama-4 or Llama-Guard"` (6 passed, using `unsloth/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct` and the RedHatAI copy). `pre-commit run` passes on the changed files.

The regression test is at the processor level because the bug is in the placeholder computation. An `LLM` test would need a Llama 4 checkpoint (12B or larger), so I ran the end-to-end check above by hand.

CI: `tests/models/multimodal/processing` runs in the CPU `Multimodal Processing` step (`.buildkite/test_areas/models_multimodal.yaml`).

## Details

Root cause: the HF `Llama4Processor` drops the image processor's `aspect_ratios` from its output (`unused_input_names`), so `Mllama4MultiModalProcessor._postprocess_hf_mm_data` recomputes them. It did so with `self.info.get_max_num_tiles()`, which reads `max_patches` from a processor built without the request kwargs. For a 1024x768 image with `max_patches=8`, HF tiles the image into 2x3 (6 tiles + 1 global tile = 7 in `pixel_values`) while vLLM recorded 3x4 (`patches_per_image=13`, 1872 `<|patch|>` tokens instead of 1008). `resize_to_max_canvas` was read from the processor attribute, which a flat kwarg sets but a scoped one does not.

Fix, in `vllm/model_executor/models/mllama4.py` only:
- `Mllama4ProcessingInfo.get_images_kwargs(mm_processor_kwargs)` returns `max_patches` and `resize_to_max_canvas` from the image processor, overridden by the merged and resolved `images_kwargs` (configured + request, flat keys routed into `images_kwargs` by `_merge_and_resolve_mm_processor_kwargs`).
- `_postprocess_hf_mm_data` uses it for the request; `get_max_num_tiles()` (profiling) uses it without request kwargs, so profiling also follows a scoped init-time `max_patches`.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Add EAGLE-3 / DSpark support (aux hidden states) for Lfm3ForCausalLM
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds EAGLE-3 auxiliary hidden-state support to `Lfm3ForCausalLM`, so LFM3 can serve as the
target model for EAGLE-3 / DFlash / DSpark speculators and for `extract_hidden_states`.

Fixes #66311.

## Claims

- `Lfm3ForCausalLM` now implements `SupportsEagle3`; previously any aux-hidden-state method
  failed at load time with `RuntimeError: Model does not support EAGLE3 interface`.
- Aux hidden states are relayed across pipeline-parallel ranks
  (`supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp = True`), mirroring `Qwen2Model`.

## Validation

Tested on 1× GPU (PP=1, TP=1) with `LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B`, using Speculators' `launch_vllm.py`
(`extract_hidden_states`, layer ids `[3, 11, 19, 23, 24]`) to feed online DSpark training:

- Before: engine fails to start with the error above.
- After: server starts, hidden states are extracted, and training runs. With
  `--no-enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager`, 0 non-finite hidden-state records in 1,000 steps.

Reproduce:
    vllm serve LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B --no-enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager \
      --speculative-config '{"method":"extract_hidden_states","num_speculative_tokens":1,
        "draft_model_config":{"hf_config":{"eagle_aux_hidden_state_layer_ids":[3,11,19,23,24]}}}' \
      --kv-transfer-config '<ExampleHiddenStatesConnector config>'

## Details

Follows the existing `LlamaModel` / `Qwen2Model` pattern: `Lfm3Model` inherits
`EagleModelMixin`, records hidden states before the first layer and after each layer via
`_maybe_add_hidden_state`, packs them into `IntermediateTensors` on non-last PP ranks, and
returns `(hidden_states, aux_hidden_states)` on the last rank. The output is unchanged when no
aux layers are configured.

**Known issue (help wanted): NaNs in extracted hidden states with CUDA graphs**

- **Symptom:** with CUDA graphs enabled, some extracted hidden states contain NaNs.
  It's intermittent: a retry of the same request usually comes back clean.
- **Workaround:** `--enforce-eager`.
- **Interaction with prefix caching:** with prefix caching also on, retrying a failed
  request appears to reuse the cached NaN hidden states, so the NaN repeats on every retry.
- **Evidence:** `--enforce-eager` with prefix caching on: 0 non-finite records over
  600 training steps. The prefix-cache hit rate in that run was 0% (no retries occurred),
  so prefix caching alone doesn't cause NaNs, but cache reuse wasn't exercised.
- **Possible cause:** how CUDA graphs capture aux hidden states for this hybrid
  conv/attention model, or this change itself. Not yet isolated.
  
**Limitations:** the PP relay path is untested (PP=1 only).

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

ERNIE-4.5-VL admits videos its profiling never ran, so an admitted video can run the engine out of memory in the vision encoder at request time (main crashes on a 4,645-token prompt with one 8-frame video at 16384). The video budget, frame count and profiling dummy are sized from image settings, while the processor resizes video frames with `video_min_pixels`/`video_max_pixels`. This PR sizes them from the video pixel limits, so startup profiles the largest admitted video: the engine either reserves enough memory for it or fails at startup.

Follows #66608 (merged). The video encoding itself is unchanged.

## Claims

- On one A100 80GB at 16384 and 24576, main runs out of memory in the vision encoder on the first admitted video (a 4,645-token prompt). With this PR all tested videos complete, including full-budget ones (15,569 / 23,941 prompt tokens); inputs are random-pixel frames at the sizes listed below.
- Profiling now covers the largest admitted video, so it reserves more: 5.57 / 8.87 GiB for transient activations and 173,056 / 64,512 KV cache tokens at 16384 / 24576 (main: 0.68 / 1.27 GiB, 323,584 / 312,320 tokens). At 32768 a full-budget video does not fit on 80 GB, and startup fails with `No available memory for the cache blocks`, where main starts and then crashes on an 11,581-token video. Video size hints in `limit_mm_per_prompt` shrink the profiled video (below).
- With default settings the per-item video budget equals the profiled video at every context length checked (8192 to 131072), also under `max_pixels`/`video_max_pixels` overrides (CPU, below). With a video size hint the dummy covered every sampled real video within it whose frames the processor does not upscale (300 random hints x 400 sizes); for 10 of those hints, a very thin frame that the processor upscales from below `video_min_pixels` still exceeds it (e.g. 450 vs. 408 cells); main has this gap too (Limits).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Security] Check the uncompressed size of embedding archives before torch.load
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`VLLM_MAX_EMBED_DECODE_BYTES` (#54632) bounds the dense size of a client-supplied `prompt_embeds`, `image_embeds`, `audio_embeds` or `video_embeds` tensor. The check runs after `torch.load`. A `torch.save` archive is a zip file, and `torch.load` reads each storage entry at the uncompressed size the archive records, so a deflate-compressed storage of zeros inflates to many GiB inside `torch.load` before the check runs. A one-row view of such a storage passes the check and keeps the whole storage alive. This PR checks the archive's uncompressed size before calling `torch.load`.

## Claims

- A 4.2 MB base64 `prompt_embeds` payload made `safe_load_prompt_embeds` allocate 3072 MiB on main. A (1, hidden) view over the same storage was accepted with its 3 GiB storage attached, although the limit is 2 GiB. With this PR both are rejected before loading, with peak RSS growth of 0 to 1 MiB.
- Archives within the limit load as before, compressed or not.

## Validation

Reproducer: `safe_load_prompt_embeds` with hidden size 1024 and `torch.bfloat16`, on a payload built by `torch.save` and re-packed with `zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED` for the storage entries. The payload is built in a child process, so the peak RSS growth covers only the load. Default limit 2147483648 bytes.

| payload | base64 size | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| (1572864, 1024) zeros, 3 GiB storage | 4175968 B | 3072 MiB, 8.4 s, rejected by the shape check | 0 MiB, rejected before loading |
| (1, 1024) view of the same storage | 4175964 B | 3073 MiB, 7.7 s, accepted with a 3221225472-byte storage | 1 MiB, rejected before loading |
| (32768, 1024) zeros, 64 MiB | 88376 B | not run | 65 MiB, accepted |

New tests in `tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_validation.py` use a one-row view of a 3 MiB storage against a 64 KiB limit. On main:

```
$ pytest -q tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_validation.py -k Compressed
E       Failed: DID NOT RAISE VLLMValidationError
FAILED tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_validation.py::TestCompressedStorageLimit::test_prompt_embeds_rejects_view_of_large_storage
FAILED tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_validation.py::TestCompressedStorageLimit::test_media_io_rejects_view_of_large_storage[ImageEmbeddingMediaIO-image_embeds]
FAILED tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_validation.py::TestCompressedStorageLimit::test_media_io_rejects_view_of_large_storage[AudioEmbeddingMediaIO-audio_embeds]
FAILED tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_validation.py::TestCompressedStorageLimit::test_media_io_rejects_view_of_large_storage[VideoEmbeddingMediaIO-video_embeds]
4 failed, 2 passed, 42 deselected
```

With this PR:

```
$ pytest -q tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_validation.py
48 passed
```

`pytest tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_validation.py tests/renderers/test_prompt_embeds_payload_validation.py tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_concurrent_race.py tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_prompt_embeds.py tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py` gives 3 failed, 215 passed on main and 3 failed, 221 passed with this PR. The 3 failures are the same `test_prompt_embeds_input_width` cases on both and need model configs that are not in my offline cache. `tests/multimodal/media/test_audio.py` needs `soundfile`, which my environment lacks, so it was not run. I did not run `vllm serve` with `--enable-prompt-embeds` on this machine. The reproducer calls `safe_load_prompt_embeds`, the function the completions and chat paths use.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the changed files. `mypy --python-version 3.11` on the five changed source files reports the same 5 errors on main and on this branch, none in the changed lines.

## Details

Root cause. `torch.load` dispatches to its zip reader when the payload starts with a zip local file header (`PK\x03\x04`). The reader allocates each record at the uncompressed size from the central directory and inflates into it. `safe_to_dense` then sees an ordinary dense tensor and measures `numel() * element_size()`, which covers the view and leaves the storage out. The global sparse-load lock is held for the whole inflate, so other embedding loads wait on it as well.

Change. `check_torch_archive_size` in `vllm/utils/sparse_utils.py` reads the zip central directory with `zipfile` and sums the uncompressed size of every entry, which bounds what `torch.load` can allocate whichever entry it reads. It raises `VLLMValidationError` when the sum exceeds `VLLM_MAX_EMBED_DECODE_BYTES`, and also when a payload with the zip header cannot be read as a zip archive (torch would fail on it too). Payloads in the legacy, non-zip format are read from the request bytes as is, so their size is already bounded by the request. The check runs before `torch.load` in `safe_load_prompt_embeds` and in the three embedding `MediaIO.load_bytes` paths. `load_file` for `--allowed-local-media-path` files is unchanged, since the server operator controls those files. Setting the limit to `0` disables this check together with the existing one.

`--enable-prompt-embeds` and `--enable-mm-embeds` are documented for trusted clients. This keeps `VLLM_MAX_EMBED_DECODE_BYTES` meaning what `docs/usage/security.md` says it means, and that page now mentions the archive check.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Mamba] Optimize prefill splits for mid-block resume (3 forward passes to 1)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

For hybrid (Mamba "align") prefix caching: when a request resumes from a prefix hit in the middle of a Mamba block and its prompt ends in the next block, main runs it in up to 3 steps (stop at the block boundary, stop at the checkpoint, then the rest). This PR runs it in 1 step by letting the checkpoint state be written into the block the request resumed from, in its block table.

Builds on #67717, which keeps blocks a mid-block resume ran past from getting the full-block hash; this PR relies on that to put the checkpoint in the resumed block.

## Motivating example

Kimi K3.1, one aggregated instance with TP8 + DCP8 (2 × 4 GB300), `--enable-prefix-caching --prefix-match-unit 128`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`. The block size is 1280 tokens, and prefix-cache hits land on 128-token boundaries.

Two requests in one conversation:
- **Request 1** has a 1,984-token prompt. Its cached Mamba state is at 1,920, the last 128-token boundary, which is in the middle of block 1 (tokens 1,280–2,560).
- **Request 2** continues the conversation: request 1's prompt and answer plus a new user turn, 2,880 tokens. It hits the cache at 1,920 (`cached_tokens: 1920`), so 960 new tokens remain. Its prompt ends in block 2.

**main**: 3 forward passes for request 2's prefill (`--enable-logging-iteration-details`):

```
Iteration(76): 1 context requests, 640 context tokens   # 1920 -> 2560: stop at the block boundary
Iteration(77): 1 context requests, 256 context tokens   # 2560 -> 2816: stop at the checkpoint
Iteration(78): 1 context requests, 64 context tokens    # 2816 -> 2880: the rest
```

**This PR**: 1 forward pass. The checkpoint (state at 2,816) is written into block 1, the block the request resumed from:

```
Iteration(72): 1 context requests, 960 context tokens   # 1920 -> 2880
```

`cached_tokens` and the prefix-cache counters are identical in both runs (2,880 queries, 1,920 hits). TTFT for request 2 drops from 0.69 s to 0.25 s. That run used `--enforce-eager`, where each pass costs ~220 ms regardless of size; the agentic benchmark below measures the effect with CUDA graphs.

## Implementation

- **Lift the gate.** `is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid` now allows the checkpoint in the block a mid-block query resumes from (`checkpoint_col >= query_start // block_size`; was `> (query_start - 1) // block_size`). That block holds only the request's private copy of the resumed state, which the align pre-copy reads into the running block before the forward. The rule is shared by the scheduler, `MambaManager` and the worker, so they stay in lockstep. `_needs_internal_checkpoint` reuses that block instead of reserving a new one.
- **Mid-block states stay unkeyed.** The blocks such a chunk leaves holding a state other than their block end (the resumed block, or a checkpoint block whose checkpoint is not its block end) are kept off the full-block hash by #67717's `MambaManager` record and `_refine_block_mask` hook; `_cache_partial_tail_block` still keys a reusable checkpoint at its own position.

## Performance

Agentic coding trace (prefill only, OSL = 1), Kimi K3.1, one aggregated TP8 + DCP8 instance (2 × 4 GB300) with a Mooncake store cache tier, `--prefix-match-unit 128`. Same image and config for both arms; only this PR's diff differs. Each run is 60 minutes; metrics are over profiling minutes 10–60.

| | c16 main | c16 this PR | c48 main | c48 this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TTFT mean (s) | 0.69 | 0.60 (**-13%**) | 2.12 | 1.88 (**-11%**) |
| TTFT p50 (s) | 0.45 | 0.39 (**-13%**) | 0.90 | 0.76 (**-16%**) |
| TTFT p90 (s) | 1.13 | 1.01 (**-11%**) | 4.77 | 4.10 (**-14%**) |
| Prefill steps | 4,303 | 3,093 (**-28%**) | 9,247 | 7,449 (**-19%**) |
| Throughput (tok/s/GPU) | 17,332 | 17,307 | 50,984 | 51,405 (+0.8%) |
| Prefix hit rate | 0.9758 | 0.9758 | 0.9709 | 0.9710 |
| Fresh tokens / request | 4,206 | 4,200 | 5,061 | 5,042 |

- Hit rate and fresh tokens per request match between arms, so the gains come from fewer forward passes, not different cache behavior.
- Throughput is unchanged at c16, where it follows the offered load. At full saturation (every step already full) fewer passes cannot add token throughput, but per-request service time still drops.
- The c48 runs set the Mooncake store connector's `lookup_timeout_s` to 5.0 in both arms. With the 1 s default (#65939), lookups queued behind bursts time out and trip its circuit breaker, and the resulting whole-prefix recomputes dominate both arms.

### End-to-end: InferenceX AgentX sweep, Kimi K3.1 on GB300

The GB300 Kimi K3.1 configs and images from the [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4907](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4907) sweep (disaggregated P/D with NIXL and a Mooncake store tier, plus one aggregated point). The two arms differ only by this PR's diff applied to each point's image. Each run is the AgentX agentic trace at a fixed concurrency, with 60 minutes of profiling. Values are the sweep's image → the same image with this PR.

| point | TTFT mean (s) | TTFT p50 (s) | TTFT p90 (s) | throughput (tok/s/GPU) | interactivity (1000 / p90 ITL) | E2E latency p90 (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| agg c1 | 1.36 → 1.31 (-4%) | 0.94 → 0.85 (-10%) | 1.84 → 2.21 (+20%) | 1,533 → 1,544 | 452.7 → 451.2 | 12.3 → 12.4 |
| 1P3D c20 | 0.71 → 0.63 (**-11%**) | 0.57 → 0.48 (**-16%**) | 1.19 → 1.07 (**-10%**) | 4,619 → 4,624 | 264.7 → 263.2 | 9.2 → 9.3 |
| 1P3D c32 | 0.91 → 0.83 (**-9%**) | 0.65 → 0.57 (**-12%**) | 1.48 → 1.34 (**-9%**) | 7,532 → 7,577 | 211.9 → 210.7 | 10.6 → 10.4 |
| 1P3D c56 | 1.20 → 1.13 (-6%) | 0.79 → 0.69 (**-13%**) | 2.09 → 1.97 (-6%) | 11,723 → 11,618 | 160.1 → 159.2 | 13.9 → 14.1 |
| hybrid 2P1D c192 | 1.99 → 1.72 (**-14%**) | 1.43 → 1.18 (**-17%**) | 3.46 → 2.94 (**-15%**) | 20,519 → 20,733 | 94.0 → 94.1 | 26.2 → 25.9 |
| hybrid 3P1D c384 | 3.75 → 3.06 (**-18%**) | 2.31 → 1.80 (**-22%**) | 8.23 → 6.46 (**-22%**) | 30,420 → 30,858 | 73.0 → 71.4 | 34.9 → 34.7 |

- TTFT drops at every disaggregated point (p50 -12% to -22%), more as the prefill queue deepens (c192, c384), since each saved forward pass also shortens the wait of everything queued behind it.
- Throughput and interactivity stay within ~1.5%. In this closed-loop benchmark, throughput is set by the number of users and their think time, and ITL by decode, neither of which this PR changes; E2E latency is dominated by decode.
- c1 runs one request at a time (~295 requests per run), so its p90 is noisy.

## Validation

- **Unit tests** (`tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py`, 4 new tests):
  - a mid-block resume ending in the next block runs in one step, and its checkpoint is keyed at its own position, under dense and sparse retention;
  - a resume running two blocks past never gives the resumed block the full-block hash;
  - a running request resuming mid-block exports into its resumed block;
  - a decode step with at least a hash block of drafts exports no checkpoint.

  Removing each guarded rule (the gate, the resumed-block reuse) makes at least one of them fail. One expectation in `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` is updated (the resumed chunk now runs to the prompt end). No new failures in `tests/v1/core` versus main:
  ```
  pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py
  # 340 passed
  ```
- **GPU unit tests:** the Mamba metadata-builder, `mamba_utils`, warmup-block and hybrid KV-connector suites give 1294 passed on both this branch and main, with identical pre-existing failures.
- **E2E** (`tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py::test_mamba_mid_block_resume_exports_into_resumed_block`, FlashInfer GDN, ~30 s): a partial hit at 768 (block 576) prefilling to 1,252 runs in one step. The checkpoint in the resumed block and the final state both match fresh prefills (relative error < 1%), and the next turn hits at the checkpoint. On main it fails at the one-step assertion (`[(768, 384), (1152, 64), (1216, 36)]`). The existing `test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv2*` tests pass on both.

## Relationship to other open PRs

- **#60888** (draft) targets the same extra step and keying bug. It fills the null slot below the resumed block, gated to a request's first chunk in the scheduler: that also covers resumes ending in the same block, but leaves next-block resumes after a connector load or on running requests split. This PR covers next-block resumes for every request without scheduler or allocation changes; the two compose.
- **#66591** and **#65887** fix the keying bug by restoring the block-boundary stop, which removes the optimization; they are superseded by #67717, which fixes it without the extra step.
- **#66881** (opt-in frontier checkpoints) is orthogonal.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Drop the defensive zero fill from the QSA output path
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Remove the defensive `output.zero_()` from the real QSA forward path for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4Exp), and strengthen tests for the kernel’s output-write contract. This is the QSA equivalent of the merged GDN change in [#64419](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64419).

## Claims

- Eliminate one full padded-output zero fill per QSA layer during inference.
- Preserve bit-identical actual-row outputs: the attention kernels are unchanged and overwrite every actual row.
- Enforce write coverage with a NaN-poisoned output buffer in the kernel correctness test.

## Validation

On B300 (`sm_103`):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare.py -x -q
```

Result: **98 passed in 119s**.

- The modified correctness test uses a NaN-poisoned output buffer and covers both dispatch arms: Triton split-K and the Blackwell fp8 decode kernel. Any unwritten actual row fails the reference comparison.
- The existing fp8 kernel test asserts that inert rows with request ID `-1` produce zero.
- All pre-commit hooks pass.

Cost of the removed fill, measured on B300 (`NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC`): `output.zero_()` on the per-layer padded output buffer `[padded_tokens, 24 heads, 256]` bf16. Device time via `flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time_with_cupti` (CUPTI, cold L2), median of the timed calls; per-step scales by the 12 QSA layers of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next:

| Padded tokens | Buffer | Fill per layer | Effective BW | Per step, 12 QSA layers |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 600 (decode) | 7.0 MiB | 3.1 µs | 2375 GB/s | 0.037 ms |
| 1,024 | 12.0 MiB | 4.4 µs | 2829 GB/s | 0.053 ms |
| 4,096 | 48.0 MiB | 14.0 µs | 3599 GB/s | 0.168 ms |
| 8,192 | 96.0 MiB | 26.6 µs | 3781 GB/s | 0.319 ms |
| 14,848 | 174.0 MiB | 47.2 µs | 3868 GB/s | 0.566 ms |
| 16,384 | 192.0 MiB | 51.9 µs | 3876 GB/s | 0.623 ms |

At prefill sizes the fill runs at ~3.9 TB/s, i.e. it is already at HBM write bandwidth — the cost is intrinsic to touching a fresh `[padded_tokens, 24, 256]` bf16 buffer every step, not fixable by tuning. The attention kernels are unchanged, so the end-to-end effect of this PR is exactly this removed memset; a serving A/B cannot attribute a sub-ms difference better than the direct measurement above.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

```python
import statistics

import torch
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti

HEADS, HEAD_DIM, QSA_LAYERS = 24, 256, 12
for tokens in (600, 1024, 4096, 8192, 14848, 16384):
    buf = torch.empty(tokens, HEADS, HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
    fn = buf.zero_
    fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    us = statistics.median(bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(fn, cold_l2_cache=True)) * 1e3
    print(f"{tokens:>6} tokens: {us:6.1f} us/layer, {us * QSA_LAYERS / 1e3:.3f} ms/step")
```
</details>

## Details

`qsa_sparse_paged_attention` writes every actual output row. Empty selections produce `0.0` when the merge normalizer is empty, and inert request rows are also written as zero. Initializing the buffer therefore does not affect actual-row results.

Padding rows beyond `num_actual_tokens` only feed row-wise operations, including the output-projection GEMM and per-row quantization, before being sliced away prior to sampling. Their initial values cannot affect actual-row outputs. Other attention backends and #64419 already rely on this contract.

The warmup/workspace branch retains its zero fill because memory-profiling runs need initialized values.

No open PR touches the QSA output fill; #64419 addressed the separate GDN path.

AI assistance was used (Kimi Code).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][XPU] Apply attn_sink in the DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA Triton kernel
commits.pr_body:
- **Problem:** On XPU the DeepSeek-V4 sparse-MLA path never applied the per-head `attn_sink` (the prefill call site did not pass it and `xpu_sparse_decode_fp8()` accepted it but dropped it), unlike the NVIDIA, ROCm and CPU backends, so the softmax was silently wrong, by 105–118 % of the output for a row with 1 valid key and 0.2–0.8 % for 512–2048 keys (fp32 reference, sinks from the released V4-Flash range [-2.20, +2.49], Intel Arc Pro B70, bf16).
- **Fix:** Adds an optional `attn_sink` to `_bf16_mla_sparse_kernel` and `triton_bf16_mla_sparse_interface` (`HAS_ATTN_SINK` constexpr; the sink joins the softmax denominator and `lse` stays over the selected keys) and passes it from the V4 prefill (`xpu_sparse.py`) and decode (`xpu_sparse_decode_fp8.py`) call sites, while callers that omit it (V3.2 / GLM-5) are bitwise unchanged.
- **Validation:** On an Intel Arc Pro B60, `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_xpu_mla_sparse.py` gives 29 passed (25 new) against 25 failed on the unpatched kernel, and deliberately breaking the kernel (missing log2(e), sink off by 0.1 nat, sink ignored) or dropping `attn_sink` at either call site makes the new tests fail, while the no-sink path is bitwise equal to `main` and kernel time is unchanged without a sink and +0.7 % to +3.7 % with one.
- **Not a duplicate:** No open PR changes the kernel or the lines this PR adds; other open PRs edit `xpu_sparse.py` in other hunks, among the sparse-MLA sources vllm-project/vllm#64065 (my own PR, which also adds a test and a CI step) and vllm-project/vllm#59019 (23 files) only change the backend file `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/xpu_mla_sparse.py`, and vllm-project/vllm#60666 renames `self.attn_sink` to `self.sinks`, so whichever lands second has to update the new prefill line.
- **AI assistance:** Claude Code was used.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Reject bad_words on generate servers without a tokenizer
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On `vllm serve --tokens-only` and on `vllm serve --enable-scale-out --skip-tokenizer-init`, a `/inference/v1/generate` request with `sampling_params.bad_words` returns 200 with the same tokens as the request without it; bad words are tokenized only when the server has a tokenizer, and `ServingTokens.serve_tokens` never reads the field. `serve_tokens` now returns a 400 for `bad_words` on a server without a tokenizer.

Fixes #67407

## Claims

- On both modes, `/inference/v1/generate` with `sampling_params.bad_words` returns 400 "sampling_params.bad_words requires a tokenizer, but this server does not load one" instead of 200 with the unconstrained tokens, sent directly or as the `GenerateRequest` from `/v1/completions/render`.
- The `sampling_params` row of `docs/serving/online_serving/token_in_token_out.md` states the 400.
- No change for a server that loads a tokenizer: `bad_words` bans the token as on main.

## Validation

Environment: vLLM main `e509ffb943` (2026-11-12) and this branch `0f39077cf8`, Python 3.12.14, one RTX A6000 per server, `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`.

Reproduction with Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, the three servers and `probe14.py` from the linked issue (`token_ids` for "Hello world", `max_tokens: 16`, `temperature: 0`, `bad_words: ["!"]`, the first unconstrained token):

```bash
python probe14.py http://localhost:18260 tokens-only=http://localhost:18261 skip-tokenizer-init=http://localhost:18262
```

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `--tokens-only` | `same token_ids as this server's no-constraint run: True` | `HTTP 400: sampling_params.bad_words requires a tokenizer, but this server does not load one (--tokens-only or --skip-tokenizer-init). Send the request to a server that loads a tokenizer, or remove bad_words.` |
| `--enable-scale-out --skip-tokenizer-init` | `same token_ids as this server's no-constraint run: True` | `HTTP 400: sampling_params.bad_words requires a tokenizer, but this server does not load one (--tokens-only or --skip-tokenizer-init). Send the request to a server that loads a tokenizer, or remove bad_words.` |
| `--enable-scale-out` (reference) | `banned token ids in the output: 0 []` | `banned token ids in the output: 0 []` |

The `/v1/completions/render` output posted unchanged to the two servers without a tokenizer gets the same 400 line; on main both return `banned token ids in the output: 1 [0]`.

The new test starts one server per mode, asserts the 400 and `bad_words` in its message, then that the same request with `bad_words: null` succeeds. It fails on main with this branch's `test_serving_tokens.py` copied in and passes on this branch:

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py::test_bad_words_rejected_without_tokenizer -v
```

Main, both modes: `E       assert 200 == 400`, `2 failed, 14 warnings in 112.80s (0:01:52)`
This branch: `2 passed, 14 warnings in 128.04s (0:02:08)`

The test files of the `serve_tokens` callers (`test_generate_stream.py`, `test_serving_tokens.py`) pass on this branch: `98 passed, 14 warnings in 930.92s (0:15:30)`.
Main at `153dc04646` changes none of the three files of this diff since `e509ffb943`.

Not tested: `stream: true` (the check runs before the stream branch) and the Rust frontend.
No model eval: the change only adds a 400 before the request is scheduled; accepted requests reach the engine unchanged.
The new test runs in the `Entrypoints Integration (API Server)` CI step.

## Details

**Root cause.** `--tokens-only` sets `skip_tokenizer_init`, so both modes run without a tokenizer. `InputProcessor.process_inputs` calls `sampling_params.update_from_tokenizer` only when `self.tokenizer is not None`, and that call is the only place that fills `_bad_words_token_ids`; the sampler registers no bad words for a request whose `bad_words_token_ids` is `None`. `ServingTokens.serve_tokens` rejects `stop` when `force_no_detokenize` is set and a non-`tokens` `output_mode` when `not self.has_tokenizer`, and reads `bad_words` in neither check.

**Fix.** `serve_tokens` returns a 400 when `sampling_params.bad_words` is set and `not self.has_tokenizer`, the condition the `output_mode` check right after it uses for both modes.

**Related PRs.**
- #46310 — rejects stop strings in `SamplingParams.verify()` when no tokenizer is loaded. It does not cover `bad_words`; `stop` on `--skip-tokenizer-init` still returns 200 with the unconstrained tokens here.

`/v1/completions` with a token-id prompt on `--skip-tokenizer-init` passes the same `process_inputs` guard and is not changed.
The test skips on the Rust frontend because it has no `--tokens-only` and its `--skip-tokenizer-init` 400 (`rust/src/text/src/error.rs`) does not name `bad_words`.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, write the fix and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line and reran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][EPD] Clear ECMooncakeConnector local cache on reset_encoder_cache
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Resetting the encoder cache on the prefill/decode (PD) instance can break the next request that uses the same image.

```
A  ->  A                 ->  succeed   (HTTP 200; the model answered "Gray.")
A  ->  reset PD  ->  A   ->  fail      (Encoder cache miss / EngineDeadError / HTTP 500)  ->  PD EngineCore shutdown
```

The PD engine has already dropped the embedding, but the Mooncake connector still thinks it is local, so it does not load the embedding from the Encoder again. The engine then hits an empty cache and raises an unhandled `RuntimeError: Encoder cache miss`. EngineCore treats this as a fatal error, the request returns `EngineDeadError` (HTTP 500), and the PD API server shuts down EngineCore.

The root cause is a bookkeeping gap. `Scheduler.reset_encoder_cache()` only called `encoder_cache_manager.reset()`, which clears EncoderCacheManager hashes without populating `freed`. The connector's `_local_cache` is only discarded later, in `build_connector_meta`, via `free_encoder_mm_hashes`. After a reset that path never runs, so `_local_cache` stays stale. On the next identical multimodal request, `ensure_cache_available()` sees `mm_hash in _local_cache` (and/or a READY transfer) and skips Load.

This PR adds `ECConnectorBase.reset()` (default no-op), calls it from `Scheduler.reset_encoder_cache` after the EncoderCacheManager is cleared, and implements it for Mooncake. The contract is cache bookkeeping only: after reset, the connector must not treat the already-cleared local Encoder Cache as a hit, and must not schedule an already-consumed transfer.

- Clear `_local_cache` and related scheduler bookkeeping, including `_event_ready_shards`, pending-work flags, and leftover push/store state.
- Expire consumed `READY`/`RESIDENT` records to `EXPIRED`. After a successful Load, `ConsumerReservationManager.take()` has already removed that reservation, so the old `transfer_id` must not be treated as a completable remote cache.
- Leave unconsumed `AVAILABLE` reservations in place so a later request can still Load from that `transfer_id`. Because `_local_cache` was cleared, `ensure_cache_available` plans a Load rather than skipping it as already local.
- Leave in-flight `WAITING_EVENT`/`LOADING` records to the existing async flow. This PR does not make in-flight reset concurrency-safe, and does not promise to support reset while loads or requests are still in flight. `EngineCore.reset_encoder_cache` already warns that reset with unfinished requests can desync caches.

Worker-side `ConsumerMemoryPool` residents follow the same contract: `invalidate_published()` evicts unleased residents at reset and marks leased ones invalidated, so lookups miss immediately and the entry is evicted when its final lease is released; `ConsumerReservationManager.take()` refuses a READY lease whose resident was invalidated, so that load fails as retryable and re-issuing the request re-runs the encode. Reset-driven evictions are not reported via `drain_reclaimed` (the Scheduler already expired those hashes at reset), and reclaim notices pending from before the reset are dropped for the same reason. In-flight `WRITING` reservations are left to the existing async flow.

Related: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52409

### Reproduction

Confirmed on stock vLLM `v0.33.0` using the in-tree Encoder–Prefill–Decode path: official `ECMooncakeConnector` and `examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_encoder/disagg_epd_proxy.py`. Mooncake used TCP (`MC_FORCE_TCP=1`, `mooncake_protocol=tcp`). Prefix cache and `cross_encoder_cache` were off. Encoder (`ec_producer`) on `:19534`; PD (`ec_consumer`) on `:19537` with `--enable-mm-embeds` and `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1` so `POST /reset_encoder_cache` is registered; the in-tree proxy on `:10002`; EC control ZMQ `127.0.0.1:19019`. The model was Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct.

Requests went through the in-tree proxy (`POST /v1/chat/completions`). Each request sent a tiny solid JPEG and asked the model to describe the image in one word. Image A and image B are two different test images. For image A the model answered "Gray."; for image B it answered "Empty.". Those are ordinary model completions, not cache or protocol status names, and were used only to confirm the request finished normally.

```bash
export VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1
export MC_FORCE_TCP=1
export MOONCAKE_EC_PROTOCOL=tcp

# Encoder
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 \
python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve $MODEL \
  --port 19534 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 \
  --mm-tensor-ipc torch_shm \
  --enable-request-id-headers \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":2,"video":0}' \
  --allowed-local-media-path tests/v1/ec_connector/integration \
  --ec-transfer-config '{"ec_connector":"ECMooncakeConnector","ec_role":"ec_producer","ec_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"tcp","cross_encoder_cache":false}}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder":false}' \
  --worker-extension-cls tests.v1.ec_connector.integration.test_epd_correctness.EncoderGraphTestWorkerExtension

# Prefill + Decode
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 \
python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve $MODEL \
  --port 19537 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \
  --mm-tensor-ipc torch_shm \
  --enable-mm-embeds \
  --enable-request-id-headers \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":2,"video":0}' \
  --allowed-local-media-path tests/v1/ec_connector/integration \
  --ec-transfer-config '{"ec_connector":"ECMooncakeConnector","ec_role":"ec_consumer","ec_ip":"127.0.0.1","ec_port":19019,"ec_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"tcp","cross_encoder_cache":false}}'

# In-tree Encoder–Prefill–Decode proxy
python3 examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_encoder/disagg_epd_proxy.py \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 10002 \
  --encode-servers-urls http://localhost:19534 \
  --prefill-servers-urls disable \
  --decode-servers-urls http://localhost:19537 \
  --ec-consumer-zmq-addrs tcp://127.0.0.1:19019

# Reset (PD only)
curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19537/reset_encoder_cache
# Traffic went through the in-tree proxy: POST http://127.0.0.1:10002/v1/chat/completions
```

Before this fix, on stock `v0.33.0`:

- Same image A twice, with no reset in between: both requests succeeded (HTTP 200; the model answered "Gray.").
- Same image A, then `POST /reset_encoder_cache` on PD, then A again: **failed 4/4**. Reset itself returned 200, but the second request for A hit `ensure local_cache_hit=true load_planned=false` → `RuntimeError: Encoder cache miss` → `EngineDeadError` → HTTP 500.
- `POST /reset_encoder_cache` on PD, then a different image B: succeeded (HTTP 200; the model answered "Empty.").
- Clean start, then `POST /reset_encoder_cache` on PD, then A: succeeded (HTTP 200; the model answered "Gray.").
- Restart PD, then A: succeeded (HTTP 200; the model answered "Gray.").

Evidence Level 3.

## Test Result

### Unit tests

```
pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_mooncake_reset_local_cache.py
20 passed
```

The tests cover: `Scheduler.reset_encoder_cache` calls `connector.reset()` and clears EncoderCacheManager; after a completed Load (`READY`), reset expires the record to `EXPIRED` and does not plan a Load on the consumed `transfer_id`; after `observe_ready` (`AVAILABLE`), reset clears `_local_cache` but keeps the reservation `AVAILABLE`, and `ensure_cache_available` plans a Load on that same `transfer_id`; `RESIDENT` then reset expires and does not plan a Load; in-flight `LOADING` is left to the existing async path; alloc-only then reset does not false-hit or invent a Load; after `ConsumerReservationManager.take()` has consumed the reservation, reset does not reschedule that `transfer_id`. On the worker pool: a leased resident skipped at reset is reclaimed when its reservation is cancelled or expires; a new reservation for the same hash does not reuse the invalidated tensor; `take()` refuses the stale READY lease and terminates its reservation; reset evictions do not surface via `drain_reclaimed` while normal LRU evictions do; and a replacement publish does not inherit the replaced entry's retire event.

Six of the worker-pool tests reproduce failures on the previous tip (`ec92ec1d`); the seventh guards retire-event ownership across replacement. Deferred frees were additionally checked on a real CUDA device (H200, SM90, torch 2.14.0+cu130): an invalidation eviction holds its bytes on the retire `torch.Event` until it completes, and after a replacement publish the orphan release gates on a fresh event recorded on the same stream, so dropping the replaced entry's event never weakens the barrier.

### After this fix

Re-ran the same stock vLLM `v0.33.0` Encoder–Prefill–Decode path described under Reproduction (official `ECMooncakeConnector` and in-tree `disagg_epd_proxy.py`), with this PR's changes applied on stock `v0.33.0`. Mooncake used TCP (`MC_FORCE_TCP=1`, `mooncake_protocol=tcp`). Serve flags were unchanged. Traffic went through the in-tree proxy. This run had no Encoder cache miss, no EngineDeadError, and no HTTP 500.

- Same image A twice, with no reset in between: both succeeded (HTTP 200; the model answered "Gray.").
- Same image A, then `POST /reset_encoder_cache` on PD, then A again: **passed 4/4**. Each repeat: the first A succeeded (HTTP 200; the model answered "Gray."), Reset returned 200, and the second A also succeeded (HTTP 200; the model again answered "Gray.").
- `POST /reset_encoder_cache` on PD, then a different image B: succeeded (HTTP 200; the model answered "Empty.").
- Clean start, then `POST /reset_encoder_cache` on PD, then A: succeeded (HTTP 200; the model answered "Gray.").
- Restart PD, then A: succeeded (HTTP 200; the model answered "Gray.").

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add the MI300X AgentX preset for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash from [InferenceX #5058](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/5058). The existing recipe describes MI300X serving but does not expose this lane's TP8 and TP4 operating points in the builder.

## Claims

- Add 12 opt-in points, concurrency 1/2/4/8/16/32 for TP8 and TP4, scoped to the measured 0909 checkpoint.
- Pin the `nightly-rocm100-f5d93296` image the lane measured, with topology-specific Engram placement: resident at TP8, host-offloaded at TP4.
- Keep vLLM's default SWA bounded replay. The pinned image carries [#65249](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65249), so prefix-cache SWA replay is also on for CDNA3. The runbook notes that the lane's earlier v0.33.0 image predates #65249 and ran with `--no-swa-bounded-replay`.
- Preserve real speculative verification in serving commands; document the separate AgentX throughput control and evaluation scope.

## Validation

Validated at `upstream/main` `fee968681`, using `vllm-project/recipes@55a0307`:

```bash
# From the renderer checkout.
node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir "$VLLM_RECIPE_CHECKOUT/recipes"

# From this checkout.
uvx typos recipes/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.yaml
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
```

The source validator passes. The rendered `tp8_*` and `tp4_*` commands match the InferenceX MI300X recipe at `3df6aeb375cc` in every serve argument and environment variable; the only addition is the recipe-wide `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S`.

Existing GPU evidence; no new GPU execution is claimed:

| Evidence | Configuration | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Run 43350013915](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/43350013915), `3df6aeb375cc` | 12 AgentX performance points; TP8 c32 real-verification GSM8K | All points passed; GSM8K 97.65% strict exact match, 1,319 samples |

Accuracy was not separately evaluated at every concurrency or on the 1017 checkpoint. This recipe-only change makes no new performance claim.

## Details

This follows the structured preset approach in [#63560](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63560) and the MI325X preset in [#64589](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64589). Searches of open and merged recipe work found no MI300X AgentX preset.

There is no TP2 lane and no monokernel point on this 192 GB part, matching the measured InferenceX lane.

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom.git); reviewed and measured on local MI300X nodes.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Quantization] Add load-time int4 lm_head quantization for RDNA…
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds weight-only online int4 quantization for the lm_head: a new weight format, `int4_per_group_32_asym` (asymmetric uint4, one scale and zero point per 32 input channels), quantizes an unquantized fp16/bf16 `ParallelLMHead` at load time. The head runs on the platform's mixed-precision linear kernel (`choose_mp_linear_kernel`); on gfx11/gfx12 that is the existing `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel`. No C++ changes.

```bash
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Quark-UINT4-G128 \
    --quantization-config '{"targets":{"re:.*lm_head$":{"weight":"int4_per_group_32_asym"}}}'
```

Targets match the full layer name, and this model's head is `language_model.lm_head`, hence `"re:.*lm_head$"`; a bare `"lm_head"` selects only a top-level head.

**Why.** Decode reads the whole lm_head every step, and many int4 checkpoints keep it in 16-bit. For Qwen3.6-35B-A3B that is 248320 × 2048, about 970 MB per token: 4.5 ms at 211 GB/s on Strix Halo (gfx1151), the largest single item in decode. llama.cpp's Q4_K_M GGUF of the same model stores it as Q6_K.

## Design

Builds on [#61815](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61815) (merged), whose `targets` selection now reaches `ParallelLMHead` through `_ONLINE_LINEAR_METHODS`.

- **Selection:** one `_ONLINE_LINEAR_METHODS` entry, keyed by the new asymmetric quant key `kInt4Static32Asym` (`int4_per_group_32` is the existing symmetric key). No lm_head-specific config field or method table. Per #61815, a pattern selects the head only if it contains the head's name, so `"re:.*"` and `linear` don't.
- **Restrictions:** the method is lm_head-only (`ValueError` on other linear layers) and weight-only (`"activation"` omitted or `null`). A checkpoint-quantized lm_head raises `NotImplementedError` (from #61815).
- **`OnlineLMHeadMethodBase`** (`online/lm_head.py`, next to the `draft_lm_head_quantization` drafter copies) holds the format-independent part: dtype and alignment checks before loading, the kernel choice, tied heads, and the hand-off to the kernel. A format (`Int4PerGroup32AsymLMHeadMethod` in `online/int4.py`) sets its weight type, group size and zero points and implements `quantize` into the standard `MPLinearKernel` layout. The int8 per-channel head in [#63402](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63402) would be another subclass.
- **Tied heads** keep the embeddings' weight and add the int4 copy next to it, so they cost memory (about 0.29 GB here) instead of saving it. That is logged at load and documented as a warning; the fp8 online methods reject a tied head.

## Results

Strix Halo (Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, about 211 GB/s), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Quark UINT4-G128, default Triton WNA16 MoE.

**Decode** (512 in / 512 out, batch 1, greedy, median of 5 after 3 warmups, CUDA graphs on; TPOT excludes the first token):

| lm_head | TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| unquantized | 25.62 | 39.0 |
| **int4_per_group_32_asym** | **22.80** (−2.82) | **43.9** (1.12x) |

The saving matches the bandwidth estimate (970 MB → about 300 MB, about 3.2 ms). Weight memory: 18.51 GiB → 17.87 GiB.

**GSM8K** (lm-eval `gsm8k_nothink`, 5-shot, greedy, all 1,319 questions):

| lm_head | strict-match | flexible-extract |
|---|---|---|
| unquantized | 89.76% | 90.37% |
| **int4_per_group_32_asym** | **89.08%** | **89.69%** |

The 0.7-point gap is within one standard error (±0.86). The unquantized run reproduces the model card's strict score (89.76%).

**Token-level** (WikiText-2, 296,670 tokens, fake-quantized lm_head): perplexity +0.74% (7.3725 → 7.4282), top-1 agreement with bf16 94.58% vs 98.14% for a bf16 rerun. That cost is why the option is opt-in; #63402's int8 per-channel head is quality-neutral (+0.01%, 99.34%).

The decode and GSM8K numbers were measured on an earlier revision of this PR with the same quantizer and kernel (main `7871c62b61`; the two GSM8K runs on different mains). The current head was serve-checked (same kernel and log lines), not re-measured.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Quark-UINT4-G128 --port 8000   # unquantized
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Quark-UINT4-G128 --port 8000 \
    --quantization-config '{"targets":{"re:.*lm_head$":{"weight":"int4_per_group_32_asym"}}}'

vllm bench serve --model amd/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Quark-UINT4-G128 --port 8000 \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 512 \
    --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 5 --num-warmups 3 --ignore-eos \
    --temperature 0
```

</details>

## Tests

`tests/quantization/test_online_int4_lm_head.py`: config and dispatch (selection, nested heads, broad patterns, `ignore`, activation, other layers, checkpoint-quantized head) and the quantizer on CPU; untied and tied heads against a dequantized reference on gfx11/gfx12.

Raw results on gfx1151, vLLM `<SHA>`:

```text
$ pytest -v --durations=10 tests/quantization/test_online_int4_lm_head.py
<paste the raw output, including the final "N passed in X.XXs" line>

$ pytest -v --durations=10 tests/quantization/test_online.py -k "lm_head or ptpc or targets"
<paste>

$ pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py
<paste>
```

## Limitations and follow-ups

- Tested on gfx1151 only; CUDA is untested.
- Weight reload (`reload_weights`, RL weight sync) is untested for untied heads and unsupported for tied heads, which keep serving the copy quantized at load (documented). Follow-up: raise an error instead.
- Drafter `ParallelLMHead`s are quantized only if a pattern matches their name; this is unrelated to `draft_lm_head_quantization`.
- Follow-ups: int8 per-channel head (#63402); possibly int6 group 32 (perplexity +0.07%, top-1 98.67%).

---

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Qwen3.5] Fuse dynamic per-token FP8 input quant into the Gemma add-RMSNorm
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Extend the Qwen3.5 NVIDIA path's fused Gemma add-RMSNorm + input quant (#64509) to dynamic per-token FP8, the activation scheme of llm-compressor `FP8_DYNAMIC` checkpoints (e.g. `RedHatAI/Qwen3.5-*-FP8-dynamic`) and online PTPC FP8. Until now these models ran a separate `dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant` after every `input_layernorm` and `post_attention_layernorm`.

## Claims

- The fused kernel produces the same FP8 codes and `(M, 1)` token scales as the unfused chain (`gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm` + `scaled_fp8_quant(..., use_per_token_if_dynamic=True)`): bitwise on every row whose normed bf16 values match, at most one code apart on the rare rows with a 1-ulp normed difference (same contract as the static FP8 path).
- 1.6-1.9x faster norm + quant at decode sizes (M = 1-64) and 1.27-1.56x at prefill sizes on SM120. The separate quant kernel after both norms of every decoder layer goes away at TP1 and wherever FlashInfer AR+norm does not run (e.g. PCIe-only GPUs): 128 kernels per decode step for a 64-layer model.
- -1.2% (c1) / -1.7% (c8) TPOT serving a 27B Qwen3.6 FP8-dynamic checkpoint at TP4 x DP2 with MTP-2 on 8x RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell (SM120); GSM8K unchanged.

## Validation

Hardware: SageMaker `ml.g7.48xlarge` (8x RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell, SM120, PCIe), vLLM post-merge image for 793a6351d6 with and without this PR's files.

Unit tests on SM120 (`pytest tests/models/qwen3_5/test_gemma_add_rms_norm_quant.py tests/models/qwen3_5/test_fused_allreduce_norm_quant.py`):

| | result |
|---|---|
| base (new tests, old code) | 25 failed / 80 passed: the 24 new `fp8_token` kernel cases and `test_forward_fused` |
| this PR | 105 passed |

Both arms ran on the same image; the "base" row ran this PR's test files against unpatched code to show the new tests fail before the change.

Kernel microbenchmark, H = 5120, CUDA graph of 20 calls, us per call (script below):

| M | 1 | 3 | 8 | 64 | 256 | 512 | 2048 | 8192 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| unfused | 4.51 | 4.92 | 5.42 | 5.73 | 9.32 | 14.10 | 58.27 | 617.60 |
| fused | 2.77 | 2.87 | 2.87 | 3.07 | 7.28 | 11.11 | 44.87 | 396.79 |
| speedup | 1.63x | 1.71x | 1.89x | 1.87x | 1.28x | 1.27x | 1.30x | 1.56x |

End to end: Qwen3.6-27B FP8-dynamic (per-channel weights, per-token activations), TP4 x DP2, MTP-2, FlashInfer attention, prefix caching. TPOT from 40 sequential (c1) and 5x8 concurrent (c8) requests of a fixed ~2k-token prompt, greedy, `ignore_eos`, 512 output tokens; mean with bootstrap 95% CI (measured before the >384-row warps change, which does not touch decode-sized batches):

| | TPOT c1 (ms) | TPOT c8 (ms) | GSM8K (1319, greedy, 0-shot chat) |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | 7.156 [7.085, 7.226] | 8.146 [7.949, 8.378] | 0.962 |
| this PR | 7.070 [7.011, 7.130] | 8.007 [7.827, 8.201] | 0.965 |

`pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` passes. CI runs both test files in the "(B200) Qwen3.5" step, whose `source_file_dependencies` now also cover `cutlass.py` and `fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm.py`. Not validated: SM90, where the CUTLASS per-token path now also takes the fused kernel.

<details>
<summary>Microbenchmark script</summary>

```python
import torch
from flashinfer.norm import gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm

from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
from vllm.models.qwen3_5.nvidia.ops.fused_norm_quant import gemma_add_rms_norm_quant

H, CALLS, REPLAYS = 5120, 20, 200


def time_graph(fn):
    for _ in range(3):
        fn()
    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
    g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(g):
        for _ in range(CALLS):
            fn()
    for _ in range(10):
        g.replay()
    start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    start.record()
    for _ in range(REPLAYS):
        g.replay()
    end.record()
    end.synchronize()
    return start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / (REPLAYS * CALLS)


w = (torch.rand(H, device="cuda") * 0.2).bfloat16()
for m in (1, 3, 8, 64, 256, 512, 2048, 8192):
    x = torch.randn(m, H, device="cuda").bfloat16()
    res = torch.randn(m, H, device="cuda").bfloat16()

    def unfused():
        gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm(x, res, w, 1e-6)
        ops.scaled_fp8_quant(x, use_per_token_if_dynamic=True)

    def fused():
        gemma_add_rms_norm_quant(x, res, w, 1e-6, None, False)

    print(m, f"{time_graph(unfused):.2f}", f"{time_graph(fused):.2f}")
```
</details>

## Details

- `gemma_add_rms_norm_quant(scale=None)` computes the row amax of the bf16 normed activation and quantizes with IEEE divisions by `max(amax / 448, 1 / (448 * 512))`, matching `dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant`. Above 384 rows it uses 8 warps instead of the static path's 4 (the row amax needs them; swept on SM120).
- `CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel.input_quant_key()` now also exposes `kFp8DynamicTokenSym`: the kernel already takes the unpadded `(M, 1)` token scales from its own `QuantFP8`. No other CUDA producer is registered for that key, so only this path changes.
- FlashInfer has no per-token AR+norm+quant pattern. Where its AR+norm runs (NVLink), `forward_fused` keeps it and the linear quantizes as before; elsewhere (PCIe-only GPUs, or above the workspace budget) it all-reduces explicitly and runs the fused norm-quant.
- The GDN gated norm and the attention sigmoid gate keep the static-only fusion: one program there owns a head, not a row, so a per-token amax would need a cross-program reduction.
- `test_forward_fused` expected bitwise equality whenever the norm absorbs the all-reduce below the workspace budget, which only holds where FlashInfer AR+norm runs. On SM120 it failed on main for that reason (19 of 1.7M normed values 1 ulp apart); it now keys exactness on `flashinfer_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm_applies`, unchanged on B200.
- Duplicate check: no open or merged PR fuses per-token FP8 into this path. #65497 and #45770 change the torch.compile RMSNorm+quant pass and its CUDA kernels; #45364 and #61073 add manual fusion for Llama-style RMSNorm.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change; I reviewed every line and ran the validation above.

---
