commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Run the Canary WER correctness test in fp32
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes the flaky `test_wer_correctness[...-model_config2]` (nvidia/canary-1b-v2) in `:amd: (MI355 DPX) Entrypoints Integration (Speech to Text)`. The test now runs Canary in fp32 and compares against the deterministic fp32 baseline. Related: #64215, which added the Canary case and its 12.34 bf16 baseline.

## Claims

- The flake is one utterance falling into a greedy repetition loop. It is not general WER drift. In bf16, whether it loops depends on batch composition.
- With `--dtype=float32`, Canary output is identical regardless of batch composition. The full-dataset WER is a fixed 12.4564, which matches the Transformers fp32 reference (12.46) reported in #64215.
- Test-only change. The whisper and cohere cases are unchanged, requests are still sent concurrently, and the tolerance formula is unchanged. A looping run (WER >= 12.98) still fails against the new limit of 12.68.

## Validation

All local runs were on MI355X (gfx950).

| What | Command / setup | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CI evidence | Canary block of the Speech-to-Text shard in builds [101918](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101918#01a1cc17-a5f7-425e-be0d-09f7587a1c0c), [101648](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101648#01a1c85a-edb3-44d3-b2c8-14aaee267a1a), [102502](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102502#01a1d585-297c-487f-af35-f1372665e442), [101603](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101603#01a1c79d-cec3-4189-b98c-96b8e82a8ca3) | 4 failing attempts: WER 12.913-12.937 with 13,940-13,952 output tokens. 29 passing AMD and 13 passing NVIDIA runs: WER 12.276-12.468 with 12,986-13,023 tokens. |
| Before, server | bf16 with unmodified server args, all 511 requests sent at once, repeated passes | **2 of 11 failed** (WER 12.9855 and 13.0937, utterance 1 at 1014 tokens). The other 9 were 12.32-12.46. |
| Before, offline | bf16, `max_num_seqs=8`, utterance 1 in random 8-request batches | **4 of 40** batches hit the loop. A second run with a different seed hit it in 5 of 40. Repeating each of 8 fixed compositions 3 times gave identical output every time. |
| After, offline | fp32, same batching setup | **45 of 45** identical outputs (3 alone, 40 batches of 8, 2 full-dataset shuffled). A second run with a different seed: 44 of 44 identical. |
| After, server | fp32 through the server, full concurrency | **12 of 12** passes at WER 12.4564, with identical transcripts in every pass. |
| After, pytest | `pytest tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/correctness/test_transcription_api_correctness.py -k "test_wer_correctness and model_config2"` | **6 of 6 passed** (4 by the author and 2 by an independent reviewer), each at WER 12.456414572562222 and about 60 s. 3 earlier attempts failed about 11 s into server startup on the shared GPU. Their logs were not captured, and the 4 reruns passed. |
| Lint | `pre-commit run --files tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/correctness/test_transcription_api_correctness.py` | All hooks passed. |

## Details

**Root cause.** Every failing CI run produced about 940 more output tokens than a passing run. Utterance 1 of the earnings22 slice is a speaker stutter (ref: "so within fiscal year 2021 say 120 a 100 depending on what the micro will do ..."). In bf16 it usually decodes as "100" or "100, 100". With some batch compositions it instead decodes as "120 100 100 100 ... 1000000000..." until `max_model_len=1024` (1014 tokens). That adds about 50 word errors, roughly +0.6 WER.

**Not a nondeterministic kernel.** A fixed batch composition always gives the same output. Changing the composition changes the bf16 numerics through both encoder padding and decode batch shape. Running the encoder per item instead of padded still varied with composition. vLLM does not guarantee batch invariance, and NeMo/HF also apply no default cap on generation length, so this is not a model bug in vLLM.

**CUDA.** None of the 22 H200 runs checked looped, but their WER also varies (12.32-12.47). CUDA is batch-variant too and has just not hit the loop yet. The 12.34 baseline in #64215 came from single bf16 runs on CPU and L40. That PR also notes that bf16 differences are batch-shape noise and that fp32 matches Transformers.

**Change.** `model_config` entries can now carry extra server args (`model_name, expected_wer, *extra_server_args = model_config`). Canary passes `--dtype=float32` and uses the 12.4564 baseline.

**Tradeoffs.**
- The baseline rises from 12.34 to 12.4564, so the limit moves from 12.56 to 12.68. This is not a tolerance bump: the new value is the deterministic fp32 WER and matches the independent Transformers fp32 reference.
- I did not add a ROCm-only bf16 baseline. bf16 WER is bimodal, so any honest bf16 limit would have to be about 13.1, which would hide real regressions.
- The test no longer covers Canary in bf16.
- fp32 roughly doubles Canary's weight memory, to about 4 GB. This ran fine at `gpu_memory_utilization=0.5` on MI355X.
- The fp32 baseline has not been measured on CUDA here. On CUDA, TRITON_ATTN supports fp32 with encoder-decoder attention, and `canary.py` uses `model_config.dtype`. Please check the NVIDIA H200 MIG Speech-to-Text job's WER in CI before merging. gfx942 (MI300/MI325) was not available for testing.

**Duplicate-work check.** I searched open PRs for "canary wer", "test_transcription_api_correctness", "canary", "canary fp32", "WER transcription flaky" and "speech to text ROCm". None of them fixes this. #66820 (encoder bucketing) and #67144 (STT error finish) are unrelated.

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Muse Spark Open on 8x MI355X (TEP8, `--monokernel`): run the 5 DSpark draft layers and the final norm as **one
persistent FlyDSL launch a draft step** for draft steps of 1 or 2 requests. Today they are about 70 small kernels
with 11 all-reduces. Every other step runs the stock draft layers. Builds on #63440 (the target monokernel); needs
#65125 (merged).

## Claims

- Draft layers + final norm, CUDA graph: **684-732 -> 337-338 us** at 1 request, **728-733 -> 380 us** at 2 requests.
- Full AgentX, same node, same image: interactivity **+4.1 %** at c=1, **+6.3 %** at c=2; total tok/s/GPU +2.8 % / +1.5 %.
- Accuracy unchanged: GSM8K (c = 1..16), multi-key needle (32k-512k), AIME25 (32 seeds, -0.10 +- 0.41 pp) and RULER
  NIAH (within stock's run-to-run spread; equal to stock at c=2, where the launch runs on every step).
- No new flag. KV cache pool -0.09 % (load-time peer / scratch buffers, no weight copies).

## Validation

Hardware: 8x MI355X, TEP8, `--monokernel`, DSpark 7 drafts. Server results: image `nightly-rocm100-a2bcb565`
(base arm = the image unchanged; PR arm = the image + this PR's files).

```
pytest tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_drafter.py tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py   # one MI355X
```

| pre-commit (`--from-ref a2bcb565`) | all hooks pass |
| target monokernel code objects before / after (CPU compile, 30 builds) | 29 sha1-identical; K3 S16 rope differs only by its known `v_add3_u32` operand-order nondeterminism |
| draft builds S8 / S16 | 256 VGPR, 0 VGPR spills, 0 scratch, LDS 66.2 / 66.8 KB |
| 8-GPU numerics vs the stock draft layers | ranks bit-identical, second launch bit-identical, graph == eager, health 0; final hidden cos 0.990-0.995 (stock vs stock with one equally valid SwiGLU rounding: 0.997) |

| measurement | stock | this PR | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| draft layers + final norm, 1 request (S8) | 684-732 us | 337-338 us | -347 to -394 us |

The one miss (32k, c=2) reasoned to the 8192-token limit with no answer; the same prompt is correct at c=1. The stock
arm showed the same greedy-loop event (2 of 192, 32k) in an earlier run of this test.

at c=2 it runs on every step and the score equals stock.

## Details

- `mono/kernels/draft.py` (new): 256 CTAs x 512 threads a rank, builds S = 8 (1 request) and S = 16 (2 requests). A
  device loop over a table of weight pointers runs a layer: the boundary (owner sum of the down_proj partials in rank
  order, norms, fp32 residual), QKV + o-gate GEMV with qk-norm / RoPE / bf16 KV insert, causal sliding-window
  attention (the target's `attn_frag`, 7 query rows a request), o_proj with in-kernel reduce-scatter + all-gather,
  gate_up and down_proj with the in-kernel all-reduce. It reuses the target monokernel's device helpers (`dev.py`,
  `k3.py`, `attn_frag.py`).
- `kernels/attn_frag.py`: build knobs `nq` (query rows a request) and the q / KV load policies; the defaults build
  the target's fragments unchanged (identical code objects).
- `mono/drafter.py` (new): startup refusals (gfx950 with 256 CUs, TP8, the draft checkpoint shape, 7 drafts, bf16
  KV); an unsupported draft keeps the stock layers (info log). Per-step checks use rank-invariant host data only.
  Weights are views of the parameters. Descriptors and the slot-mapping table are keyed by their contents, so FULL
  graphs capture the launch. Health words go through the target's `poll_health` (`decoder.py`, a small registry).
- `common/dspark.py`: `forward` tries the launch ahead of the draft model's compiled `__call__`; the drafter attaches
  in `process_weights_after_loading` on ROCm. The NVIDIA specialized decode (#64077) stays a separate path: it is
  CUDA-only (CuTe kernels, `decode_backend="latency_specialized"`) and is off on ROCm; the two blocks do not interact.
- Limits: draft steps of 1 or 2 requests only (3+ requests run the stock layers); the Markov rounds, LM head and
  draft prepare are unchanged (a separate PR fuses the Markov rounds).
- CI: the new test is wired into `models_basic.yaml` (MI355 Basic Models). It needs one MI355X; the 8-GPU numerics
  and server runs above ran outside CI.
- Related: #65386 (MiniMax M3.1 drafter monokernel, TP4, MXFP8) is a different model and kernel; this PR shares only
  its host pattern (hook ahead of the compiled wrapper, stock fallback).

commits.pr_title: [Feature][AuxOutput] Support routed experts with P/D disaggregation
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Return routed experts under P/D disaggregation with the request fields that exist today. Rewritten on top of `main` (previous head of this PR: `9fa3343d64`); the proxy-concatenation protocol is kept, the engine side is smaller.

Protocol:

- The prefill instance (`max_tokens=1`) returns rows `[0, R)`. `R` is the prompt length minus the KV connector's prefill backoff.
- The proxy sends the decode request with `routed_experts_prompt_start = R` (the number of rows prefill returned, not the prompt length).
- The decode instance returns rows from `R` on, and the proxy concatenates the two parts.

No new request or response field.

## Changes

- **Config:** remove the check that rejects routed experts with the Nixl, MoRIIO and Mooncake KV connectors.
- **Hits need rows only from the emit start on.** `max_cache_hit` is `min(max(rows-backed tokens, emit start), num_tokens - 1)`, where the emit start is `routed_experts_prompt_start` (capped at the prompt length) for a new request and `num_tokens - 1` once it has output. An external hit that ends at or before the emit start is kept; one past it must still be block aligned and rows-backed. So the decode instance loads the prefill KV, including Nixl's full-prompt load, instead of recomputing the prompt.
- **KV blocks without rows here are tracked by hash** (`_rowless`):
  - the blocks of such an external load, including the block it ends inside, marked in `cap_external_hit` before the scheduler allocates and caches them (sync and async alike; the async load keeps that block in the loading set);
  - the block holding a request's first computed token when that token is mid-block and the block's hash appears only later (a prompt-end block), marked in `take_output` right after the token that completes it is appended, before the next schedule can cache it.

  Neither counts as rows-backed for later hits or retention. A request clears the marks of the blocks it computed in full when it finishes. The marks are pruned to GPU-cached or loading blocks once they outgrow the row-cache capacity. With no P/D this set stays empty, and same-step prefix sharing between identical prompts is unchanged.
- **Worker:** a request's first capture may start mid-block (after a mid-block load). Rows before the next block boundary are not buffered, so the block-aligned row buffer no longer asserts.

Effect on the decode instance: a repeated prompt or the next turn reuses local KV for the blocks it computed instead of reloading them, and a preempted request can resume from its loaded KV instead of recomputing it.

## Test Plan

Unit (CPU):

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py \
  tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py -k "auxiliary or aux_output or test_store or test_aux or retained"
```

New cases: `test_kv_loaded_without_auxiliary_outputs_is_hit_before_emit_start` (returns-prompt, returns-prompt-mid-block, returns-from-prompt-end), `test_worker_skips_initial_partial_block`, `test_connector_hit_needs_rows_from_emit_start` (prompt-start, resumed), `test_connector_forgets_loaded_blocks_once_evicted`, `test_connector_keeps_mark_of_partly_loaded_block`, `test_connector_marks_partly_computed_block_once_its_hash_exists`.

End to end: Qwen3-30B-A3B, one prefill and one decode instance on one H200 node, `NixlConnector`, `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`.

- Basic: prompts of 1000, 1025, 517, 2049, 64 tokens; a repeat of the first; a second turn (1332 tokens); a plain request sent straight to the decode instance.
- Preemption: decode with `--num-gpu-blocks-override 150`, 12 concurrent requests of 600 prompt + 400 generated tokens, then plain requests for each prompt.
- Checks: row counts of both parts against a non-P/D teacher-forced reference, position alignment against that reference, decode token sources from `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source_total`, and `vllm:num_preemptions_total`.

## Test Result

Unit: 120 passed. All 9 new cases fail on `main`.

End to end on `main` (release image of `9bc16ae6a3`, the files of this PR mounted over it), decode-side prompt tokens. The first column is from an earlier base with only the config check removed:

| | config check removed only | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 5 P/D prompts | all `local_compute` (the remote load is rejected) | all `external_kv_transfer` |
| repeat of the 1000-token prompt | 960 local hit + 40 computed | 960 local hit + 40 transferred |
| second turn, 1332 tokens | — | 1024 local hit + 308 transferred |
| plain request on decode | 960 local hit + 40 computed, 1003 rows | 1000 computed (loaded blocks have no rows here), 1003 rows |
| preemption, 12 requests | — | 2 preemptions, 12/12 row counts match |

- Row counts match the reference for every request; no errors in either server log.
- Decode rows match the reference at the same position (expert-set match 0.85–1.0) and not at a one-token shift (0.20–0.69).

## Known limitation

If a decode request's first forward after a mid-block load is split by chunked prefill so that the first chunk samples nothing, the deferred emission would need the skipped rows. It needs a prefill backoff > 0 and chunking of those few tokens.

commits.pr_title: [Mooncake] Route KV transfers through a backend interface
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`MooncakeConnectorWorker` creates `mooncake.engine.TransferEngine`, asks it for its RPC port, registers KV memory with it, and runs both transfer directions against it, so the connector is bound to one engine implementation.

This PR puts that role behind an interface and wraps the Transfer Engine in an adapter, and the connector stops touching `mooncake.engine.TransferEngine`. Behaviour is unchanged: same status text, same per-request failure fan-out, no new configuration key, no wire change.

What the interface covers:

- `register_regions` / `unregister_regions`: pin and release KV memory.
- `submit(peer, op, ranges)`: start one request; every range carries an id.
- `poll()`: terminal outcome per range.

`TransferEngineBackend` implements it with the same blocking batch call the connector made before, and reports the batch status for every range of the request. The Transfer Engine settles a request inside the call, so the events of a submission come back to the submitting thread; the adapter keeps them per thread so concurrent sender workers never read each other's results.

## Why per-range events

The engine answers with one status per batch today. Keeping that status as per-range events keeps a failure attached to the blocks it happened on, and gives an engine that reports finer outcomes a place to put them without another change in the connector.

## Duplicate work

No open PR puts an interface in front of the engine usage in the Mooncake connector. #61974 adds the pull-mode connector and edits `mooncake_connector.py`; it keeps calling `mooncake.engine.TransferEngine` directly, so the two changes can be combined in either order.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_transfer_backend.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_stats.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/transfer/backend.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/transfer/te.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/transfer/__init__.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_stats.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_transfer_backend.py
```

## Test Result

On a single 8×H20 host:

- `test_mooncake_stats.py`: 21 passed
- `test_mooncake_connector.py`: 98 passed, 37 failed

Those 37 failures are the same set on the base commit in the same host: they open a connection to a bootstrap endpoint that is unreachable there and fail on the pytest timeout. No test that passes on the base commit fails with this change.

`pre-commit` passes on all changed files.

### E2E: Mooncake P/D disaggregation

Single 8×H20 node, vLLM built from this head (`399ae875`, `0.30.1rc1.dev2528+g399ae8757`), `mooncake-transfer-engine==0.3.13.post1`, RoCE `mlx5_1`, one prefill and one decode instance.

| Configuration | GSM8K exact_match (expected 0.41) | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run_accuracy_test.sh`, TP 1/1, util 0.2 | 0.4208 | 1 passed in 58.4s |
| sweep: TP 1/1, util 0.6 | 0.4223 | 1 passed in 58.0s |
| sweep: TP 2/2, util 0.6 | 0.4208 | 1 passed in 62.2s |
| sweep: TP 1/1, sleep/wake | 0.4230 | 1 passed in 57.2s |

`test_mooncake_imports.py`: 1 passed. Every run ended with `Num failed transfers=0` and `Num failed recvs=0`; transfer throughput stayed around 26–32 GB/s.

Two H20 hosts over RoCE `mlx5_0`: prefill on one host, decode on the other, `mooncake_connector_proxy.py` forwarding between them, same build and Mooncake wheel. GSM8K exact_match 0.4208, 1 passed in 63.1s over 1319 questions, with `Num failed transfers=0` and `Num failed recvs=0`.

This host does not support DMA-BUF export (`CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_DMA_BUF_SUPPORTED=0`), so the extensible KV cache cannot be registered that way. The runs used the connector's fallback path, `WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM=1` with `--disable-extensible-kv-cache`; no code changed for this.

```bash

bash tests/v1/kv_connector/mooncake_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh

```

commits.pr_title: [Recipe] Kimi-K3.1-Pro: MI355X kimi-k31-5c14fe8 image and SP prefill, align with InferenceX#5089
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Align the Kimi-K3.1-Pro MI355X AgentX TP8 preset (`mi355x_agentx`, from #67600) with [InferenceX #5089](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/5089) (`kimik3.1-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-dspark`). That PR moves the lane to the `kimi-k31-5c14fe8` image and sets `VLLM_K3_SP_PREFILL=1` on every point.

## Claims

- **Image.**
  - The preset pins `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31-5c14fe8@sha256:a61996b4c270ec09111802f62b44f5c20ad4cb73068be022b2804a287b924b9a`, the digest #5089 measured.
  - The recipe-level AMD `docker_image` moves from `kimi-k31-6d74a15` to `kimi-k31-5c14fe8`.
- **Environment.** Every point adds `VLLM_K3_SP_PREFILL=1`. No other argument or environment variable changes at any point.
- **Source.** The preset's source is now InferenceX #5089 at `75d74552`.
- **Runbook.**
  - **Sequence-parallel prefill.** The variable is set on every point, but it only runs under DCP8 (concurrency 4 to 48). At concurrency 1 (no DCP) the server log reports `sequence-parallel prefill unsupported by this configuration`, and the default all-reduce path runs.
  - **Low-latency decode speedups.** The image turns these on by default at concurrency 1 and 4: `VLLM_K31_BEAT_*`, `VLLM_K3_INDEXER_SAMPLED_TOPK`, and `VLLM_KIMI_SD_DSA_PROLOGUE_INDEXER` at concurrency 1. They all default to 1, so the preset sets none.
  - **Concurrency-4 KV capacity.** Now 19.1M tokens; it was 18.9M.
  - **Results.** The image section lists the new image-only switches. The results table and GSM8K numbers now come from InferenceX run 43717568009.

## Validation

From a `vllm-project/recipes` checkout at `131ec1a`, with this branch as the `vllm` source:

```bash
node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir "$VLLM_CHECKOUT/recipes"
node --test scripts/test-guide-html.mjs scripts/test-presets.mjs scripts/test-schema.mjs
pre-commit run typos --files recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro.yaml   # typos v1.51.1
```

- The source validator passes.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Sort Engram host lookups by table offset on MI355X
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

On MI355X with the DP-shared Engram table (`--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"embedding_across_dp":true}'`, 94 GiB in `/dev/shm`), a prefill step spends 36 to 110 ms per Engram layer in `_engram_lookup_kernel` while the main stream is idle. `_engram_lookup_thresholds` has a measured branch only for SM100, so ROCm never takes the existing sort-by-table-offset path (`sort_min_rows is None`). The table is mapped with small pages, and unsorted lookups of more than about 32K rows thrash the GPU's address translation.

This enables the sort path on ROCm from 32768 rows (4 lines). The inline-lookup threshold stays `None`.

Related: #59327 added the sort path; #67677 adds SM120 thresholds to the same function (no overlap). No open PR covers ROCm.

## Test Plan

Standalone microbenchmark against a real-size table (one shared `/dev/shm` file, `cudaHostRegister`, 8 GPUs reading it concurrently, `rows = tokens * 24`, random row ids, sort cost included in the timing), plus a DEP8 prefill profile (32 requests x 8192 tokens, 2 bursts) before and after.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py -v -k "head_shards or lookup"
```

## Test Result

Microbenchmark (94 GiB table, median over 5 runs):

| rows | unsorted | sorted |
|---|---|---|
| 24,576 | 0.2 ms | 0.3 ms |
| 49,152 | 3.8 ms | 3.1 ms |
| 98,304 | 9.0 ms | 4.3 ms |
| 196,608 | 17.3 ms | 4.3 ms |
| 589,824 | 54 ms (all 8 GPUs) | 5.1 ms (all 8 GPUs) |

The same 589,824-row lookup against a 20 to 40 GiB table takes 6 to 8 ms unsorted, so the slowdown is specific to the full-size table. Private 2 MiB-page tables (about 750 GiB host RAM across 8 ranks) also reach about 4.8 ms, but sorting needs no extra memory. The 32768 threshold is where the kernel switches to 128-row tiles and where sorting starts to win.

DEP8 prefill profile, rank 0 `_engram_lookup_kernel`, launches over 1 ms: 110.1, 109.9, 109.9, 109.9 ms before, 5.5, 5.1, 3.9, 3.9 ms after. Summed over the profiled window, per rank: about 586 ms before, 27 to 37 ms after (all 8 ranks). During the 110 ms launches the trace showed nothing else running on the GPU.

`tests/kernels/test_engram.py -k "head_shards or lookup"`: 68 passed (the existing test already forces the sort path and checks results against the reference lookup).

AgentX c256, one hour, DEP8 MI355X (host-offloaded DP-shared Engram table, MegaMoE/MoRI, cadence 96 @32K, fp8_e4m3 KV), this PR vs a main baseline run on a slightly older main (9bc16ae), single run each:

| | main | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| total tput / GPU | 175,582 | 182,270 | +3.8% |
| output tput / GPU | 1233.6 | 1277.7 | +3.6% |
| intvty p90 | 96.4 | 115.6 | +20% |
| intvty p50 | 151.7 | 161.9 | +6.7% |
| TTFT p50 | 2.06 s | 1.85 s | -10% |
| TTFT p90 | 4.41 s | 3.68 s | -17% |

The e2e (non-interactive) p90 is 28.9 vs 33.2 (this PR finished more requests: 36287 vs 35177 ok). The baseline commit differs from this PR's base, so part of the delta may not come from this change.

GSM8K (5-shot, chat completions, DSpark block rejection, this PR): strict-match 0.9757, flexible-extract 0.9750 (baseline main strict-match 0.9727). Only the row visiting order of the lookup changes, so outputs are expected to match.

Only DEP8 on MI355X with the 94 GiB table was run.

## AI assistance

commits.pr_title: [XPU][LoRA] Support unquantized MoE LoRA
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Route unquantized (BF16) MoE LoRA on XPU through `XpuFusedMoe`'s `activation_hook`/`output_hook` instead of Triton experts, by mixing `LoRAExpertsMixin` into `XPUExperts` (a single class, like `TritonExperts`).

## Changes
- `XPUExperts` now mixes in `LoRAExpertsMixin` as a single class, mirroring `TritonExperts`. FP8 / BlockFP8 / WNA16 / MXFP4 opt out via `supports_lora()`.
- The hooks add the LoRA deltas in place on `XpuFusedMoe`'s expert-grouped `gemm1_output` / `gemm2_output`, so there are no extra gather/scatter ops between the grouped and `(token, topk)` layouts.
- `fused_moe_lora` (`fused_moe_lora_op.py`) gains an optional `row_map` that maps each `(token, topk)` pair to its output row (and its input row when `mul_routed_weight=True`); `-1` skips the pair. It is plumbed through the one-shot, small-batch and shrink/expand kernels, `PunicaWrapperXPU` and `LoRAExpertsMixin`. With `row_map=None` (all non-XPU callers) the generated code is unchanged; TMA is disabled when `row_map` is set.
- Fix: in `_fused_moe_lora_one_shot_kernel` the `topk_weights` load is hoisted before the shrink loop. On XPU (Triton 3.8) the original placement read zeros, so the w2 LoRA delta was dropped for batches > 64 tokens (prefill) on both the Triton and XPU paths.
- Intel CI now runs `tests/lora/test_olmoe_tp.py`.

## Validation

AI assistance (GitHub Copilot) was used. Not a duplicate: #62631 is MXFP4, #61310 is FP8/W4A16; no open PR covers unquantized XPU MoE LoRA.

- `pytest tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py` on Intel XPU: 471 passed, including the new `test_fused_moe_lora_kernel_row_map` (mapped vs unmapped must match exactly, with 25% of pairs skipped, for the one-shot, small-batch and shrink/expand paths, with and without `mul_routed_weight`).
- `pytest tests/lora/test_olmoe_tp.py` on Intel XPU (before the `row_map` change): 7 passed (log shows "XPU Unquantized MoE LoRA backend"), with kernels#648 installed locally.
- Perf and GSM8K vs the Triton backend (Qwen3-30B-A3B + LoRA, 4x Arc Pro B60, TP=4, eager): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62807#issuecomment-6785730406. XPU mean TPOT is 111.8 ms vs 113.2 ms for Triton, and GSM8K is 0.664 vs 0.644.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Don't cache a block that a mid-block prefill resume ran past
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes Mamba `align` prefix caching serving the wrong SSM state. A prefill that resumes from a partial hit inside a Mamba block and runs past that block's end leaves the block holding the **resume-point** state. `cache_blocks()` still publishes the block under its **full-block** hash, so the next request sharing that prefix gets a full-block hit, loads the truncated state and generates garbage.

Related: #53614 (lets a mid-block resume run past the block boundary when the backend exports the prompt checkpoint internally), #66938 (uses the same masking idea in a broader change).

## Claims

- A block whose saved Mamba state is not at its block end is never published under the full-block hash.
- On the minimal repro below, the cached output now matches the no-cache output (main: wrong answer from a stale 832-token hit).
- No change for blocks whose state is at the block end, prompt extensions, or the prompt checkpoint (still cached at its own position).

## Validation

**Unit test:** `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py::test_mid_block_resume_running_past_block_end_does_not_cache_it`. It fails on main and passes with this PR (3/3 runs each).

**End-to-end minimal repro.** `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-tiny-preview`, `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, `prefix_match_unit=16`, dense retention (`prefix_cache_retention_interval=None`). The Mamba block size resolves to **832**. Run on one GB300.

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams, TokensPrompt

llm = LLM("ibm-granite/granite-4.0-tiny-preview", enable_prefix_caching=True,
          mamba_cache_mode="align", prefix_match_unit=16,
          prefix_cache_retention_interval=None, mamba_ssm_cache_dtype="float32",
          max_model_len=16384, max_num_batched_tokens=16384, max_num_seqs=1,
          enforce_eager=True, gpu_memory_utilization=0.6, seed=0)
B = llm.llm_engine.vllm_config.cache_config.mamba_block_size  # 832
tok = llm.get_tokenizer()
enc = lambda s: tok.encode(s, add_special_tokens=False)

words = ["igloo", "koala", "radish", "tunnel", "walrus", "anchor", "castle",
         "lemon", "penguin", "pillow", "magnet", "quilt", "cactus", "zebra"]
T = enc("Security desk log. Each ticket has a one-word passcode.\n")
k = 0
while len(T) <= 2 * B + 32:
    k += 1
    T += enc(f"\nTicket {k}: the passcode is {words[(k - 1) % len(words)]}."
             " The weather was calm and the hallway lights stayed on all night.")

ask = T[:B] + enc("\nQuestion: what is the passcode on Ticket 10?\n"
                  "Answer: the passcode on Ticket 10 is")
run = lambda ids, n: llm.generate(
    [TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=ids)],
    SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=n), use_tqdm=False)[0]

run(T[:17], 1)           # request 1
run(T[: 2 * B + 17], 1)  # request 2
out = run(ask, 16)       # victim
llm.reset_prefix_cache()
ref = run(ask, 16)       # reference, no cache
print(f"cached (hit {out.num_cached_tokens}): {out.outputs[0].text!r}")
print(f"no cache (hit {ref.num_cached_tokens}): {ref.outputs[0].text!r}")
```

| | victim hit | victim output | no-cache output |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 832 | `" 'access'.\n\nQuestion: what is the passcode on Ticket 1"` | `' pillow.'` |
| this PR | 16 | `' pillow.'` | `' pillow.'` |

The correct answer is `pillow`. Ticket 10 sits around token 275, inside the range 16-832 that main's stale state skips.

## Details

### What happens, step by step

Block size B = 832, `prefix_match_unit` = 16. The request lengths are 17, 1681 (2B + 17) and 858 (B + 26 question tokens). In `align` mode a block holds the state at the position where a chunk stopped. The scheduler splits prefill chunks in `_mamba_block_aligned_split`.

**Request 1, `T[:17]`.** Hit 0.
- Chunk 1 is `[0, 16)`, 16 tokens. It stops at the prompt checkpoint `(17 - 1) // 16 * 16 = 16`.
- Chunk 2 is `[16, 17)`, 1 token.
- Saved: the state at 16, under the partial hash `T[:16]`.

**Request 2, `T[:1681]`.** Hit 16, from request 1. There is no longer entry yet.
- Chunk 1 is `[16, 1681)`: **a single 1665-token chunk**.
  - The prompt checkpoint `1680` is valid for internal export: `checkpoint_col = cdiv(1681, 832) - 2 = 1 > initial_state_col = 0`. So `use_internal_checkpoint=True`.
  - That drops the "mid-block start stops at the next block boundary" stop (#53614). The chunk runs straight past 832 and 1664, and **no state at 832 is ever computed**.
- The request's Mamba blocks afterwards:
  ```
  block 0  [0,    832)   state at 16    (resume point; nothing wrote it again)
  block 1  [832, 1664)   state at 1680  (prompt checkpoint, exported internally)
  block 2  [1664, 1681]  state at 1681  (running block)
  ```
- `cache_blocks(num_computed_tokens=1681)` publishes `1681 // 832 = 2` full blocks:
  - **block 0 under `hash(T[:832])` while it holds the state at 16. This is the bug.**
  - Block 1 under `hash(T[:1664])`. In the same call, `_cache_partial_tail_block` re-keys it to the checkpoint position `T[:1680]` (`replace_existing_hashes=True`), which matches its contents.

**Victim, `T[:832] + question` (858 tokens).**

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Mamba lookup | `T[:832]` found (request 2's block 0) | `T[:832]` absent; `T[:16]` found (request 1) |
| hit | 832, but loads the state at 16 | 16 |
| chunks | `[832, 848)` 16 tok, `[848, 858)` 10 tok | `[16, 832)` 816 tok, `[832, 848)` 16 tok, `[848, 858)` 10 tok |
| result | Mamba layers lose tokens 16-832: wrong answer | correct; block 0 now holds the real state at 832 under `T[:832]` |

On the PR, the victim has no valid internal checkpoint (`checkpoint_col = 0`), so its mid-block resume stops at 832. That writes the correct state at 832, and later requests sharing the prefix get a correct 832 hit.

### Fix

- `MambaManager` records each scheduled chunk's range in `get_num_blocks_to_allocate`.
- In `cache_blocks`, `_record_mid_block_states` notes the blocks the chunk leaves holding a state other than their block end:
  - the block a mid-block resume ran past;
  - a mid-block checkpoint block.
- A new no-op hook, `SingleTypeKVCacheManager._refine_block_mask`, is overridden by `MambaManager` to drop those blocks from the full-block hash.
- The checkpoint block is still cached at its own position by the existing `_cache_partial_tail_block`. Nothing else changes.

### Tradeoffs and limitations

- **Hit length.** The first request to share a prefix after such a resume gets the shorter, correct hit (16 above) instead of main's stale full-block hit. The full-block state was never computed, so it cannot be served. That request writes the real block-end state, so later requests get the full hit.
- **Recovering the full hit for that first request** would need the scheduler to stop at the block boundary even with an internal checkpoint, which adds one step per such prefill. That is left out of this bugfix.
- **Checkpoint-block masking.** On current main, `_cache_partial_tail_block` already re-keys the checkpoint block in the same call, so masking it is defensive here. It keeps the block's full-block key from ever being published when the checkpoint is not at the block end.

---

commits.pr_title: [MoE][NVIDIA] Support SM107 in flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl for NVFP4 experts for FI 0.7.3
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This PR lets the existing flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl MoE backend run on SM107 (compute capability 10.7, NVIDIA Rubin) GPUs for NVFP4 experts, through FlashInfer's Sm107_Nvfp4_Nvfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig (FlashInfer >= 0.7.3, detected at runtime). The backend is never selected automatically. The FlashInfer pin and the SM100/SM103 path are unchanged.

Related: #62603, #64289, #58540, #59912, #45320, #64629, #62073, #63875, #65464, #65727, [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7910](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/7910). Details are under "Related PRs" below. There is no tracking issue.


## Claims

- **SM107 support.** On SM107, `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl --enable-expert-parallel` can be selected for NVFP4 expert checkpoints when `flashinfer-python>=0.7.3` is installed. The other requirements are in the new docs section "FlashInfer MegaMoE on SM107": `vllm download-kernels`, `nvshmem4py-cu13`, `CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_107a`, and `NVSHMEM_SYMMETRIC_SIZE` only when the backend's bound exceeds NVSHMEM's default heap.
  - Validated end to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash NVFP4 (ModelOpt checkpoint) with DP4 + expert parallelism on one node with 4x SM107 GPUs, using the runtime environment variables the docs give (the packages were installed differently; see Environment).
  - ModelOpt NVFP4 is the validated format. Compressed-tensors NVFP4 checkpoints take the same code path by code reading, but were not run on SM107, and the docs say so.
  - GSM8K matches the default MoE backend on the same node within the noise of one run: 0.9007 with this backend, 0.9067 with the default (`FLASHINFER_TRTLLM`), 1319 questions each.
- **Older FlashInfer is refused with a clear error.** This includes the pinned 0.7.2.post1, which lacks the 0.7.3 field on the SM107 config. Selection fails with an error that names the installed version and the upgrade command, checked against real 0.7.2.post1 and 0.7.3 installs (see Validation).
- **Refused on SM107:** MXFP4 experts, `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` and EPLB at selection, and reloading weights (`reload_weights`) at load.
- **No behavior change on SM100/SM103.**
  - The new logic is keyed on compute capability 10.7.
  - The per-format capability table still admits NVFP4 and MXFP4 on 10.0/10.3.
  - CPU tests and the kwargs test pin this.
  - The SM100 GPU tests were not re-run. See Validation.
- **No performance claim.** The serving benchmark under Validation is informational.


## Validation

### Unit tests

| Hardware | FlashInfer | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| GH200 (SM90) | 0.7.2.post1 (pinned) | `python -m pytest -v -rA tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py`, then the same for `tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py` | `37 passed`; `4 passed, 20 skipped` |
| GH200 (SM90) | 0.7.3 | same as above | `37 passed`; `4 passed, 20 skipped, 3 warnings` |
| 4x SM107, 1 node | 0.7.3 | `CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_107a python -m pytest -v -rA`, same two files, one at a time | `37 passed`; `8 passed, 16 skipped, 3 warnings` |
| SM100/SM103 | - | not run | Not re-run on a GPU in this PR; see below. TODO(optional) |

Notes on the table:
- Every row that ran used this commit's tests, with its three `vllm/` files overlaid on a build of 520cae222.
- GH200: the 4 passes are the 4 `test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer` ids. The 20 skips are 16 x "The MXFP4 MoE-EP megakernels require SM100/SM103" and 4 x "The SM107 NVFP4 MoE-EP megakernel requires SM107".
- SM107:
  - `flashinfer.__version__` is 0.7.3, and all 4 GPUs report compute capability 10.7. Of the documented variables only `CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_107a` was set, with no NVSHMEM variable; the harness also set home, temp and cache directories, `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` and unbuffered output.
  - The 8 passes are the 4 `test_sm107_nvfp4_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs` ids (`[2-dsv4.1-flash]`, `[2-dsv4-flash]`, `[4-dsv4.1-flash]`, `[4-dsv4-flash]`) and the 4 kwargs ids.
  - All 16 skips have the MXFP4 reason, "The MXFP4 MoE-EP megakernels require SM100/SM103".
  - The SM107 cases ran once. They were not repeated.
  - When FlashInfer 0.7.3 builds its SM107 kernel, CuTe DSL prints a `TYPE_INT_LITERAL_OUT_OF_RANGE` warning (a Python integer that "does not fit in Int32" is truncated) that points at FlashInfer's own `software_sync.py`. It appears once per rank in the 4 SM107 exactness cases, which still passed bit-exact, and once per worker at server startup in arms B and B'; arm A does not print it. Its cause was not investigated in this PR.
- The 3 warnings on 0.7.3, on both GH200 and SM107, are FlashInfer's `DeprecationWarning: apply_topk_in_fc1 is deprecated; use apply_routing_weights_before_fc2.`
  - One comes from the unchanged SM100 call (`[cutedsl]`).
  - Two come from the SM107 config call (`[cutedsl-sm107]`, `[cutedsl-sm107-default]`). It uses the same keyword as the SM100 call (see Design), so on 0.7.3 it goes through the same deprecated alias.

FlashInfer version check. The probe does not depend on the GPU:

```bash
python -c "import flashinfer; from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import flashinfer_moe_ep as m; \
print(flashinfer.__version__, m.flashinfer_sm107_nvfp4_gap())"
```

Run on the GH200 images with this PR's files overlaid. The SM107 selection check was run with the device capability patched to (10, 7), through the same `is_supported_config` call the CPU tests use:

| FlashInfer | `flashinfer_sm107_nvfp4_gap()` | SM107 selection check |
|---|---|---|
| 0.7.2.post1 (pinned) | ``SM107 with FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 (requires flashinfer-python>=0.7.3, then `vllm download-kernels`)`` | refused: ``kernel does not support SM107 with FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 (requires flashinfer-python>=0.7.3, then `vllm download-kernels`)`` |
| 0.7.3 | `None` | admitted |

- At startup, vLLM prefixes the reason with `<backend> does not support the deployment configuration since`, the same wrapper as arm C's refusal below.
- On SM107 hardware with 0.7.3, arm B selected the backend and the 4 SM107 GPU cases ran instead of skipping.
- The CPU test `test_sm107_flashinfer_probe` also covers `[v0.7.3rc1]`, `[v0.7.3-old-field]` and `[import-error]` against fake modules.

**SM100/SM103.** Not re-run on a GPU in this PR. What the "unchanged" claim rests on:
- New runtime branches are keyed on compute capability 10.7. The only exception is the per-format table, which admits (10, 0)/(10, 3) for both formats as before.
- The SM100 epilogue is unchanged by inspection: one `is_sm107_device()` guard in `experts/flashinfer_moe_ep.py`, which also covers the reload refusal.
- The SM100 behavior is pinned by:
  - `test_device_gate_admits_sm107[sm100]`;
  - the (10, 0) half of `test_sm107_refuses_eplb`;
  - the (10, 0) half of `test_sm107_appends_flashinfer_gap_verbatim`: NVFP4 and MXFP4 are admitted, and the SM107 FlashInfer probe is never called;
  - `test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer[cutedsl, deep_gemm]`: the SM100 config types, and `FLASHINFER_SM107_MEGA_CHECK_ROUTES` left unset.
- (10, 3) is in the same capability set as (10, 0) and has no separate test row.
- The existing `test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs` keeps its SM100 behavior: the new helper arguments default to the old values, and the skip was widened only for 10.7. TODO(optional): if run on a 4-GPU SM100 node, add the result of `pytest -v -rs tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k "cutedsl and not sm107"`.

### End to end on SM107

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash NVFP4 (`nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4`, revision `3431dde3`), DP4 + EP on one node with 4x SM107 GPUs (compute capability 10.7 on all 4), FlashInfer 0.7.3.

Setup:
- One node with 4x SM107 GPUs.
- DP4, TP1, expert parallel, `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`.
- Default CUDA-graph mode, FlashInfer autotune at its default (on).
- No speculative decoding.
- `FLASHINFER_SM107_MEGA_CHECK_ROUTES` not set, so this PR's default applies.
- The runtime environment the docs give: `CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_107a` only, with no `NVSHMEM_SYMMETRIC_SIZE` and no `NVSHMEM_MAX_TEAMS`.
- **Environment outcome.** The SM107 unit tests and every server arm ran with the documented environment; arm B' additionally set `FLASHINFER_SM107_MEGA_CHECK_ROUTES=1` on purpose (see Limitations). No NVSHMEM variable was set in any step, so this backend ran with NVSHMEM's default heap. The server arms also exported harness settings only: home, temp and cache directories, `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`, a longer engine-ready timeout, Python fault-handler and unbuffered output, and the site's NCCL settings (IB service level, socket interface, NVLink scheduling).

Environment:
- vLLM: upstream main at 520cae222 (`0.33.0rc1.dev774+g520cae222`), built from source on aarch64 with `docker/Dockerfile` (target `vllm-openai`, `CUDA_VERSION=13.4.1`, `torch_cuda_arch_list=10.0`, `INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true`, `INSTALL_RUBIN_PRERELEASE=true`, Triton from source at `3f6e4113`, `NCCL_VERSION=2.32.3`). `torch_cuda_arch_list=10.0` replaces the release pipeline's aarch64 arch list; the SM100-family code it builds runs on SM107.
- This PR's three changed files under `vllm/` were overlaid on the installed package. The PR changes no compiled code.
- CUDA 13.4.1, torch 2.16.0.dev20261009+cu134 (from `requirements/rubin-prerelease.txt`), triton 3.8.0+git3f6e4113, NCCL 2.32.3, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 4.8.0, `nvidia-cudnn-frontend` 1.32.2.
- FlashInfer:
  - `flashinfer-python` was upgraded from the pinned 0.7.2.post1 to 0.7.3 on top of that build. No other package changed in that step.
  - `flashinfer-cubin` 0.7.3 and `flashinfer-jit-cache` 0.7.3+cu134 come from `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 python3 -m flashinfer download-kernels`, the FlashInfer command that `vllm download-kernels` wraps. The image was built without a GPU, and `vllm download-kernels` needs one to infer the device type.
- `nvshmem4py-cu13` 0.4.0, installed with `--no-deps` (`nvidia-nvshmem-cu13` 3.7.2).
- This is not the docs' install command; see "Install" under Design.

Server. Both arms use the same command, except that only arm B passes `--moe-backend`:

```bash
export CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_107a
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --revision 3431dde3247c13b5957f682b1e3c6fcae2566079 \
  --served-model-name dsv41 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --language-model-only --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"embedding_across_dp":true,"dp_shared_memory":false,"use_thp":true}' \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl   # arm B only; arm A leaves this out
```

Notes on the server command:
- The revision is pinned because later revisions store the Engram tables as MXFP4, which vLLM cannot load until #61530. `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4-DSpark-TP4.yaml` uses the same pin.
- The checkpoint was served from a local copy of that revision. Before the run, a check confirmed the copy's FP8 Engram tables and its revision marker. The run passed that directory in place of the Hub id and `--revision`. The other arguments are as above.
- Neither arm used a fallback: the attention config above was kept, and FlashInfer autotune stayed on.

GSM8K, the same command for both arms:

```bash
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port <port> --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 \
  --max-tokens 256 --max-concurrency 64 --seed 42
```

Both arms ran FlashInfer 0.7.3 and the documented environment.

| Arm | `--moe-backend` | MoE backend selected (from the log) | GSM8K accuracy | Invalid rate | n |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (baseline) | not set | `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` | 0.9067 | 0.0008 | 1319 |
| B (this PR) | `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` | `FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_CUTEDSL` | 0.9007 | 0.0000 | 1319 |

How to read the table:
- One greedy run per arm, B then A, on the same node with the same server arguments.
- The binomial stderr, sqrt(p(1-p)/1319), is 0.0080 for A and 0.0082 for B. The stderr of B - A is about 0.011, so one run per arm cannot resolve differences smaller than about 2-3 points.
- B - A = -0.0061, about half that stderr.
- The 0.85 floor (0.88 - 0.03) comes from the upstream DeepSeek-V4.1 NVFP4 GSM8K config. That config runs TP4 with DSpark speculative decoding. The main check here is the A/B difference on the same node, which passes if |B - A| <= 0.03. Both checks pass.

Other arms on the same node:
- **B'**: arm B with `FLASHINFER_SM107_MEGA_CHECK_ROUTES=1` did not start. See Limitations.
- **C**: arm B's command on the same image without this PR was refused at startup. The error is in the logs below.


</details>

### CI coverage

- There is no SM107 runner in CI, so CI cannot run the 4 `test_sm107_nvfp4_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs` cases. They, the rest of both test files on SM107, and the serving runs were run by hand on one 4x SM107 node; see above.
- The CPU tests run in the existing `cpu-small` step: selection and refusals, the FlashInfer probe against fake modules, and the epilogue math.
- `test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer` runs in the L4 "MoE Kernels" step against the pinned FlashInfer.
  - That includes the two SM107 cases. They build the SM107 config with the same keyword call as production, and check the route-check default ("0" on SM107, unset on SM100).
  - The real probe against FlashInfer 0.7.3, and the deprecated-alias path on 0.7.3, run only outside CI.
  - TODO: after CI runs, confirm that `[cutedsl-sm107]` and `[cutedsl-sm107-default]` are PASSED in the L4 log.
- No CI step runs the existing SM100 MXFP4 exactness test: the B200 kernels step ignores `kernels/moe`, and on L4 those cases skip. That gap predates this PR. Adding this file to a multi-GPU B200 step is left as a follow-up.

## Details


### Design

- **Capability gate.** The per-format table comes from #62603. Its names are kept (`_BLACKWELL_CAPABILITIES`, `_FORMAT_CAPABILITIES`, `_current_capability()`, the "<FORMAT> weights on this GPU" reason, and the `_current_capability` patch in the `megakernel_host` test fixture), so whichever PR lands second only has to merge table rows. #64289 uses the same gate. This PR adds (10, 7) to the `nvfp4` entry only; MXFP4 stays on SM100/SM103. If #62603 lands first, I will rebase onto it.
- **FlashInfer requirement, without a pin bump.**
  - The pinned 0.7.2.post1 already exports `Sm107_Nvfp4_Nvfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig`, but SM107 refuses it for two reasons. Its route check cannot be disabled, so any non-finite router score triggers a device assertion that kills the worker. Its NVFP4 input staging is also unfused.
  - 0.7.3 makes the route check switchable and fuses the staging.
  - The requirement is detected through the 0.7.3 config field `apply_routing_weights_before_fc2`, not by comparing version strings. 0.7.3 release candidates already have the field and are accepted.
  - **Routing keyword.** The SM107 config is built with `apply_topk_in_fc1=`, the same keyword as the SM100 call.
    - FlashInfer 0.7.3 renamed that field to `apply_routing_weights_before_fc2`. It still accepts the old keyword as a deprecated alias, and emits a `DeprecationWarning` for it.
    - The unchanged SM100 call already gets the same warning when 0.7.3 is installed.
    - With the old keyword there is no version branch, and CI on the pinned release runs the exact production call.
    - The FlashInfer pin-bump PR should rename both calls.
  - The pin is not bumped here because 0.7.3 also breaks two all2all backends; see Limitations.
  - **Install.** The docs give this command:
    ```bash
    uv pip install flashinfer-python==0.7.3 nvshmem4py-cu13
    vllm download-kernels
    ```
    - The docs also say that pip or uv may warn about a dependency conflict, because vLLM pins `flashinfer-python==0.7.2.post1`. The in-place upgrade worked here, but with `--no-deps` (see Environment), so the warning itself was not observed. Resolving vLLM and 0.7.3 together, for example in a uv-locked project, needs an override of vLLM's pin.
    - From 0.7.2.post1 to 0.7.3, FlashInfer's base requirements change only in `nvidia-cudnn-frontend>=1.32.0` (inside vLLM's `>=1.31.0`) and `nvidia-cutlass-dsl>=4.8.0` (equal to vLLM's pin).
    - This command was not run verbatim in a fresh environment for this PR. The SM107 environment above was assembled differently (see Environment).
- **SM107 NVFP4 epilogue from the checkpoint's activation input scales.**
  - FlashInfer's NVFP4 MegaMoE takes `input_norm_const` (nx), `fc1_alpha`, `fc1_norm_const` (nh) and `fc2_alpha`. The contract is in FlashInfer v0.7.3 `docs/design_docs/moe_ep_sm107_qualification.md`, section "NVFP4 normalization".
  - On SM107, vLLM sets nx = 1/max(`w13_input_scale`) and nh = 1/max(`w2_input_scale`). It multiplies `fc1_alpha`/`fc2_alpha` in place by the two maxima, so they keep aliasing the layer's weight global-scale parameters. This is the same in-place convention the TRT-LLM NVFP4 experts use.
  - Why: FlashInfer's NVFP4 block scale is e4m3(amax / 6 * norm_const), and a block whose scale rounds to zero is zeroed. With unit constants, small-magnitude blocks can get subnormal or zero scales.
  - The w13 maximum is taken over the EP group because tokens are quantized on their source rank, so nx must be the same on every source rank. The w2 maximum is also EP-wide, but that is a choice (one constant per layer); FlashInfer would accept a per-local-expert `fc1_norm_const`.
  - Cost: one 2-element MAX all-reduce and one host read per MoE layer at load. Nothing changes in the forward path.
  - Every EP rank must process its MoE layers in the same order. This holds for the initial load and is the same contract as the existing per-layer FlashInfer setup collectives. Reloads are refused on SM107 (see Limitations), so only the initial load runs this collective.
  - Non-finite local scales become +inf before the reduce, so a bad scale on any rank fails the load on every rank. A layer whose maximum is not positive also fails.
  - `amax_for_moe_activation_quant` is not reused. It reduces across ranks only under EPLB, because the global-scale NVFP4 backends load every expert's input scale on every rank. This backend loads only the local experts' scales.
  - Compressed-tensors static NVFP4 reaches the same epilogue by code reading: `w13_input_scale`/`w2_input_scale` are derived as `1/input_global_scale`. It was not run on SM107, and the docs say that only ModelOpt NVFP4 is validated there. Per-token NVFP4 activations remain refused for this backend at load.
  - SM100/SM103 keep unit constants. Applying the same epilogue there has not been measured and is a follow-up that needs an SM100/SM103 accuracy comparison.
- **Owned-output forward on SM107.**
  - On SM107 the adapter uses FlashInfer's owned-output forward instead of the workspace view that upstream requests for DeepSeek-V4 routing.
  - On SM107 the view binds the workspace's capacity-sized output, so the top-k reduce writes every capacity row on each call. The owned output allocates `[num_tokens, hidden]` in BF16 and writes only the live rows.
  - `apply()` makes the same single copy either way.
  - This is from code reading and has not been measured. SM100/SM103 keep the view.
- **`FLASHINFER_SM107_MEGA_CHECK_ROUTES` default.**
  - When the SM107 adapter is built, vLLM calls `os.environ.setdefault("FLASHINFER_SM107_MEGA_CHECK_ROUTES", "0")` inline, so a value the user already set wins. This follows the same pattern as `MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE`. FlashInfer reads the variable on every call, so the value is in effect from warmup and CUDA-graph capture onward.
  - Why: in FlashInfer 0.7.3 the SM107 route checks are on by default, and a failed check is a device assertion that ends the worker's CUDA context.
  - FlashInfer's SM100 MegaMoE backends, which this backend already uses on SM100/SM103, do not enable route-value checks; only the SM107 backends do. So "0" gives SM107 the same contract as SM100: the caller guarantees valid routes.
  - "0" is also the default on FlashInfer main since flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7910, which makes these checks opt-in. That change is not in 0.7.3.
  - By code reading, vLLM's top-k routers return unique, in-range expert ids, but they do not guarantee finite scores: the DeepSeek-V4 router replaces NaN only for expert selection. With "0", a non-finite score on a valid route is not sanitized, the same as on SM100.
  - "0" also skips the expert-id range and duplicate-id checks. Export `FLASHINFER_SM107_MEGA_CHECK_ROUTES=1` to debug a router.
  - One run had the route checks on (arm B'). The server did not start: FlashInfer's combined route check (expert-id range, duplicate ids, finite scores) fired during startup, and which condition failed was not isolated; see "Route checks on" under Limitations.
- **Knobs.** The SM107 config uses FlashInfer's default knobs (`knobs=None`), as the SM100 path does. They are independent of FlashInfer's autotuner and not tuned for throughput.
- **One INFO line** per process names the SM107 config class and the FlashInfer version, so users can confirm which backend was selected.
- **Docs.**
  - A new section, "FlashInfer MegaMoE on SM107", in `docs/serving/expert_parallel_deployment.md`: requirements, the install command, behavior, and what is not supported.
  - A link to it from the dummy-loading note in `docs/features/quantization/modelopt.md`.
  - The `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` entry of `KernelConfig`'s `moe_backend` docstring.
- **Size.**
  - About 175 lines under `vllm/` (+173/-12), all for SM107 except the per-format table, plus 28 lines of docs. The backend stays explicit-only.
  - The CPU tests (selection, the probe, epilogue math) run in CI.
  - The single SM107 GPU test extends the existing SM100 bit-exact grid test and reuses its helpers. Below end-to-end, it is the only check of the kernel numerics: the prequantized weight handoff, gate/up order, per-expert and EP-local epilogue indexing, the EP reduce of the activation scales, and the owned-output forward.
  - The test split: CI runs the CPU file and the kwargs cases. The SM107 GPU test runs only on SM107 hardware, where all 4 of its cases passed in the documented environment (EP 2 and 4, expert shapes `dsv4.1-flash` and `dsv4-flash`).
- **MXFP4 test skip.** The existing MXFP4 exactness test now skips on SM107. `is_device_capability_family(100)` includes 10.7, so without the skip that test would run on SM107 and fail, while this PR refuses MXFP4 there by design.


- **Validated layout.** Only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash NVFP4 (ModelOpt) with DP4 x EP4, TP1 and default CUDA graphs on one node was run end to end. The following are not validated on SM107:
  - TP x EP (which turns on DeepSeek-V4.1's sequence-parallel MoE input), DP x TP x EP, and multi-node EP;
  - routing that applies the weights after FC2, which covers every method except DeepSeek-V4's. The bit-exact SM107 GPU test covers it at EP 2 and 4 only;
  - the SwiGLU clamp, which is covered only by the DeepSeek-V4.1 run;
  - compressed-tensors NVFP4 checkpoints, which take the same code path by code reading but were not run. The docs say they have not yet been tested on SM107.
- **Speculative decoding.**
  - On SM107, speculative decoding whose draft or MTP expert layers are MXFP4 is not supported with this backend. Those layers inherit `--moe-backend`, and MXFP4 experts are refused on SM107.
  - This PR offers no workaround. A draft `moe_backend` override in `--speculative-config` cannot currently be combined with a FlashInfer MoE-EP target, because the target binds the passthrough all2all backend and the draft config inherits it. #63875 is the prerequisite for such an override.
  - The SM107 validation ran without `--speculative-config`.
- **Route checks on.** Arm B' reran arm B's command and environment with `FLASHINFER_SM107_MEGA_CHECK_ROUTES=1`, which is FlashInfer 0.7.3's own default.
  - The server exited during startup. FlashInfer's device-side route assertion printed after FlashInfer's autotuning had finished: `MegaMoE routes require unique expert IDs in [0, E), or -1, and finite scores for valid routes`.
  - The workers then failed in vLLM's KV-cache-sizing warmup (`run_kv_cache_sizing_warmup` -> `run_context_prefill_warmup` -> `execute_model`) with a CUDA error reported at a later cuBLAS GEMM (`CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED`). CUDA reports such errors asynchronously, so this call chain shows where the error surfaced, not which kernel asserted.
  - This PR did not isolate the root cause, including which of the assertion's conditions failed.
  - With this PR's default ("0"), the same command started and served GSM8K (arm B).
  - The router-guard follow-up below includes root-causing this failure.
- **Weight reload.**
  - On SM107 every reload is refused. The first load marks each MoE layer. A second load of that layer raises `NotImplementedError`, before the epilogue's EP all-reduce and before a new FlashInfer layer is built, so every rank raises at the same layer.
  - On SM100/SM103, `reload_weights` with `flashinfer_moe_ep_*` backends is unchanged and not validated on any GPU. Each reload rebuilds the FlashInfer layer for every MoE layer and keeps a second copy of the routed-expert weights, and the old layer is released through `__del__`. This predates this PR.
- **EPLB** is refused on SM107. It is untested there; this is not a known correctness issue.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Cap warmup and CUDA graph sizes to max_num_seqs * max_model_len
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #66244.

When `max_num_batched_tokens > max_num_seqs * max_model_len`, dummy forwards could run with more tokens than a real batch can hold: compile-range warmup, FlashInfer autotune (`_run_flashinfer_autotune_dummy_runs`) and full/mixed CUDA graph capture all size them up to `max_num_batched_tokens`. `InputBatch.make_dummy` spreads those tokens over at most `max_num_reqs` requests, which gives sequences longer than `max_model_len` and out-of-bounds block table access (`CUDA error: an illegal memory access` in FlashAttention).

#67545 caps `_dummy_run`, which covers compile-range warmup and FlashInfer autotune. CUDA graph capture does not go through `_dummy_run`, so this PR limits the capture sizes.

## Changes

- `CudaGraphManager._init_candidates` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`): drops prefill/mixed capture sizes above `max_num_reqs * max_model_len`, with a warning in the style of the existing "Dropping ... from ..." message.
- Tests: `test_cudagraph_candidates_skip_sizes_exceeding_max_model_len` (`tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py`). The CUDA graph test helpers now set a concrete `max_model_len`.
- An earlier revision also capped `_dummy_run`. dfc2c72 dropped that cap and its test, since #67545 added the same cap.

## Verification

- Reproduced the crash on Colab L4 (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, `max_model_len=448`, `max_num_batched_tokens=1000`, `max_num_seqs=1`) with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` (`_vllm_fa2_C.varlen_fwd` illegal memory access).
- @Pb314314 reproduced #66244 on GB200 with `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN`, including the FlashInfer autotune path, and confirmed both pass with the earlier revision, whose `_dummy_run` cap gives the same token counts as #67545's.
- Unit tests at dfc2c72: the 22 test files that build a CUDA graph manager or call `_dummy_run` and import in my environment give the same results as `main` (692 passed, 28 skipped, 20 failed; the 20 fail the same way on `main` locally). `test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py` and `test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py` need FlashMLA, which my local build lacks.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the modified files.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DeepSeek-V4.1] Enable eager prefill context parallel for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enables eager prefill context parallelism (PCP) for the text-only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model on ROCm, Model Runner V2. This picks up the inactive draft #62981 by @haic0 (kept as co-author) and ports it onto current main.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash serves with `--prefill-context-parallel-size 2` on ROCm. On main it fails at startup with `NotImplementedError: DeepSeek-V4.1 PCP currently supports NVIDIA CUDA only.`
- GSM8K with TP=2 + PCP=2 lands within about one standard error of the no-PCP baseline. Expert parallel on top of PCP also works.
- MoE routing input IDs are gathered across PCP ranks when expert parallel is off, matching the MoE runner's PCP gather of hidden states.
- PCP attention skips the ROCm stream-overlap path, which caches the compressor latent without the PCP gather, zeroes the PCP-padded output tail, and returns early on a rank with no tokens, as CUDA FlashMLA does.
- Unsupported combinations (PP, DP, DCP, microbatching, spec decode, KV transfer, prefix caching, `aiter_mega_moe`, monokernel) are rejected at startup.
- `fused_compress_quant_cache.py` picks the PCP predecessor row with `tl.where`, which avoids a ROCm Triton compile failure at real cache sizes (triton-lang/triton#12695).
- CI: `test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py` now runs in the MI355 `Basic Models (Other)` mirror. It was not listed there before, so the ROCm CI never ran it.
- Docs: ROCm section in `context_parallel_deployment.md`.

## Validation

MI350X (gfx950), `/data/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, eager, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, prefix caching off, on the branch merged with current main.

**GSM8K** (all 1319, 5-shot, greedy):

| Config | repo `gsm8k_eval.py` | lm_eval strict / flexible |
|---|---|---|
| main, TP=2 + PCP=2 | fails at startup | - |
| TP=2 + PCP=2, run 1 | 90.0% | 93.1% / 93.1% |
| TP=2 + PCP=2, run 2 (the new CI config through `test_gsm8k_correctness.py`) | 89.6% | - |
| TP=2 + PCP=2 + EP | 90.1% | - |
| TP=4, no PCP | 91.4% | - |

Before the merge with main, TP=2 + PCP=2 gave 90.5% / 90.4% on the repo harness and TP=2 without PCP gave 90.5%, with lm_eval at 92.3-93.4% for both. TP=2 without PCP no longer fits after the merge (OOM in the MXFP4 MoE weight conversion with 140.65 GiB already used), so the baseline above is TP=4. PCP splits the experts over all four GPUs (81 GiB of weights per GPU), so it is not affected. The PCP-to-baseline gap of 1.4 points is about 1.2 standard errors of the difference at 1319 questions.

The docs command, run as written (default 1M max length), started and answered a 4k-token retrieval prompt correctly.

EP + PCP ran with the `AgRsAll2AllManager`, 96 of 384 experts per rank, and no server errors.

**Tests:**

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py   # 30 passed, 2 skipped (8-GPU CUDA only); 10/10 runs on 1 GPU
```

The 12 new ROCm cases fail on main and pass here, on one visible GPU and on four. Removing the routing-ID gather, a gate condition, or the `use_pcp` check in the attention forward each makes the matching test fail. pre-commit is clean, incl. mypy.

**Compressor kernel:** with a 2.14 GiB state cache, `_fused_save_compress_norm_kernel` fails to compile on main (`'scf.if' op ... region branch point has 2 operands, but region successor needs 1 inputs`) and compiles here; its output is bit-identical to the small-cache result.

## Details

- **Not a duplicate:** this supersedes #62981, a draft with no activity since 2026-10-27 and no reply to a follow-up on 2026-11-05. No other open PR enables PCP for DeepSeek-V4.1 on ROCm (#66322 adds PCP/DCP to the V3.2/GLM sparse MLA backend and does not touch `deepseek_v41`).
- **CI gap:** the first version of the gate test built a real `ParallelConfig(prefill_context_parallel_size=2)`, which fails on a 1-GPU CUDA agent with `World size (2) is larger than the number of available GPUs (1)`. ROCm CI did not catch it because the MI355 mirror keeps its own file list and never ran `test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py`. On ROCm it would have passed anyway: that world-size check is gated on `is_cuda()`. The test now uses a plain config object, and the file is added to the mirror.
- **Port notes:** the `_prepare_and_attn_*` helpers #62981 touched no longer exist; the V2 runner's PCP manager already rejects CUDA graphs, LoRA and multimodal for this model, so those gates were dropped; the empty-buffer guards in the decode top-k and SWA paths were dropped because an empty rank now returns before reaching them, and the fused packer only runs with the monokernel, which PCP rejects.
- **Triton root cause:** #62981 worked around the compressor failure with `AMDGCN_USE_BUFFER_OPS=0`. ROCm Triton's `CanonicalizePointers` handles an `arith.select` between a >2 GiB pointer and a narrowed one, but not the same merge through `scf.if`; the ring state cache exceeds 2 GiB at real sizes. `tl.where` lowers to the select the pass already handles. Reported as triton-lang/triton#12695.
- **Limitations:** PCP=4 needs eight GPUs at TP=2 and was not run. The `tl.where` change is in a kernel CUDA also runs; it is standard Triton but was not run on NVIDIA.

## Overview

Enable CUDA IPC weight-cache restarts for serialized compressed-tensors 128×128 block FP8 linear weights. Part of #56049.

This is now independent, directly based on main `34d5de18cd8b`. [Review only this feature](https://github.com/liusy58/vllm/compare/34d5de18cd8baf9f5958e45720858939863a7264...d8f56f42ec4e9a8bfc020de0e6e0b786994f7edd); head `d8f56f42ec4e`. Rebuilt in response to Zifeng’s request to decouple the stacked PRs.

## Claims

- Reuse processed weights/scales across engine restarts with the validated CUTLASS backend.
- Preserve exact outputs, shared storage and required Python metadata; unsupported configurations remain rejected.
- Include only this feature and its necessary common plumbing beyond merged main.

## Validation

B300, November 4, exact source hashes verified against this head:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Layer/configuration regressions | 16 passed, 46 deselected in 17.25s |
| Real model: ordinary → fallback → IPC → second IPC | 1 passed in 118.06s |
| All changed-file pre-commit hooks | Passed, including mypy, ruff and CI test tethering |

Both IPC loads forbid fallback. Exact greedy outputs use `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`; layer tests also verify shared pointers and unchanged tensors. The real model is `RedHatAI/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8-BLOCK`, pinned to `5def00c475640c0527e3a7067b1a26b94decefb5`, with its checked-in configuration unchanged.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k 'preprocessed or test_scheme_selection' -q -rs
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_ipc_cache_compressed_block_fp8 -q -rs
pre-commit run --files $(git diff 34d5de18cd8baf9f5958e45720858939863a7264 HEAD --name-only)
```

The isolated runtime used Python 3.12, Torch 2.14/cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, process-local CUDAcompat13.4, and reused stable extensions from `5d55ef159`. Relevant CUTLASS FP8 C++ is unchanged; unrelated HiSparse binding and removed Qutlass-wrapper changes are outside these tests. This is targeted smoke/output equivalence, not a pristine full-source rebuild, full accuracy evaluation, performance benchmark, or upstream GPU CI result. No new skips, retries or weakened assertions were added. GPU occupancy guards prevented launches onto busy GPUs; other workloads were untouched.

On original base `4f9c3c8c06` plus new tests, the real model failed after successful ordinary/fallback generation: `UnsupportedQuantForIPCError: CompressedTensorsLinearMethod does not support loading from pre-processed weights` (1 failed, 103.87s). The fused block layer also rejected pre-processed weights (1 failed, 8.50s). These are historical baseline runs, not a rerun on today’s main.

</details>

## Details

Only the actual CUTLASS block-FP8 kernel with 128×128 blocks opts in. IPC retains the untransposed layout and dynamic group-128 activation state. Tensor/channel FP8 from #63673 is not included in this branch.

This includes the minimal compressed-tensors capability bridge and attention-buffer restoration shared with #63673, so it can land first. Neither PR requires the other. If both merge, retain both narrow capability cases; the shared hook may need a textual conflict resolution.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Patch the platform class, not the instance, in the humming quantization tests
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`(H200 MIG 35GB) Quantization` Shard 4/4 has failed on every main build since [102780](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102780), through nightly 102861:

```
FAILED quantization/test_modelopt.py::test_modelopt_nested_mixed_checkpoint - _pickle.PicklingError: Can't pickle <functools._lru_cache_wrapper object at 0x...>: it's not the same object as vllm.platforms.cuda.NvmlCudaPlatform.get_device_capability
FAILED quantization/test_modelopt.py::test_modelopt_mixed_dspark_checkpoint - (same)
```

`test_humming_nvfp4_linear_declares_executed_activation` (from #59460) monkeypatches `get_device_capability` on the `current_platform` *instance*. Before pytest 9.2, undoing an instance patch writes the inherited value back onto the instance. That leaves a bound `@classmethod @cache` method in `current_platform.__dict__`. A later test that sends a closure over `current_platform` through `LLM.apply_model` then fails in cloudpickle, which can't pickle that lru_cache wrapper by reference.

No code change caused this. The step was re-enabled at 102760 (#66672). Once the runtime sharder had timings, it re-split the shards and put `test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py` before `test_modelopt.py` in shard 4.

The fix patches the class (`type(current_platform)`) with a `classmethod` for both patches in that file. Undoing it then restores the original attribute cleanly on any pytest version. This is a test-only change.

## Relation to #67673

#67673 fixes the same leak globally by raising the pin to pytest>=9.2.0 and regenerating 8 requirement locks. This PR is the narrow, test-only fix for the file that leaks. It can land first to turn the step green, and it stays correct after #67673. Either can land without the other.

## Test Plan

- A minimal pytest 9.1.0 + cloudpickle repro: patching the instance reproduces the exact `PicklingError`, and patching the class doesn't.
- CI: `quantization` (H200 MIG 35GB, all shards), as a selected-steps build on this PR.
- `pre-commit run --files tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py`

## Test Result

- Repro behaves as expected, and pre-commit passes.
- GPU: [build 102870](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102870), `quantization` (H200 MIG 35GB): all 4 shards passed. In Shard 4/4 `test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py` ran before `test_modelopt.py`, the order that fails on main, and both modelopt tests passed.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; I reviewed the change.
